### Breaking Changes

- coding-agent: persist sessions in version-3 directories containing meta.json, messages.jsonl and index.json. Explicitly opening a valid legacy session migrates it and retains its original JSONL backup; listing alone does not migrate. Older Loop versions cannot read new history. Session file accessors now identify meta.json; use SessionManager for reads and the collection accessor for session creation. See [session storage](packages/coding-agent/src/docs/session-format.md).

### Added

- Web UI: support persistent chats without a project, using independent working directories and the existing history, pin, read and archive lifecycle. Replace the standalone welcome page with the shared chat workspace and keep the composer mounted through the first message. Add a Chats sidebar section; Chats, Pinned and Projects initially show five entries and reveal ten more per Show more action. Project selection remains available only before the first message.

- Web UI: add a fixed New task button above the scrolling sidebar history, opening a new draft in the selected session's workspace, or an independent chat when no accessible project is selected. Align its icon with the Pinned heading, including with classic scrollbars.

- Web UI: keep the Pinned heading at the top while sidebar sessions scroll, then stack Projects beneath it when reached; reverse naturally when scrolling up and use the top position for Projects when no pins remain. Clip session rows passing behind the headings while preserving the original sidebar background without solid-color blocks. Click Pinned or Projects to scroll to its first row below the sticky headings; Projects expands if needed, with folding retained on its separate chevron.

- Voice build: automatically build, verify and publish engine/model packages, manifests and checksums to GitHub Releases when pinned voice inputs or build configuration change on main, or on voice-vX.Y.Z tags. Use explicit semantic resource versions for main pushes, keep manual runs build-only and replace same-name assets on existing releases with the latest verified build, uploading the manifest last and serializing voice workflows.

- coding-agent and Web UI: add optional local streaming speech input and continuous voice calls, with editable dictation, automatic submission, interruptible spoken progress, queued follow-ups, atomic safe-boundary steering and explicit task cancellation. Preserve typed drafts, existing approvals and session history; hangup does not cancel accepted work. Add authenticated, bounded WebSocket audio for local, paired remote and development access, with single-use tickets, device-revocation cleanup and foreground recovery. Unify Voice settings field columns, compact control dimensions, typography and step spacing. Label the Voice steps Select features, Install components and Test; add a Features field label and align the compact, fixed-width feature dropdown and microphone test controls with their respective titles. Show Voice profile names and descriptions together inside the dropdown options and omit descriptive captions from the microphone test step. Match the microphone and Test audio label typography; share the feature/device dropdown component with menus matching the trigger width, including option spacing, hover states, selection marks and keyboard navigation. Place speech-preview and microphone sampling controls on separate labeled rows; show a compact capsule with reduced vertical padding, denser, smaller waveform dots, continuous volume-sensitive waveform movement with background-noise suppression and a higher saturation threshold, preserving peak height while distinguishing ordinary and louder speech and smaller grey circular backgrounds with unchanged icon and hit-area sizes for discard and stop controls, showing the microphone-test capsule only after preparation completes and listening begins, while the disabled microphone shows a smaller spinner ring during preparation without changing the icon size or position, replace the sampling capsule with persistent final text and a Retry action in the same row on stop, keep the leftmost X during recording to cancel and hide the sample, and show Retry only after recording completes to clear the previous result and record again on the same prepared microphone and engine connection and keep the microphone row height stable across preparation, recording and results with scrollable long text, automatically finalize each microphone test after 30 seconds of listening with a countdown outside the capsule on its right, reserving its width before recording and showing 30S only after recording starts, restart sampling from the microphone and discard cancelled samples without verification or visible status captions with accessible labels and hover titles. Provide a three-step Voice settings flow for component installation and microphone testing; enable voice entry once the required components are ready, keep Step 3 testing optional and direct disabled-button hovers to Settings component details. Retain browser-local test completion for the selected profile, microphone and resource versions, requiring a new test after changes. Show compact chat dictation sampling controls beside an audio-reactive orb in place of Send, preserving other composer tools, preserving the editable draft above, with red Discard and Stop icons in Light mode, softer coral-red icons in Dark mode, a denser waveform with smaller dots, real waveform feedback and a reserved 60-second countdown; buffer dictation until completion, then populate the editable draft, while cancellation preserves existing content. Place icon-only Voice input and Call actions immediately to the left of Send, with symmetric spacing; keep Voice input visible with typed or transcribed drafts so recording can restart after Stop. Keep Call black in Light mode. Replace the bottom toolbar during calls with live microphone waves and a rightmost End call icon, without a Discard action; play a quiet locally synthesized melody during initial connection and reduced-motion-aware wave animation during connection and reconnection, stopping the melody on readiness, cancellation or failure. Manage verified resources on the backend computer with resumable downloads, repair, updates and uninstall; retain license notices and prepare macOS ARM64 assets through a manual build workflow. Discover published resources through a bounded, versioned Release manifest with protocol, pinned-model, URL and integrity validation; preserve installed resources on discovery failure without copying generated catalogs into Loop. Audio is processed locally without saving recordings; submitted text still reaches the configured Agent.

- Web UI: add a folder-icon Reveal action to the local session context menu, opening the saved session’s storage folder in the host file manager.

- coding-agent: add indexed three-round history reads, append message bytes on ordinary saves, commit metadata separately, recover uncommitted tails and rebuild missing or stale indexes. Use writable positioned file handles for append and truncation on Windows. Preserve full-history model execution. Archive and restore retain all three storage files and legacy backups; deletion removes complete session directories, migration backups and traces together, restoring staged files if the archive update fails.

- Web UI: load only the latest three conversation rounds in HTTP and event snapshots, fetching three earlier rounds per upward scroll with viewport preservation, retry and stream-change protection. Show a localized spinner and pause scrolling while fetching earlier messages; restore the visible message position before resuming, and preserve assistant component identity and tool expansion across prepends. Prioritize history requests, pause thumbnail sources during paging, decode images asynchronously and reserve media space to reduce loading contention and layout shifts. Keep live messages, timing and read receipts aligned with absolute history indexes; switching sessions resets the loaded window.

- Web UI: preserve inline local-file links within their sentences as downloads, and turn standalone assistant Markdown links to local files into download cards, with native audio/video controls and PDF previews in a new browser tab. Serve session-referenced project and temporary files up to 512 MiB with device authentication, streaming and byte-range seeking; force other file types to download. Playback and PDF display depend on browser support.

- Web UI: add installable production PWA metadata and icons, home-screen guidance, optional browser installation, explicit update/reload prompts and a themed offline page. Cache only validated static build assets; keep navigation, chat APIs, authentication and SSE online. Leave document navigation on private Dev Tunnels addresses to the browser so refreshes and Microsoft sign-in redirects retain the native navigation context; generic offline navigation remains available on other origins. Improve mobile safe areas, touch controls, scrollable approvals, wrapping composer controls and drawer focus isolation. Touch-keyboard Enter inserts a newline, with Send or Ctrl/Command+Enter to submit; switching chats no longer opens the touch keyboard automatically. See [mobile layout and PWA](packages/web-ui/src/frontend/docs/pwa.md).

- Web UI: add experimental Dev Tunnels controls in Settings with verified official CLI installation, resumable downloads, managed uninstall, Microsoft sign-in/sign-out and private tunnel connection/disconnection. Show compact four-step setup and device pairing, completion/failure markers and localized inline progress for installation, uninstall, sign-in, sign-out, connection and shutdown; hide the service address and redundant status captions. Preserve partial downloads on Pause, validate resumed ranges and verify the pinned executable before installation. Uninstall removes only the managed executable and preserves CLI credentials. Sign out finishes tunnel shutdown before account logout. Persist sign-in and reconnect booleans, restore the persistent tunnel after backend restart when enabled, and avoid credential-store probes when opening Settings. Explicit account or host operations may require system credential approval; errors remain in the responsible step with manual retry. Keep control commands same-origin and cookie-protected. Automatically show a one-use QR invitation in Step 4 after Step 3 connects, renew it automatically on expiry while connected with no pending pairing request, and provide a single-arrow refresh icon beside Paired devices for manual replacement or retry without changing the tunnel URL. Generate a fresh code after reconnect. Place brief phone-scanning guidance beside Paired devices and show the QR image beside the paired-device list, without a pairing link; cap the list at the QR image height with vertical scrolling for additional devices. Keep Step 4 green while a valid device remains paired, show each device’s authorization expiry, and mark expired devices with a red cross and a re-pairing prompt; expired records remain removable until the next approval prunes them. Add isolated remote ingress with one-use QR invitations, phone requests and desktop confirmation codes, Secure HttpOnly device cookies, hashed credential storage, fourteen-day expiry and device revocation. Require exact Origin and CSRF checks for remote chat commands; terminate active HTTP/SSE access on revocation or tunnel disconnect. Unpaired devices see only pairing, while desktop configuration and project administration stay local. See [setup](packages/web-ui/src/backend/docs/remote-access.md) and [device pairing](packages/web-ui/src/backend/docs/remote-devices.md).

### Fixed

- CI: pin Linux verification to Ubuntu 24.04 so runner image upgrades do not break Bubblewrap sandbox preparation before repository checks start, preserving the existing required-check name so successful runs unblock merging.

- Web UI: restore full-width waveform controls in place of composer tools during voice input and calls, adding an animated audio-reactive orb at the rightmost Send position while respecting reduced-motion preferences. Give Send and the orb the same fixed-size footprint without extra padding, use equal-sized, vertically centered idle voice and Send controls with a compact 4px gap between voice entries and an 8px gap before Send, and keep audio animation inside the orb without outward scaling; the model selector remains directly before Voice input.

- Web UI: keep connection music looping during initial voice startup through direct audio output, separate from the speech media stream; readiness and cleanup immediately silence and disconnect all tone nodes, and subsequent reconnection stays silent.

- Web UI: narrate complete voice-call replies and intermediate assistant text in ordered short segments instead of limiting replies to two sentences or dropping queued narration; retain unread updates until playback is ready. Start narration at completed streaming sentences and prefetch one synthesis segment during current playback to reduce startup and between-segment delays.

- Web UI: route local voice playback through a managed media audio element to improve browser echo-cancellation compatibility while preserving live microphone capture and interruption; release playback tracks on failure or hangup.

- Web UI: replace the lower voice-call panel with microphone, spoken-reply and correction icon controls in the composer toolbar, retaining a single red Stop control to end calls and removing the lower submission-status text row. Select correction by default on call start or resume, clearing it after the next submitted utterance.

- Voice installation: report connection failures as download errors rather than generic resource-operation failures, preserving partial files for retry.

- Voice settings: share in-flight Release discovery across concurrent status requests, retry unavailable catalog checks and retain installed engine readiness when discovery fails, preventing false unpublished-package states.

- Web UI: reduce voice-input startup by preparing microphone capture and the backend concurrently, skipping unused TTS loading and integrity reads for dictation and microphone tests while retaining synthesis for calls and speech tests; clean up prepared calls on microphone failure or cancellation.

- Web UI: replace whitespace-only composer drafts when inserting dictation so empty editor line breaks do not precede recognized text.

- Web UI: close the local voice preview connection and release microphone capture when playback finishes, mute input during preview, label the playback test Test speech, show a compact spinner around its icon while preparing audio and display the sample text with a highlight following elapsed audio playback, and keep preview loading, completion and failures independent of microphone-test state and Step 3 completion.

- Web UI: keep the microphone test Stop control available during intermediate phrase transcription; only explicit finalization disables Stop. Stopping chat or test dictation drains queued microphone frames and the final partial PCM frame before requesting recognition completion, while retaining the transcription connection until queued audio is finalized and explicitly acknowledged, then inserts the completed text instead of closing after 1.8 seconds or an earlier phrase result. Drive the microphone spinner from detected local speech energy while recording, retaining rotation through quiet speech and brief pauses with a lower continuation threshold and a 1.2-second silence hold instead of using intermediate transcription status; retain connection and finalization feedback.

- Web UI: start Settings microphone samples in session-independent test mode and finalize their last phrase on Stop, avoiding startup rejection for a missing chat session.

- Web UI: show one Voice Download icon button until all components are installed, then replace it with an Uninstall icon button; download installs speech synthesis even when the input profile is selected. Treat user-stopped installation as paused without a failure message, disable Download and provide a Resume icon to continue partial downloads from their retained percentages, reporting the on-disk offset before waiting for network data; verified installed packages retain completed markers during resume instead of flashing loading. Install independent packages concurrently, aggregate download progress, let unaffected packages finish after individual failures and wait for all workers before activation, cancellation cleanup or retry. Show four horizontal package markers with evenly spaced circles, single-line ellipsized package names underneath with full-name hover titles, detached horizontal separators, per-package percentages inside inner progress rings filling clockwise from the top with gradient strokes, subtle orbiting halos and looping comet highlights along the downloaded arc, green completion checks and a red failure cross with per-package error tooltips on hover or keyboard focus, with an info icon beside each package name showing only that package’s sizes, version and license on hover or focus, without storage paths or a trailing divider. Prioritize current package operation states and error reasons over installed-file readiness in info tooltips. Restore fixed-position tooltip styling so package details remain visible above Settings on hover. Place each Voice step title beside its step number. Place the installation action directly after its title above the evenly spaced packages, with per-package progress only and errors on a separate row.

- Voice build: use the dedicated VOICE_RELEASE_TOKEN Actions secret for publication and report missing credentials explicitly, supporting release tag creation for commits containing workflow changes.

- coding-agent: allow pinned voice model downloads through Hugging Face's AWS CDN and create nested model/license directories during clean asset preparation, while retaining exact-host redirect checks and size/SHA-256 verification.

- Web development: keep the gateway, private Tunnel and device authorization alive across backend source reloads under `pnpm dev`. Restart only the business worker, return a retrying recovery page during startup, and reject unavailable API calls without queuing or replaying commands. Automatically build the phone frontend on startup and rebuild after source or build configuration edits, debounce and serialize updates, and preserve the last successful frontend on failure. Browser disconnects and SSE termination during worker replacement avoid spurious abort/termination errors; unexpected failures and incomplete data responses still fail. Running generation is interrupted; production and direct Web startup retain their existing lifecycle.

- Web UI: bound remote startup authorization checks and chat downloads, exposing a retry action instead of waiting indefinitely. Reload the root page after a failed module download and provide an HTML fallback when startup scripts stall. Bound explicit PWA update activation with a reload fallback; on origins other than private Dev Tunnels, show the generic recovery page on navigation timeout or HTTP 503 as well as network failure. Preserve native private-tunnel navigation and authentication responses.

- Web UI: remove the browser's brief touch-tap highlight on mobile and prevent long-press text selection across navigation, session lists, menus and action controls. Use the mobile layout below 768px and on coarse-pointer touch viewports up to 1024px, keeping portrait phones and unfolded compact foldables consistent across the sidebar, composer and Settings. Use a fixed mobile viewport and 16px base, message, session title and tool text, a larger composer and header, 44px toolbar controls and keyboard-resizing viewport metadata. Hide inline session pin buttons in mobile layouts while retaining pin actions in the context menu. Retain keyboard focus indicators and selection in messages, code, file contents, error details and text inputs.

- Web UI: recover session and list streams after foreground return, network restoration and stale heartbeats, using bounded backoff and existing cursor replay/snapshots without replaying commands. Preserve loaded chats on transient authorization-check failures, show offline/retry guidance, and retain unconfirmed prompt identities after timeouts or HTTP 5xx. Delay reconnect guidance for two seconds so ordinary session switches do not flash warnings; show offline guidance immediately. Reject browser prompt submissions targeting an obsolete server stream before execution.

- Web UI: display local raster images referenced by assistant Markdown through session-scoped image responses, including project screenshots and temporary images. Show message images as horizontally scrollable thumbnails with a larger preview, previous/next controls and detail inspection. Zoom around the selected image point on click or tap. Support image-only two-finger zoom and bounded dragging on phones without zooming the page; reset the view when switching images. Require an existing message reference, validate file boundaries and image signatures, and retain device authentication for phone access.

- Web UI: preserve the private tunnel URL across reconnects and backend restarts by persisting the tunnel identity, verified origin and ingress port. Retain the cloud tunnel on disconnect, sign-out and uninstall, recover interrupted provisioning, and reject missing resources or occupied ports without silently changing addresses. Existing temporary tunnels need one new pairing at the stable address; same-browser device authorization then survives restart until expiry or revocation. Confirm fresh, stable cloud host connectivity before completing connection, check health every thirty seconds, and reconnect at the same address with bounded exponential backoff after host exit or confirmed disconnection. Keep Disconnect available during connection and recovery; stop, sign-out and shutdown cancel recovery; repeated failures remain actionable without opening account login.

- Web development: keep the API and active sessions running when Vite configuration fails. Serve the last built frontend or a retrying unavailable page, retry frontend initialization on page requests, and exclude frontend build configuration from backend restarts. Build frontend assets in staging and publish only successful builds with atomic file replacement, retaining old hashed resources for open tabs and keeping the active frontend available through Node and Vite rebuilds.

- Web UI: use root-served public icon URLs in development and production, avoiding Vite public-directory warnings while preserving theme-aware loading icons and static logo caching.

- Web UI: keep the latest messages above the composer when the phone keyboard opens or closes while the conversation is at the bottom; preserve manual history positions and fit the mobile shell to the visible viewport.

- Web UI: apply the saved or system theme and loading-screen background directly from HTML before application resources load, preventing a white flash on refresh. Show a 48px theme-aware Loop icon beside medium-weight 20px loading text from the initial placeholder through chat loading.

- Web UI: preserve SSE anti-transformation headers on remote device connections so intermediaries are instructed to forward streamed chat updates without compression or response rewriting while keeping responses uncached.

- Web UI: serve a lightweight standalone phone pairing page with the device-name form already in HTML, independent of chat downloads and authorization-check latency. Keep the pairing form hidden on ordinary refresh while checking authorization and loading chats, so paired devices return directly to chats; show a fresh QR invitation form immediately. After authorization, download the chat entry and shell in parallel and reuse the fresh in-memory authorization check. Defer Settings until opened and math/code highlighting until needed, keep ordinary messages readable during renderer downloads, and negotiate gzip for static scripts/styles. Distinguish a browser without a pairing request from an expired request, so opening a bare tunnel URL in a new browser or incognito window asks for pairing without incorrectly claiming expiry. Preserve an unsubmitted invitation in same-tab session storage for up to five minutes after capture so refresh does not lose it; clear it after submission or successful authorization, and keep server expiry and one-use checks authoritative. Retain localized pairing, comparison codes, retry guidance and ongoing access checks.

- Web UI: serve the built frontend from the workspace Web package when pnpm dev hosts remote pairing, fixing the phone page returning 404 while the local Vite page works.

- Web UI: preserve the original Host and Origin when starting Dev Tunnels so phone scans and pairing requests pass the isolated ingress checks instead of returning invalid_host or invalid_origin. Allow cross-site top-level navigation to the public pairing page after browser handoffs or sign-in redirects, retaining strict checks for APIs, frames, writes and foreign origins.

- Web UI: remove the browser focus outline appearing between Model and Effort menu rows while retaining the theme-aware keyboard focus background.

- Web UI: align all Settings section titles to a shared position and heading height so switching sections no longer shifts the title.

pages.markdown:
# Loop Loop is a local-first, open-source coding harness built with TypeScript. Use it in your browser or terminal, or integrate it through the TypeScript SDK, to read and edit files and run commands in your projects. Connect your preferred model provider to get started.

## What can Loop do? Loop can: - work in your browser or terminal, or inside your application through the TypeScript SDK - read and edit project files, run shell commands, and execute your tests - connect to built-in model providers, custom gateways, and compatible local model endpoints - save conversations by project and restore previous sessions to continue your work - load reusable Skills and use external MCP tools in the Web UI or through the SDK - compact long conversations automatically or on demand while preserving the original history - control tool access with permission presets and approve operations that need additional access ## Why Loop - **Local-first:** work directly in your projects, with conversations and settings stored on your machine. - **Three ways to work:** use the Web UI, CLI, or TypeScript SDK with the same session and tool APIs. - **Model choice:** choose your provider and model, including compatible gateways and local endpoints. - **Controlled execution:** set read-only, workspace-write, or full-access permissions and review approval requests. - **A focused core:** a single-agent loop with inspectable TypeScript code, reusable Skills, and MCP integrations. ## Start With Node.js 24+ installed, start the published Web UI: ```bash npx @loop-harness/loop web ``` The browser opens when the local service is ready. Configure providers in Settings → Models. The published package includes the CLI, SDK and prebuilt Web UI; no Bun or frontend build tools are required. Optional local speech input and calls are configured in Settings → Voice. Resources are installed explicitly on the backend computer; see [voice setup and limits](packages/web-ui/src/frontend/docs/voice.md). ## Local development Requires Node.js 24+ and pnpm 11. Install dependencies and start the Web UI: ```bash pnpm install pnpm dev ``` The browser opens when the loopback service is ready. Configure providers in Settings → Models. Development serves React through Vite middleware on the same port as the API; frontend changes use HMR. A stable development gateway keeps the private tunnel and device authorization alive while backend source edits restart only the business worker. For the CLI, configure LOOP_AI_PROVIDER, LOOP_MODEL and LOOP_AI_API_KEY in the environment or a local .env, then run pnpm coding-agent. See [models](packages/coding-agent/src/docs/models.md) for compatible gateways and configuration. Build and launch the production application: ```bash pnpm build node dist/bin.js web node dist/bin.js web --port 3081 --no-open node dist/bin.js --help ``` The public npm package is `@loop-harness/loop`; the installed executable remains `loop`. See [distribution](docs/development.md#distribution) for packaging and publication. ## Architecture | Package | Responsibility | | --- | --- | | packages/agent | In-memory model and sequential tool loop | | packages/coding-agent | Sessions, permissions, tools, persistence, CLI and SDK | | packages/web-ui | Frontend, backend and shared protocol | | packages/telemetry | Local trace recording, storage and retention | All four are private workspace packages with independent manifests and public exports, bundled into the root distribution. Root bin.ts and sdk.ts are application distribution entries. Commands flow Web/CLI/SDK → coding-agent → agent → model API. Events flow upward through subscriptions. Only the model-runtime module configures and injects the model runtime; the loop initiates requests. pnpm check:architecture enforces dependencies and rejects cycles and private imports. Loop remains single-agent. Reliability, safety, recoverability and usability determine maturity. ## Documentation The manually maintained [marketing website](website/README.md) lives in `website/`, with its own development and static build commands. It is independent of Loop application code and excluded from the application build and published package. | Area | Entry | | --- | --- | | Agent API, events and tools | [Agent](packages/agent/README.md) | | SDK, CLI, models and sessions | [Coding-agent](packages/coding-agent/README.md) | | Local execution logs | [Telemetry](packages/telemetry/README.md) | | Browser application and server | [Web UI](packages/web-ui/README.md) | | Development, build and distribution | [Development](docs/development.md) | ## Validation Run pnpm typecheck, pnpm check, pnpm build and pnpm test. Use affected tests by default; the build is required for distribution startup tests. Model tests use synthetic local responses. The CLI PTY test requires Python 3. Confined shell tests require macOS Seatbelt or Linux Bubblewrap. See [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md), [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md), [Security](SECURITY.md) and [License](LICENSE). The software is MIT-licensed. The Loop icon remains reserved under the [brand asset policy](packages/web-ui/src/docs/assets/loop-brand/BRAND-ASSETS.md); guide fonts retain their [SIL OFL 1.1 license](packages/web-ui/src/docs/assets/loop-brand/fonts/OFL.txt).

# Loop Web Frontend

A React interface for local chat. It sends commands over HTTP and receives session state over SSE. The frontend does not call models, execute tools, or read the filesystem directly; the Web backend provides these capabilities through the public coding-agent SDK.

## Start

From the project root:

```bash
pnpm dev
```

Configure a service in **Settings → Models**, then add a project and create a session. Existing sessions keep their selected model; change it in the composer's model settings menu. React and CSS support hot updates; backend source changes require a restart. See the [Web README](../../README.md) for installation.

## Features

| Feature | Documentation |
| --- | --- |
| Create projects, select source folders, and navigate sessions | [Projects and sessions](docs/projects.md) |
| Compose, send, cancel, and retry after failure | [Chat input](docs/chat.md) |
| Local dictation, foreground voice calls and speech settings | [Voice input and calls](docs/voice.md) |
| Markdown, Mermaid, thinking, tool results, and copying | [Message rendering](docs/messages.md) |
| Custom providers and the current session's model | [Model settings](docs/models.md) |
| Configure, enable and discover MCP servers | [Integration settings](docs/integrations.md) |
| SSE subscriptions, snapshots, and reconnection | [Streaming state](docs/events.md) |
| Per-session permissions and allow-once/reject controls | [Permissions and approvals](docs/permissions.md) |
| Layout, language, appearance, and browser storage | [Interface preferences](docs/preferences.md) |
| Microsoft sign-in, tunnel controls and device pairing | [Remote connection settings](docs/remote-access.md) |
| Mobile controls, installation, updates and offline page | [Mobile layout and PWA](docs/pwa.md) |

Each page covers one feature: usage, contracts, lifecycle, limits, and links to source and colocated tests. Components use arrow functions with matching CSS and test files. Hooks and utilities are split by responsibility.

## Validation

Run the matching tests for changed components, hooks, or utilities. For documentation-only edits, check links and content without running the full application suite. To check the entire frontend, run from the project root:

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run packages/web-ui/src/frontend
```

The [Web workspace](../../package.json) owns dependencies and development scripts; the frontend has no separate package.json. See the [backend documentation](../backend/README.md) for service contracts.

# Loop coding-agent

A CLI and TypeScript SDK built on the existing [Loop Agent](../agent/README.md). Coding-agent owns model configuration, built-in tools, resources, and persistent sessions. Every prompt creates a fresh Agent with completed history.

Import from [index.ts](src/index.ts). This private pnpm workspace package owns its dependencies and public SDK/CLI exports. The root `@loop-harness/loop` distribution bundles it.

## Start

Manual context compaction is available through interactive `/compact`, Web composer `/` → **Compact**, or SDK `session.compact()`. Originals remain saved while the next request uses a summary and recent turns. See [compaction](src/docs/compaction.md) for cancellation and recovery.

From the project root, install with `pnpm install` and configure [a model](src/docs/models.md). Then choose a consumer:

```bash
pnpm run coding-agent
pnpm run coding-agent --print "Read package.json and explain the scripts."
node --conditions=loop-source --import tsx packages/coding-agent/src/sdk.sample.ts "Hello, what time is it now?"
```

The CLI is interactive by default. The SDK sample performs one request workflow and exits; it keeps history in memory. Both default to OpenAI GPT-5.5 and support a custom URL through model configuration.

## Features

| Feature | Documentation |
| --- | --- |
| Embed Loop and call the public API | [SDK](src/docs/sdk.md) |
| Interactive commands and Print mode | [CLI](src/docs/cli.md) |
| Model selection, credentials, custom URLs | [Models](src/docs/models.md) |
| Configuration files and environment | [Settings](src/docs/settings.md) |
| Queue, reorder, steer, stop and resume inputs | [Message queue](src/docs/message-queue.md) |
| Create, restore, replace, and save sessions | [Sessions](src/docs/sessions.md) |
| Preserve and restore archive membership | [Session archive](src/docs/session-archive.md) |
| Automatic titles, renaming and regeneration | [Session titles](src/docs/session-titles.md) |
| On-disk JSONL schema | [Session format](src/docs/session-format.md) |
| Stream output and observe run completion | [Events](src/docs/events.md) |
| Record execution events to local logs | [Telemetry](src/docs/telemetry.md) |
| Inspect trace event names and business mappings | [Trace events](src/docs/trace-events.md) |
| Read, bash, edit, and write | [Tools](src/docs/tools.md) |
| Configure MCP servers and discover external tools in the background | [MCP servers](src/docs/mcp.md) |
| Discover and call tools through isolated JavaScript | [Codemode](src/docs/codemode.md) |
| Install, discover, select and load task workflows | [Skills](src/docs/skills.md) |
| Session permission presets and native file sandboxing | [Permissions](src/docs/permissions.md) |
| Request, answer and cancel host approvals | [Approvals](src/docs/approvals.md) |
| Run local speech recognition and synthesis | [Voice runtime](src/docs/voice.md) |
| Discover project instructions | [Context files](src/docs/context-files.md) |
| Track system permissions and expand selected Skill instructions | [Runtime context](src/docs/runtime-context.md) |
| Trace model messages to complete history and runtime snapshots | [Model input projection](src/docs/model-input-projection.md) |
| Check complete model input and reserve response capacity | [Context budget](src/docs/context-budget.md) |
| Summarize older model input while preserving original history | [Compaction](src/docs/compaction.md) |

Each page covers one feature, with usage first, API or configuration reference, current behavior and limits, and links to source/tests. The README is the entry point, keeping feature details in `docs/`.

## Samples and validation

- [cli.sample.sh](src/cli.sample.sh): executable CLI usage, custom endpoint flags, and session restore.
- [sdk.sample.ts](src/sdk.sample.ts): model setup, session creation, text subscriptions, prompting, cancellation, and cleanup through public SDK exports.

Samples use real configured models and can execute enabled tools. Tests use local synthetic endpoints and temporary directories; the interactive PTY test requires Python 3.

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run packages/coding-agent/src
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run check
```

Coding-agent supports Loop's sequential Agent, editable input queue, steering, cancellation, local voice runtime and JSONL history, including manual and automatic [context compaction](src/docs/compaction.md).

pages.title: Loop Agent
pages.markdown:
# Loop Agent

An in-memory conversation loop for Loop. The host supplies a model and stream function; Agent manages completed messages, sequential tools, subscriptions, and cancellation.

Import from [index.ts](src/index.ts). This private workspace package declares its own dependencies and public exports. It is bundled into the root `@loop-harness/loop` distribution.

## Start

See [Agent API](src/docs/agent.md) for a minimal call and [agent.sample.ts](src/agent.sample.ts) for a custom-endpoint example. Replace its example gateway URL, model ID, and capabilities, and set `AGENT_EXAMPLE_API_KEY` as needed before running it. The sample makes real model requests when configured and executed.

## Features

| Feature | Documentation |
| --- | --- |
| Create an Agent, prompt, and reuse history | [Agent API](src/docs/agent.md) |
| Model requests, tool turns and scheduled input boundaries | [Agent loop](src/docs/agent-loop.md) |
| Streaming messages and subscriptions | [Events](src/docs/events.md) |
| Declare, validate, and execute tools | [Tools](src/docs/tools.md) |
| Abort, failure, truncation, and turn limits | [Cancellation and errors](src/docs/cancellation.md) |

Session storage, built-in coding tools, and model configuration belong to [coding-agent](../coding-agent/README.md). Agent has no default stream registration, persistence, queue storage, compaction, or provider implementation.

## Validation

From the project root:

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run packages/agent/src
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run check
```

These documents describe Loop's implemented API and its limits.

pages.title: Development and distribution
pages.markdown:
# Development and distribution

## Setup

Loop requires Node.js 24+ and pnpm 11. Install workspace dependencies from the repository root:

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

The browser opens when the local service is ready. Configure a provider in Settings → Models before creating a conversation. Development uses Vite middleware for frontend HMR on the same loopback port as the API. A separate `tsx watch` process restarts the Node backend when its loaded source files change; frontend source is excluded from backend watching. The backend runs without Node's `--watch`, keeping its Worker channels free of Node dependency-tracking messages.

For the terminal, configure the environment described in [models](../packages/coding-agent/src/docs/models.md), then run pnpm coding-agent. The application entry loads the working directory's .env; inherited environment variables take precedence. SDK imports do not load environment files.

Vite initialization errors leave the API and sessions running. Development falls back to the last Web build, or shows a retrying unavailable page if no build exists; page requests retry initialization after the configuration is fixed. Frontend source and package-level TypeScript build configuration are excluded from backend restarts. See [server recovery](../packages/web-ui/src/backend/docs/server.md#readiness-and-development-updates) for the retry and restart limits. Restart `pnpm dev` after updating its watcher command.

## Build and launch

```bash
pnpm build
node dist/bin.js web
node dist/bin.js web --port 3081 --no-open
node dist/bin.js --help
```

Production serves prebuilt Web assets from the installed package, independently of the working directory. Vite and Bun are not runtime requirements. The server binds to loopback only; browser opening is suppressed over SSH and with --no-open.

## Packages

Three private packages own Agent, coding-agent and Web. The public root distribution is named `@loop-harness/loop`. Installed SDK consumers import `@loop-harness/loop`; workspace consumers import @loop/agent or @loop/coding-agent. Public exports resolve to build output; development uses the loop-source export condition.

Web and terminal/SDK entries consume coding-agent; coding-agent consumes agent; agent calls the model API through its injected stream function. The model-runtime module configures the model runtime and injects its stream function; the agent loop initiates requests. Browser/shared modules may consume coding-agent types but cannot import its runtime. SDK imports do not load terminal or Web implementations.

## Validation

Run pnpm typecheck, pnpm check and pnpm build. Run affected tests with pnpm exec vitest run followed by their file paths. Build before tests that launch the compiled application. Model tests use synthetic local responses. Confined shell tests require macOS Seatbelt or Linux Bubblewrap.

Linux CI installs Bubblewrap and, when Ubuntu restricts unprivileged user namespaces, loads an AppArmor profile permitting them specifically for /usr/bin/bwrap on the disposable runner. A sandbox startup probe must pass before running the suite. Network isolation and capability dropping remain enabled; sandbox failures are not skipped or retried without confinement. PTY tests accept Linux EIO as terminal EOF while still requiring the CLI to exit successfully.

Windows CI runs type, formatting and architecture checks, builds and packs the distribution, and verifies an isolated installation's CLI, SDK and Web assets/API. Its test selection covers Agent, Web frontend/shared behavior, static-asset confinement, CLI argument parsing, SDK setup, file tools, release validation, distribution contents and rejection of unavailable sandboxes. The complete application suite, POSIX PTY and real confined-shell integration tests run on Linux and macOS. Windows has no confined-shell backend; restricted Bash commands fail closed. This CI coverage does not claim full Windows terminal or shell support.

Package verification exercises graceful Web shutdown via SIGTERM on Unix and a verifier-only IPC hook invoking the same handler on Windows, where Node's kill() forcibly terminates children. Source checkout uses LF line endings across runners. A failure on one operating system does not cancel the other matrix jobs.

The active main-branch ruleset requires a pull request and the GitHub Actions checks `verify (ubuntu-latest)`, `verify (macos-latest)` and `verify (windows-latest)` before merging. The PR must be up to date with main; failed, pending or missing required checks block merging. No bypass actors are configured. These requirements live in GitHub repository settings, not workflow YAML; preserve or update the required names when renaming jobs.

## Distribution

The root tarball contains minified CLI/SDK JavaScript, minified Web assets, public SDK type declarations and license notices. Production builds disable JavaScript, CSS and declaration source maps, remove ordinary code comments and strip generated source-location comments from declarations. SDK types remain readable because they describe the public API, not its implementation. Development retains source access and HMR.

Every root build runs pnpm check:distribution. It rejects source files, tests, unexpected assets, separate or inline source maps and generated source-location comments, including files accidentally copied into dist. Packing runs this build through prepack. Do not bypass lifecycle scripts for releases; the command below skips them only after a verified build.

These measures exclude original TypeScript/TSX and reconstruction metadata, but do not make distributed code confidential or prevent reverse engineering. Anyone running the package can inspect or reformat its JavaScript and observe its behavior; minification also reduces stack-trace readability. Native binaries and obfuscation cannot guarantee otherwise. Code that must remain confidential must run on a controlled remote service and must not be distributed to clients. Loop currently runs locally.

Verify a local package after building:

```bash
pnpm --config.ignore-scripts=true pack
pnpm verify:package loop-harness-loop-0.1.2.tgz
```

Verification checks the actual tarball's file list and installed Loop payload, installs production dependencies, rejects module resolution outside the installation, and checks SDK imports, CLI help, Web assets/API and shutdown. Third-party production dependencies keep their own published contents and license notices; Loop's content checks cover its own distribution.

Publish the verified tarball from an npm account with publishing rights in the `loop-harness` organization. The root manifest sets public access and the npm registry; packaging and local verification do not publish a release. Complete npm authentication and any required two-factor verification locally.

```bash
npm whoami --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/
npm publish ./loop-harness-loop-0.1.2.tgz --access public --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/
npx @loop-harness/loop@0.1.2 web
```

The executable remains `loop`; internal `@loop/*` packages stay private and are bundled into this single public package. The [Check workflow](../.github/workflows/check.yml) builds, packs and verifies on Linux, macOS and Windows, with the platform-specific test coverage described above. Creating or reopening a pull request, or pushing new commits to its branch, runs one matrix. There is no separate branch-push trigger: merging into or directly pushing to `main` does not start another check, and branches without a PR are not checked automatically. Release tags invoke the same checks through the Release workflow. It uses a version-independent `loop.tgz` filename so version bumps do not require editing CI. PR checks do not publish.

## Automated releases

The [Release workflow](../.github/workflows/release.yml) runs on pushes of `v*` tags. It accepts only stable `vX.Y.Z` tags matching the root package version, on commits already merged into `main`. Prerelease tags are rejected and cannot update npm's `latest` channel.

Before the first automated release, configure a Trusted Publisher in the npm package settings. Select GitHub Actions, enter this repository's owner and name, and set the workflow filename to `release.yml` (without a directory). Allow direct publishing with `npm publish` if npm displays an allowed-actions setting. Leave the environment field empty; this workflow does not use a GitHub deployment environment. The package's `repository.url` must match the GitHub repository exactly, including case. See [npm Trusted Publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/).

Publishing uses Node.js 24, npm 11.5.1 or newer and short-lived OIDC credentials. Only the publish job receives `id-token: write`; no npm token secret is needed. This repository is public, and the published package includes npm provenance. Configuring the workflow file does not configure npm's trust relationship.

For each release:

1. Update the root package version. Internal workspace packages remain private.
2. Move pending changelog entries into a new `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD` release section immediately below Unreleased, with release notes and a valid date no later than the current UTC date. Keep exactly one empty `## [Unreleased]` section at the top, followed by releases in reverse chronological order. Release validation rejects missing, duplicate or misplaced Unreleased sections and pending entries.
3. Merge those changes, then create and push the matching tag on that commit. For example, after preparing version `0.1.2`:

```bash
git tag -a v0.1.2 -m "Release v0.1.2"
git push origin v0.1.2
```

The workflow rejects existing npm versions and stops if registry availability cannot be confirmed. It runs the shared Check workflow on all three operating systems, then publishes the exact tarball verified on Linux after all matrix jobs pass. The publish job downloads that run's artifact and does not rebuild or execute package lifecycle scripts. Release runs are serialized. The workflow publishes to npm's `latest` channel; it does not create a GitHub Release.

If validation, tests or authentication fail, publishing stops. Configure npm trust before retrying an authentication failure. Before retrying an uncertain publish, check npm for that version: published versions cannot be overwritten. Do not move an existing release tag; prepare a new version for changed code. The already published `0.1.0` is not a test release for this workflow.

pages.title: Chat Input
pages.markdown:
# Chat Input

The composer submits a user message and the backend runs the model and tool loop. The frontend displays activity and provides cancellation and save recovery; it does not execute Agent in the browser.

## Usage

New empty sessions center the input in the conversation area, with the theme-aware Loop icon and **Loop everything** stacked above it. The input returns to the bottom when the conversation starts. Draft text, attachments, model controls and recovery notices remain available in both layouts; short viewports can scroll the welcome area.

New empty sessions show a project capsule in a rounded gray strip attached to the top of the composer. The strip sits 12px inside the input's sides and extends behind its rounded top edge, with a theme-aware background distinct from the conversation. The capsule and project choices use a rounded folder outline with a horizontal divider. Hover or focus gives the capsule a neutral gray background and replaces its folder with a 20px gray circle containing a centered white cross, keeping the project label in place. Clear the capsule to choose a different registered project or add a folder with Create project. Sending requires a selected, accessible project. Switching folders retains unsent input, attachments, model, effort and permissions; saved conversations keep their original project. See [Projects and sessions](projects.md).

The empty input shows **Loop anything...**. Press Enter to send and Shift+Enter for a newline; these shortcuts are not displayed beneath the input. On devices with a coarse primary pointer, Enter inserts a newline; tap Send or use Ctrl/Command+Enter to submit. Enter does not submit during input-method composition. Pasted text is inserted as plain text; pasted files become attachments. During generation, **Stop generating** remains available beside Send when a new draft is ready. The adjacent model pill configures the current model and its supported reasoning effort; see [model settings](models.md). The session header no longer contains a model selector. Its compact layout uses a 48px minimum height and 5px top/bottom padding on desktop and mobile, preserving the folder button and inline title editor.

The input text, caret and attachment previews share a left edge aligned with the **+** button's circular hover background on desktop and mobile. The **+** button's left inset and the Send/Stop button's right inset both use 12px, keeping the circles symmetrically spaced from the composer border.

On devices with a fine primary pointer, creating a new session or switching sessions focuses the input, with the caret at the end of any restored draft. Sending with Enter or the Send button returns focus to the input without scrolling the page on these devices. Touch devices do not automatically open the keyboard on session changes. The input remains editable while sending or generating. Routine response updates do not take focus from other controls. On narrow screens, the app shell fits the visual viewport as the phone keyboard opens, closes or pans the page. Messages that were at the bottom stay above the composer; manually scrolled history keeps its reading position. Pinch zoom does not resize the shell through this keyboard adjustment, and browsers without Visual Viewport support retain the CSS dynamic-viewport layout.

Sending requires a connected session with no pending save and text or at least one image or text file; submissions during generation or a pause enter the queue. New messages are blocked during attachment reads, model or permission changes, save operations, send confirmation, or disconnection. Queued items appear above the composer in execution order. The [permission menu](permissions.md) sits beside the attachment button in the toolbar below the text input; approval cards stay above the composer.

Composer and session error notices, including run cancellation, have an **×** button at the top right. Closing a notice hides that occurrence without changing the draft, attachments, validation rules or recorded session outcome. Reconnection and pending-save recovery remain available. A new error is displayed again, including a repeated failed upload; dismissal does not carry over to another session.

When a remembered conversation returns session_not_found (404), clear only its active selection and open a new independent chat. Unsent drafts and attachments are retained. Other request failures keep the selection for Retry; generic API failures display the backend error detail instead of replacing it with an uninformative label.

## Requests and Drafts

The Compact command shows the estimated context/window percentage and a matching ring. Reopening a nonempty chat or completing compaction locally recomputes this estimate, including the summary and retained messages; no extra model request is made. A disabled Compact item still shows the percentage. The backend reports planner-backed availability; short contexts are disabled before the first click and show a concise reason on hover. Escape or an outside click dismisses the command menu for the current input; editing the text or clearing and retyping `/` opens it again.

Type `/` and choose **Compact**, or submit `/compact`, to summarize older context while preserving complete conversation history. The host selects complete recent turns using projected message estimates, including selected Skill instructions. If all uncompressed turns fit the retention budget, show **Nothing to compact** without calling the model or saving a checkpoint. The notice follows the interface language, appears only once and closes after five seconds or through its Close button. It retains the draft and attachments. After a no-work response, disable another attempt until the conversation history, checkpoint or selected model changes. Delayed compaction state updates do not clear the notice. Starting another operation clears the local notice; it is not retained as a session error. See [context compaction](../../../../coding-agent/src/docs/compaction.md).

Compaction appears at the end of the conversation with a compact outline icon and **Working for** elapsed time above a thin divider. After 15 seconds, add **This can take a few minutes**; elapsed time comes from the server’s operation start and survives refresh or reconnection to the live server. The composer keeps its ordinary background, temporarily hides slash-command text and offers **Stop generating**. Failure or cancellation restores the command draft and preserves attachments and Skills. Success leaves **Context compacted** at the checkpoint’s original history position; the latest saved checkpoint restores this marker when reopening. The marker is interface metadata, not a new conversation message, and is withheld while a save remains pending. Starting compaction reveals the status once; later updates preserve manual scrolling.

| State | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Before submission | usePrompt creates a requestId and records text, images, text files and streamId |
| Sending | Keep the input editable; block another submission until delivery is confirmed |
| HTTP acceptance | Release unchanged submitted text, attachments and Skills; allow a new submission. A 202 is not a successful answer |
| Generating | Keep the next draft editable; further sends enter the queue. With existing queued items and draft text or attachments, show only Send; restore Stop when the draft is empty |
| Successful completion | Preserve the new draft; start the next queued input |
| Failure or cancellation | Preserve the new draft and unconsumed queue; Stop exposes Resume |
| Lost response | Retain the unconfirmed request and block sending it again with a new ID |

Sending and HTTP acceptance are tracked across session switches within the current page. Only the request payload is persisted: after a reload, an unmatched saved request requires confirmation again. A changed server event stream also makes an unmatched accepted request uncertain. The delivery warning appears for unresolved requests, not for ordinary HTTP or SSE latency.

**Check and retry same request** first fetches the backend snapshot. If the original requestId was accepted, it does not execute again. Otherwise, it resends the original ID only within the same event stream. A changed streamId after a restart reports delivery_unknown and requires inspecting history first. See [backend session commands](../../backend/docs/sessions.md) for deduplication limits.

Prompt delivery and read-only API checks time out after 30 seconds, including response-body reads. A timeout or HTTP 5xx preserves the original request identity for confirmation; no automatic resend occurs. Slow administrative commands retain their existing lifecycle rather than using this prompt timeout. Browser prompts carry the observed streamId so the server also rejects a restart between status confirmation and submission.

## Cancellation, Waiting, and Save Failures

**Stop generating** calls the abort endpoint and waits for cleanup. It retains the queue and pauses draining. Keep the text already streamed in history with a muted “You stopped after” duration and divider above that attempt (localized in Chinese). Each Resume appends another response segment with its own duration; prior stopped text and labels remain visible through reconnect and reopening. Partial text is retained for display as aborted history and is excluded from model replay, so the resumed model may regenerate earlier wording. Once the server reports a resumable task, the composer replaces its Send arrow with a black circular **Resume** button containing a white right-pointing triangle. Resume works with an empty input and continues the stopped task from completed history without submitting or clearing the current draft. The queue shows its retained items and pause status without a separate Resume button. Disconnects, pending saves and active composer operations disable Resume; failures keep it available for retry. Switching sessions or disconnecting the event stream does not cancel the model request.

While a connected session is generating a response, **Looping...** appears after the latest content in the conversation with a highlight sweeping from left to right. It remains visible while waiting for the model, streaming text or thinking, and executing tools, then disappears when the prompt ends or the connection is lost. Reduced-motion and forced-color preferences use a static label. Routine session labels such as Ready, Running and Completed no longer appear above the input. Reconnection, errors and save recovery remain visible when needed. Provider configuration and the current session's model are separate choices; see [model settings](models.md) for troubleshooting.

When hasPendingSave is true, the status area offers **Retry save**. flush saves existing results without requesting the model or executing tools again. Sending and model changes remain blocked until saving succeeds.

## Attachments

Use the **+** button at the lower left of the composer to open the **Add** menu, then choose **Files** (the paperclip item). The picker allows selecting images and UTF-8 text/code files together. The menu supports keyboard navigation, Escape and outside-click dismissal. Images and text/code files can also be pasted into the input together. Preview and remove attachments before sending; attachment-only messages are supported.

The picker filters for supported image types and text/code extensions, excluding PDF, PowerPoint and other unsupported formats by default. Browsers may allow overriding this filter; attachment validation still rejects unsupported files. Extensionless files such as Makefile can be pasted when the system picker hides them.

- Images: up to four PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF images per message, totaling at most 3 MiB. Known text-only models reject images before sending; custom gateways forward them to the service without a capability checkbox.
- Text files: up to four files, with no application-imposed per-file or combined text byte limit. Supported extensions include TXT, Markdown, JSON, CSV, YAML and common source/configuration formats; extensionless files such as Makefile are also supported. See [the extension list](../../shared/prompt-files.ts).

Text files are decoded as UTF-8 without a parser; an optional UTF-8 BOM is removed, and whitespace is preserved. Invalid UTF-8, binary control characters and unsupported extensions reject with a visible error; contents are never silently truncated. PDF, Office documents, archives and non-UTF-8 encodings are not supported. Prompt JSON bodies have no application-imposed byte limit; image-specific limits still apply.

Loop sends the full text to the model without a local estimated-context rejection. Actual model/provider context limits and browser/server memory still apply; provider failures use the existing error flow and retain drafts and attachments. Files are read and serialized in memory, not stored separately for on-demand reading. Automatic compaction and chunked file retrieval are not implemented.

Click a text attachment's filename to expand its plain-text preview. Sent files appear as compact pills above the message, displaying a file icon, filename and extension; long names shorten while the extension stays visible. Pills wrap and align to the right, alongside right-aligned image previews. Filenames and contents are sent as native text blocks and stored with the session; restored history renders the same expandable pills. No original file is written into the project.

Unsent attachments stay in memory across session switches; refreshing discards them. Unconfirmed requests retain the exact images and text files with their request identity for retry, subject to browser storage availability. Acceptance clears unchanged submitted attachments. Later failures do not restore them over the next draft. Queued text is editable; sent-history editing, regeneration and automatic retries are not supported.

## Source and Tests

- [ChatComposer](../components/chat/ChatComposer.tsx) / [tests](../components/chat/ChatComposer.test.tsx).
- [useComposerInput](../hooks/useComposerInput.ts) / [tests](../hooks/useComposerInput.test.tsx).
- [ComposerAttachments](../components/chat/ComposerAttachments.tsx) / [tests](../components/chat/ComposerAttachments.test.tsx).
- [ComposerAddMenu](../components/chat/ComposerAddMenu.tsx) / [tests](../components/chat/ComposerAddMenu.test.tsx).
- [useComposerAttachments](../hooks/useComposerAttachments.ts) / [tests](../hooks/useComposerAttachments.test.tsx).
- [Text file decoding](../lib/read-text-file.ts) / [tests](../lib/read-text-file.test.ts).
- [Text file contract](../../shared/prompt-files.ts) / [tests](../../shared/prompt-files.test.ts).
- [usePrompt](../hooks/usePrompt.ts) / [tests](../hooks/usePrompt.test.tsx).
- [request-store](../state/request-store.ts) / [tests](../state/request-store.test.ts).
- [SessionStatus](../components/chat/SessionStatus.tsx) / [tests](../components/chat/SessionStatus.test.tsx).
- [LoopingIndicator](../components/chat/LoopingIndicator.tsx) / [translation fallback test](../components/chat/LoopingIndicator.test.tsx), displayed by [MessageTimeline](../components/chat/MessageTimeline.tsx) / [tests](../components/chat/MessageTimeline.test.tsx).

## Queue Controls

Messages display oldest to newest in an inset panel joined to the top of the input. Each compact row shows a single-line text preview with the full text on hover, followed by Steer, a delete icon and a more-options menu. Choose **… → Edit** to edit the complete message in the main chat input after the server confirms an editing hold. Hide the corresponding queue row while it is in the composer; the server keeps its reserved position and skips it so later messages can run. Load the full text, images, file bodies and selected Skills into the composer, temporarily saving the previous unsent draft. Send saves the edited content and Skills at the original reserved position if no later message has been dispatched during editing. Once a later message starts, sending appends the edited item to the queue after all remaining and newly queued messages, without interrupting the active response. Editing uses the ordinary composer surface without an editing banner or Cancel control. Show only one black Send arrow while editing, including during generation or a paused task; hide Stop and Resume until the edit is sent. Empty edits disable Send. A confirmed save restores the previous composer draft and the normal generation controls. Failed saves keep the editor and hold. Disable editing another queued item until the current edit is sent. Session switches retain the editor in memory; a page refresh keeps the server hold but loses the local edit mode and unsaved attachment changes, so the held row can be reopened through **… → Edit**. The delete icon removes an item. The options menu supports keyboard navigation, Escape and outside-click dismissal without being clipped by the queue scroll area. Hover or focus a row to reveal its dotted drag grip beside the queue icon. Dragging uses a full-row preview, dims the placeholder and smoothly shifts neighboring rows into the proposed order when the pointer crosses each original row midpoint. Drop commits one move, including moves after a row or to the end; dropping in the original slot sends no command. Dragging near the scroll edges scrolls the queue. Cancelling, disconnecting or receiving a changed queue clears the preview without submitting a stale move. Focused handles also support Up/Down keys; reduced-motion settings remove the transitions.

Steer marks any item to run after the current response and entire tool batch, before another model call. The selected item displays a waiting state and locks editing/deletion until consumed. When paused, Steer starts the selected input immediately. Stale IDs reject rather than recreating consumed work; use authoritative SSE state before retrying.

Queues and paused state survive page refresh and reconnect to the live server. Server restart or instance disposal discards them. Resume requests continuation from complete history without restoring a stream cursor or replaying finished tools. See [core scheduling](../../../../coding-agent/src/docs/message-queue.md), [queue UI](../components/chat/MessageQueue.tsx) and [tests](../components/chat/MessageQueue.test.tsx).

## New and independent chats

The main area always uses ChatWorkspace. With no selected session it opens an in-process independent draft, displays the empty conversation greeting and the same composer used for history. The first accepted user message replaces only the greeting with the timeline; the composer stays mounted. Empty drafts are excluded from sidebar history and do not persist across backend restarts. A provider must be configured before opening a new draft; creation errors expose Retry.

The project selector shows **No project** by default. Before the first message, select a registered project or remove the selection to start an independent chat. Selecting a different scope creates a new empty handle and transfers unsent text, attachments and model/permission choices. A conversation containing messages cannot change project ownership.

Independent conversations appear under **Chats**. Pinned conversations appear only under **Pinned**. Both use the same session row actions as project conversations. Chats, Pinned and the Projects list initially show five entries; **Show more** reveals ten additional entries per click. Each section supports folding and heading navigation. Empty Chats and Pinned sections are hidden.

pages.title: Streaming State
pages.markdown:
# Streaming State

The frontend receives session updates through a same-origin EventSource. HTTP queries provide initial snapshots; SSE continues with activity, message, and tool events. There is no direct connection from the browser to the model service.

## Loading and Subscribing

ChatWorkspace first requests `/api/sessions/:id`. After it succeeds, useSessionEvents connects to `/api/sessions/:id/events?approvals=1` and passes frames to session-store. Components read the latest display snapshot instead of maintaining separate message histories. The query parameter explicitly enables the session's interactive approval adapter.

| Frame type | Display behavior |
| --- | --- |
| session.snapshot | Initialize or completely replace current state |
| session.state | Synchronize completion, model changes, or save state from a server snapshot |
| run.accepted | Record the accepted requestId/runId and running state |
| loop.event | Update drafts, completed messages, and tool cards by message position |

loop.event preserves the native coding-agent event contract, including the model stream event inside message_update. The browser synchronously commits tool_execution_start updates to React so a burst of start/end events cannot skip the running icon's effect. Other frames use normal updates; results and errors are applied immediately. This uses the existing brief success-icon hold rather than delaying SSE frames or tool execution. The projection replaces drafts with the cumulative message in the event. Do not append that cumulative text again or add the same final message to history twice. prompt_timing upserts state.promptTimings by userMessageIndex, so the duration row recovers the same timestamps on reconnect and stops before saving.

## Reconnection and Deduplication

Drafts preserve the cumulative native assistant message at draftIndex, without a separate thinking/text/tool phase state. Ordinary phase updates, tool batch disclosures and final text render in history order. Native text deltas update cumulative text in place before session settlement; later calls do not relocate that text. Thinking remains in events and snapshots but is hidden from the conversation.

Each view records a streamId/seq cursor. Duplicate frames are ignored. A sequence gap or changed stream in incremental frames closes the connection and requests a full snapshot. Older snapshots behind the current cursor in the same stream are ignored.

After a network error, mark the view disconnected and reconnect with its cursor using exponential delays from 1.5 to 30 seconds. Messages and heartbeats reset the delay. Parse errors request a fresh snapshot. Existing content remains visible while disconnected, but normal sending and model switching are disabled. Reconnect guidance and its Retry button appear only after two seconds without a connection, with the grace period reset on session switches; browser offline guidance appears immediately. See [the SSE service](../../backend/docs/events.md) for replay limits.

Switching sessions closes only the previous view's EventSource. Backend sessions continue, and reopening synchronizes their latest results. If every interactive view disconnects, existing approvals remain pending until a decision, cancellation or session shutdown; reconnecting restores them. New disconnected requests fail closed. Session snapshots/state frames update the open conversation and its header title, including asynchronous title updates that preserve the current operation. See [permissions and approvals](permissions.md).

Permission and approval submissions use the live SSE updates on success and request a fresh snapshot after a failed or uncertain HTTP result. The store then marks that session disconnected, clears its cursor and increments a local connection revision. The hook reconnects without replaying commands. This avoids replacing newer live state with an older HTTP response or interrupting a working connection after each decision.

Before disconnecting, useSessionEvents copies the last connected snapshot's generation status and title into the existing sidebar summary. It cancels older in-flight list requests before this handoff and invalidates the project list for a fresh server result. This preserves the spinner while switching sessions or reconnecting, without retaining a stale running snapshot after a background completion update. Callbacks from unmounted subscriptions are ignored.

## List Synchronization

Session and list streams rebuild when the page returns from hidden to visible, a network-online event arrives, or a page is restored from the back/forward cache. Offline events close streams while preserving loaded content and drafts. A visible-page watchdog checks every 15 seconds and rebuilds connections after more than 45 seconds without a message or observable heartbeat. Late callbacks from closed connections are ignored. Session recovery reuses the cursor; unavailable replay falls back to a snapshot. Retry in the session status requests a fresh snapshot. These paths never resubmit commands. Browser connectivity signals cannot distinguish a sleeping computer from a disconnected tunnel; recovery waits until reachable.

AppShell mounts useListEvents once per page, connecting to `/api/workspaces/events`. This subscription stays open when switching sessions. The backend watches all loaded sessions, allowing background generation status and late titles to update every connected page without five-second polling. Project and archive changes use the same stream.

sessions.changed invalidates the affected project's session query and archived chats. projects.changed also invalidates the project list. lists.reset invalidates all three list caches. Active queries refetch; collapsed or unmounted lists remain stale until used. A 50ms window coalesces bursts of notifications; token deltas do not produce list events. This is change-driven batching, not a periodic refresh.

Before invalidating, the hook cancels older in-flight list requests using AbortSignal. Notifications arriving during a refresh are retained for another batch, preventing a stale response from swallowing a newer change. The shared recovery transport reconnects automatically, and every connection begins with lists.reset. Duplicate incremental frames are ignored; sequence gaps, changed stream identities or malformed JSON force a full list refresh. Unmount closes the connection and cancels pending batches.

The list stream does not change the selected conversation or discard unsent drafts on other pages. It covers this Web process's changes; external CLI or filesystem edits require a reload.

## Boundaries

session-store is held only in memory; refreshing relies on the server for recovery. SSE reconnection does not resubmit prompts or guarantee exactly-once execution across server restarts. [Chat input](chat.md) handles unconfirmed submissions separately.

## Source and Tests

- [ChatWorkspace](../components/chat/ChatWorkspace.tsx) / [tests](../components/chat/ChatWorkspace.test.tsx).
- [useSessionEvents](../hooks/useSessionEvents.ts) / [tests](../hooks/useSessionEvents.test.tsx).
- [useListEvents](../hooks/useListEvents.ts) / [batching and reconnection tests](../hooks/useListEvents.test.tsx).
- [session-store](../state/session-store.ts) / [tests](../state/session-store.test.ts).
- [Shared protocol](../../shared/protocol.ts), [message projection](../../shared/session-projection.ts) / [tests](../../shared/session-projection.test.ts).

pages.title: Integration settings
pages.markdown:
# Integration settings

Open **Settings → Integrations → MCPs** to manage MCP servers, or **Skills** to manage skills. These are separate Settings sections with their own headings and search fields. MCPs uses a plug outline in navigation; Skills uses a document outline. The Skills subtitle and search placeholder read Manage Skills and Search Skills in English. Server rows show transport, current connection status and discovered tool count. The gear edits configuration; the switch persists enabled state; failed connections offer Retry. The header says Manage MCPs. Each integration panel uses the same 18px, medium-weight heading and 13px control text as other Settings sections, with a pill search field and outline search icon. Both titles align vertically with their compact 32px search fields and Add on the first row. Manage MCPs and Manage Skills occupy a separate full-width row below. Skills places Refresh between search and Add. MCPs has no visible server-count badge; Skills keeps its Personal and named-project tabs below the Installed overview. Both catalogs default to two columns, switching to one column below a 480px panel width. Standard rows are about 56px high with 10px vertical padding, 32px icon tiles, 13px names, 12px secondary text and compact actions; MCP errors retain readable wrapping and Retry. Server rows have no card borders; transport icons, server names, status details and blue enabled switches share a consistent alignment. The compact pill Add button uses a 34px minimum height, with black background and white text in Light and the inverse in Dark. Both sections share the same rounded dropdown styling. Skills offers Create skill, Install from GitHub and Add local folder; MCPs offers only Add MCP server. The dropdown has a 196px minimum width, 4px inset and 12px outer radius. Each compact 32px row has a muted 16px outline icon, 12px label and 8px icon-to-label gap. Selecting an action opens its inline form in the current section; pointer selection and Enter activate it, arrow keys cycle between items, Escape closes the menu and restores trigger focus, and clicking outside or pressing Tab dismisses it. Transient focus changes during pointer activation do not remove the item before its click opens the form.
