Re-adding a registered folder reveals its existing node without duplication or renaming. Failed saves retain the name and folder for retry. Cancel, Close and Escape discard the unsaved selection; closing while the picker is open cancels its request.

New empty sessions show only a project capsule above the input. Hover or keyboard-focus it to reveal **×** in a compact 16px gray circle with a centered 14px icon; removing the selection preserves text and attachments and disables sending, including Enter. **Choose project** opens the registered-project menu and focuses **Search projects** at the top. Search filters project names immediately, ignores case and trims surrounding spaces; clearing search restores the full list, and reopening the menu starts with an empty search. Arrow keys move from search to the available choices; Escape closes the menu. Search and **Add folder…** remain visible while long project lists scroll. No matches shows a hint and still allows adding a folder; inaccessible folders cannot be selected. **Add folder…** opens the same Create project dialog, then selects the registered folder. Switching projects creates a new empty session under that folder and transfers unsent text and attachments, keeping the model, effort and permission preset. A failed switch keeps the existing draft for retry. Clearing is remembered across reloads during the server's draft lifetime. After the first submission, the session retains its project and the capsule disappears.

2. Click the project row to expand or collapse its history; the folder icon opens and closes with it. Hover or keyboard focus highlights the row and reveals **…** and the compose pencil. Touch devices keep these actions visible. Click the pencil to open a new draft. It becomes a sidebar session only after its first user message is accepted into the conversation.
3. Each project initially shows up to five history entries. If more exist, click **Show more** to reveal the next ten, or all remaining entries when fewer than ten remain. The button disappears when all entries are visible. Click a history entry to select it. Switch conversations through the sidebar; the folder button opens the project drawer on narrow screens.
4. Hover or keyboard-focus a session row to highlight it and reveal its Pin and Archive icon buttons. Touch devices keep both visible. Pin moves the session into Pinned; its button then becomes Unpin, which returns it to its project's normal ordering. Click Archive to archive that chat immediately. Right-click the title, or press Shift+F10 while it has focus, to open Rename, Pin (or Unpin), Archive and Permanently delete without switching the selected chat.

A local macOS service opens the system folder picker. If selection fails, the dialog shows a retryable error. Cancelling selection does not create a project. Folder selection accesses the computer running the Web service.

## State and Interfaces

| Operation | Request and state |
| --- | --- |
| Query, add, rename, or remove a project | useProjects calls `/api/workspaces` and refreshes the project cache on success |
| Select a source folder | useDirectoryPicker calls the system folder picker API |
| Query history | useProjectSessions and PinnedSessions share queries by workspaceId; all accessible registered projects load independently of expansion so saved pins can be discovered |
| Reveal more history | SessionList displays five unpinned summaries initially and adds up to ten per click, independently for each project; Pinned displays all pins |
| Pin or unpin | useSessionActions sends PUT /api/sessions/:id/pin with workspaceId and pinned; the server saves header pinnedAt and refreshes project summaries |
| Start a draft | Submit workspaceId and select the returned draft handle; no history file or sidebar item is created yet |
| Open an existing session | workspace-store records the selected session and its project; the view loads a snapshot and subscribes to events |

Drafts show **New session** in the header but do not appear under their project. Typing, adding attachments, changing models, renaming the header or clicking New session repeatedly does not create sidebar items. The first user message adds the item during the run; an image-only or file-only message also counts. Empty submissions and preflight failures do not create items. Older unarchived records without user messages are hidden without deleting their files. When no generated or manual title exists, the first eligible user text supplies the fallback title, including for restored historical sessions. New conversations also make an independent model request to generate a short title in the prompt's language. Saved titles appear in the header and sidebar rows. Failed generation keeps the existing title. Project renaming remains available through the API; the previous inline Rename/Remove links are replaced by the project menu.

The header contains only a folder icon and the session name above a single divider. Its folder icon matches the collapsed project icon in shape, size and stroke. Its background matches the conversation, with compact spacing between the left border, folder and title. The folder button and title control sit directly beside each other; their internal padding separates the icon and text while preserving both click areas. Long titles truncate to fit. Hovering or keyboard-focusing the name highlights it, with 8px padding on either side of the text. The padding stays consistent during hover and editing. Click to edit with the current text selected; Enter confirms, while Escape or clicking outside cancels. Enter during IME composition does not submit. Blank names cannot be saved; failed saves retain the draft and show an error. Successful saves pin the manual title and update the header and sidebar immediately. Editing is unavailable during another session operation or pending history save. Title regeneration remains available through the SDK/API, with no header button.

Active sessions receive title updates through SSE, including results arriving after the answer. A page-level list event stream refreshes affected project lists when background sessions change, including late titles, and resynchronizes lists on reconnect. There is no periodic list polling. Reading untitled history derives a fallback without making a model request or rewriting the session file. See [list synchronization](events.md#list-synchronization) and [title policy](../../../../coding-agent/src/docs/session-titles.md).

A small rotating ring at the far right of a session row indicates response generation, including model waiting, streaming and tool execution. Live session events update the open session immediately; background sessions refresh through list change notifications. The ring disappears when generation ends and does not appear for model changes, saves or title updates. Long titles truncate before the ring. Reduced-motion preferences keep the ring static.

While approval is pending, an 8px yellow dot appears to the left of the session title without shifting its alignment, and a static 14px clock icon replaces the right-hand generation ring. Both indicators have a **Waiting for approval** / **等待审批** tooltip; only the clock carries the accessible label to avoid duplicate announcements. The waiting indicators take priority over the generation ring and unread dot without changing read receipts. Waiting sessions remain selectable and can be pinned or unpinned; Rename, Archive and Permanently delete are disabled. The indicator clears when all pending requests resolve or are cancelled; generation then resumes its ring when still running.

Switching to another session preserves the previous session's latest live status in the list cache before closing its subscription. Older pending list requests are cancelled and a fresh summary is requested, keeping its ring or approval dot visible during the handoff. Background list updates clear the ring when generation finishes, including cancellation and failure.

After generation ends with new output, an 8px blue dot replaces the ring until the latest content has been viewed. Its tooltip and accessible label are **Unread** / **未读**. Selecting a session alone does not clear it: the completed content must reach the conversation viewport in a visible, focused browser page. Scrolling to the latest content or opening a completed chat at its latest content clears the dot; staying at the submitted user message while a longer answer grows leaves it unread. Hidden pages, open dialogs and the mobile sidebar overlay do not mark messages read. Generation keeps the ring instead of the dot.

A boolean unread persists in each session header and survives browser changes, session switches, reloads and server restarts. Reading in one browser updates the other browsers through list notifications. The dot clears after the server confirms the receipt; failed saves remain unread and retry while the completed content is visible. Read requests include the displayed message count so an older page cannot clear newer output. The sidebar renders unread directly; it does not calculate completed turns or keep a read-position cache. Background sessions receive the header flag through list refreshes, including when reopening a collapsed project or reconnecting. Title/model changes and save retries do not set unread again. A cancelled or failed run with saved output can be unread; a run with only a user message cannot. Missing unread metadata defaults to false. Read receipts belong to the Loop server's data directory; separate installations do not synchronize.

## Lifecycle and Errors

Revealing more entries changes only the visible portion of the cached session list; it does not make another history request. List refreshes retain the current display limit. Collapsing and reopening a project or the Projects group, or reloading the page, resets the limit to five.

The Pin icon is a diagonal outlined pushpin with a rounded head and shoulder, shared by the row button and context menu. Unpin adds a diagonal slash to the same outline.

**Pin** sits directly below Rename in the context menu and changes to **Unpin** for pinned sessions. Pins persist in the session header as optional pinnedAt timestamps, shared by browsers connected to the same server and restored after restarts. Missing pinnedAt means unpinned; the latest timestamp sorts first, with session ID as a stable tie-breaker. The sidebar loads summaries for every accessible registered project even when Projects is collapsed. A successful pin request updates the shared list cache and publishes a sessions.changed notification; other pages and reconnects refresh from the server. Pin changes preserve the current conversation, activity timestamp and drafts, and remain available during generation or approval waiting. Buttons prevent duplicate submissions while saving. Failed requests show a row error and refetch to reconcile uncertain delivery. Archived chats retain their pin for restoration; removing a project hides its pins without modifying session files, so re-adding it restores them. Permanent deletion removes the header with its history. There is no browser pin storage.

The session context menu supports arrows, Home/End and Escape, fits within the viewport and stays above sidebar scrolling. **Rename** edits the row inline: Enter saves, Escape or blur cancels, and failed saves retain the input. **Archive** immediately removes only that session from the sidebar and keeps its history, drafts and attachments for restoration from Settings. Neither action asks for confirmation. **Permanently delete** opens a confirmation warning that the chat and its saved messages will be deleted irreversibly. Cancel and Close do not submit; the confirmation disables closing and duplicate submission while pending. Success removes the complete session storage directory (metadata, messages and index), any retained legacy JSONL backup and associated traces, clears only that chat's local drafts, attachments and pending request, and closes it if selected. Failures retain local data. Deletion errors stay inside the confirmation dialog; closing it or choosing a new row action clears the previous error, so it does not appear under the session title or carry into a new confirmation. Known busy sessions disable Rename, Archive and Permanently delete; the backend also rejects archive and deletion while any session in the project is busy or has pending saves.

Switching sessions preserves unsent drafts and in-memory image attachments, keeps history, and does not stop backend generation. Returning retrieves current state through a snapshot. Reloading restores the selected session. An unavailable project directory shows **Directory unavailable** and disables new sessions for that project.

The project **…** button and right-clicking the project row open the same menu containing **Archive chats** and **Remove project**, separated by a divider. Both items use the same neutral text and icon color. Right-clicking does not expand, collapse or select a session. Arrow keys and Home/End navigate; Escape closes and restores focus. The menu stays within the viewport and is not clipped by sidebar scrolling.

**Archive chats** loads all currently unarchived chats even when the project is collapsed, then asks for confirmation with their count and project name. **Archive all** archives exactly that confirmed selection; chats created afterward remain visible. Archiving changes only archive membership: metadata, messages, index and any legacy backup remain in place on disk and are excluded from the sidebar. Restoring a chat reuses those same files. The selected chat closes after success, while drafts, attachments and unconfirmed requests remain intact. Open **Settings → Archived → Archived chats** to view and restore chats from registered, accessible projects. **Unarchive** returns a chat to its project list. Re-add a removed directory to access its archived chats again.

The archive page groups chats into rounded project cards, with folder icons, chat counts, titles and localized last-update timestamps. Filter by project or by all chats, chats with messages, and empty chats. There is no search field. Click a title to open the chat and close Settings. The trash button deletes one archived chat; the project menu deletes all archived chats in that project; **Delete all** targets every loaded archived chat, regardless of filters. Each deletion requires a second confirmation with its exact count and a permanent-deletion warning. Project files and unarchived chats are preserved. Local drafts and unconfirmed requests are cleared only for successfully deleted chats. Requests run project by project; if one fails, already completed deletions remain completed and the confirmation shows the remaining selection for retry.

**Remove project** requires confirmation explaining that local files and saved chats will remain. If drafts or unconfirmed requests exist, the dialog additionally warns that unsent data will be discarded. After the backend succeeds, the frontend clears that project's drafts, attachments and unconfirmed requests. If its session is selected, the main area opens a new independent chat. Busy sessions, pending creation/loading or pending saves prevent archive, restore and removal; failures retain frontend state and display an error in the dialog. Cancel, Escape and the close button do not submit changes; closing and repeat submissions are disabled during the request.

The Create project dialog uses a compact 480px width and 360px height, an 18px title, and 13px inputs, folder labels and actions to match existing dialogs. It keeps the same dimensions while selecting or removing a folder, saving and displaying errors. Longer content scrolls within its content area; the footer remains visible. Its size adapts to the viewport.

Each project has one source folder. System folder selection requires local macOS; unavailable pickers show an error in the dialog. There is no typed-path input or browser directory navigator. There is no file-tree editor, history search, or session transfer between projects. See [project registration](../../backend/docs/projects.md) for backend path normalization and persistence.

## Source and Tests

- [Composer project selector](../components/chat/ComposerProjectSelector.tsx) / [tests](../components/chat/ComposerProjectSelector.test.tsx).
- [Draft project selection](../hooks/useComposerProject.ts) / [tests](../hooks/useComposerProject.test.tsx).
- [Create project dialog](../components/projects/AddProjectDialog.tsx) / [tests](../components/projects/AddProjectDialog.test.tsx).
- [Create project state](../hooks/useCreateProject.ts) / [tests](../hooks/useCreateProject.test.tsx).
- [Source-folder selection](../components/projects/ProjectSourceFolders.tsx) and [folder row](../components/projects/ProjectSourceFolder.tsx).
- [Sidebar](../components/layout/Sidebar.tsx) / [tests](../components/layout/Sidebar.test.tsx).
- [SessionItem](../components/projects/SessionItem.tsx) / [tests](../components/projects/SessionItem.test.tsx).
- [Unread row indicators](../components/projects/SessionList.test.tsx), [read receipts](../hooks/useReadReceipt.ts) / [tests](../hooks/useReadReceipt.test.tsx).
- [Session actions](../hooks/useSessionActions.ts) / [tests](../hooks/useSessionActions.test.tsx).
- [ProjectItem](../components/projects/ProjectItem.tsx) / [tests](../components/projects/ProjectItem.test.tsx).
- [ProjectActions](../components/projects/ProjectActions.tsx) / [tests](../components/projects/ProjectActions.test.tsx).
- [Confirmation dialogs](../components/projects/ProjectConfirmation.tsx) / [tests](../components/projects/ProjectConfirmation.test.tsx).
- [Pinned sessions](../components/projects/PinnedSessions.tsx) / [tests](../components/projects/PinnedSessions.test.tsx).
- [Archived chats](../components/settings/ArchivedChats.tsx) / [tests](../components/settings/ArchivedChats.test.tsx).
- [useProjects](../hooks/useProjects.ts) / [tests](../hooks/useProjects.test.tsx).
- [useProjectSessions](../hooks/useProjectSessions.ts) / [tests](../hooks/useProjectSessions.test.tsx).
- [useDirectoryPicker](../hooks/useDirectoryPicker.ts) / [tests](../hooks/useDirectoryPicker.test.tsx).
- [workspace-store](../state/workspace-store.ts) / [tests](../state/workspace-store.test.ts).
- [SessionName](../components/layout/SessionName.tsx) / [tests](../components/layout/SessionName.test.tsx).
- [useSessionRename](../hooks/useSessionRename.ts) / [tests](../hooks/useSessionRename.test.tsx).

The local session context menu includes **Reveal** with a folder icon. It opens the saved session’s storage folder in the server computer’s file manager, including while generation is running. Unsaved sessions report an error. This action is unavailable to remote devices.

## Independent conversations

The sidebar has separate Pinned, Chats and Projects sections. Chats contains unpinned conversations created with no project. Each section initially shows five entries; Show more reveals the next ten. Independent chats support the same rename, pin, archive, restore and delete actions as project chats. Project membership is fixed after the first message. See [chat input](chat.md#new-and-independent-chats).

pages.title: Mobile Layout and Installed App
pages.markdown:
# Mobile Layout and Installed App

Loop can be installed from a production build on a secure origin. It keeps the same remote pairing and permission checks as the browser. Installation provides a home-screen entry and a standalone window; the computer, Loop process and tunnel must remain available for chats.

## Usage

1. Build with pnpm build, start Loop and connect the private tunnel in **Settings → Remote access**.
2. Pair the phone in its browser and approve it on the computer.
3. Choose **Install Loop** when offered. Otherwise choose **Add to home screen** for instructions. On iPhone or iPad, open in Safari, choose Share, then Add to Home Screen. On Android, use Install app or Add to home screen in the browser menu.
4. Open the home-screen entry. If its storage is separate, use a fresh invitation and approve pairing there.

Installation is optional. Dismiss hides the hint for the current page. Browser policy determines whether a native install prompt is available. Embedded browsers can require opening Safari or Chrome first.

## Mobile Controls

The sidebar becomes a drawer below 768px. Opening it moves focus inside and makes the conversation inert; Tab stays within its controls, Escape and the scrim close it. Returning to a desktop width restores access to the conversation.

Below 768px, session rows hide the inline pin button. Pinning and unpinning remain available in the session context menu.

Header, sidebar and composer account for safe-area insets. Primary chat and approval controls use at least 44px touch heights. Permission and model menus remain scrollable, and approvals have a bounded scrolling area above the composer. The toolbar wraps when both Stop and Send are available.

On devices with a coarse primary pointer, Enter inserts a newline. Tap Send to submit, or use Ctrl/Command+Enter on an attached keyboard. IME composition never submits. Opening or switching chats does not automatically open the touch keyboard. The existing visual-viewport adjustment keeps bottom-aligned messages above the composer when the keyboard appears.

## Cache and Offline Behavior

The shared theme suppresses the browser's transient tap-highlight overlay on touch screens, including the pairing page. Interface labels, navigation, session lists, menus and action controls do not support long-press text selection or native touch callouts on controls. Message bodies, code, file contents, error details and text inputs remain selectable. Keyboard focus indicators, scrolling and component interaction states remain available.

The build produces /manifest.webmanifest, /sw.js, /offline.html and 192px/512px PNG icons. Public icons, including the light/dark loading logos, are served directly at the origin root in development and production. The manifest starts at / without invitation codes or credentials. Its link includes credentials for private tunnel access. Registration occurs only in a production build in a secure context; remote pairing remains a separate lightweight bootstrap.

The service worker precaches only the generic offline page, manifest and installation icons. An exact build-generated allowlist permits caching successful JavaScript, CSS, image and font downloads. Query-bearing requests, cross-origin requests, non-GET requests, APIs, authorization endpoints, errors, redirects and HTML returned for scripts are excluded. Conversation HTML, API responses, SSE, invitations and authentication material are never written to this cache. Existing browser draft preferences retain their previous behavior.

Navigations always use the network. On devtunnels.ms subdomains, the worker leaves document navigation entirely to the browser, including refreshes and Microsoft sign-in redirects. It does not call respondWith or fetch for these navigations, preserving the native navigation and cookie context. Static caching remains available. On other origins, a network failure, HTTP 503 or a navigation that has not returned headers within 15 seconds returns a generic themed offline page with Retry; timed-out downloads are aborted. Private tunnel navigation uses the browser's network error page instead. Neither path displays cached chats or accepts offline commands. HTTP authentication failures retain their real response. The in-app offline message reflects the browser connectivity signal, which does not prove the computer or tunnel is reachable.

## Updates and Limits

Frontend builds publish staged assets before atomically replacing HTML entries and publishing the worker last. Failed builds leave the previous frontend available, and old hashed resources remain readable by open tabs until the output is explicitly cleaned while stopped. The pnpm dev command builds the remote frontend on startup and automatically rebuilds after frontend source, shared protocol or build configuration edits. Changes debounce for 500 milliseconds; edits during a build queue one subsequent build. Failures preserve the last successful release and the next edit retries. Refresh the phone after publication or choose Reload to update when offered. Manual builds remain available with pnpm --filter @loop/web-ui build:frontend.

A downloaded update shows **Reload to update** and **Later**. Finish unsent input or approval before choosing reload. The worker does not force-reload an existing chat; only an explicit update action requests activation and reloads that page. The browser checks for updates on registration, when the page becomes visible and when it goes online. Failed registration or update checks leave normal browser use available.

Explicit updates reload at most once even if the worker emits repeated activation events. If activation does not respond within two seconds, or posting the activation message fails, the page reloads anyway. If the old document still runs 250 milliseconds after requesting reload, it replaces the current entry with the root URL as a recovery attempt. This fallback neither clears device authorization nor guarantees completion of an external sign-in flow.

Installation is tied to the exact public hostname. If a new tunnel has a different address, add a new home-screen entry and pair again. Installation cannot keep the computer awake, bypass tunnel sign-in or preserve a connection while the computer sleeps. Foreground and network recovery use the shared [stream lifecycle](events.md). Transient authorization-check network/5xx failures preserve already-loaded chats with a retry notice; explicit denial, expiry or revocation clears access and cached session state. First authorization still fails closed. Background streaming and notifications are not provided.

When launched with `pnpm dev`, backend source edits restart a separate business worker while the gateway, private Tunnel and pairing stay alive. Opening the remote document during that interval displays a retrying recovery page. Existing chats reconnect after the worker is ready; active generation is interrupted and commands are not replayed. Stopping the whole development command still disconnects the Tunnel.

## Device Verification

[Voice input and calls](voice.md) are foreground features. Microphone and playback require a tap and browser permission; backgrounding or locking pauses the call. Returning to the page can require Continue voice. PWA installation does not grant background microphone access or guarantee uninterrupted audio.

Remote startup bounds authorization checks, including body reads, to 10 seconds and chat downloads to 30 seconds. Failures expose Retry; module-load failures reload the root URL so the browser can request current entry assets. The HTML loading placeholder also exposes a root-page retry after 35 seconds if startup scripts have not replaced it. This recovery does not clear device cookies, unregister the worker or automatically repeat pairing commands.

Use a production frontend build and an approved device. These checks require real Android/iOS browsers and the deployed tunnel; automated tests do not establish carrier, regional connectivity or Microsoft sign-in behavior.

1. Start a response, background the browser, then return: the stream catches up without a new prompt.
2. Disable the phone network: offline status appears and sending is disabled. Restore connectivity or switch Wi-Fi/mobile data: messages and lists synchronize without replaying commands.
3. Interrupt connectivity after sending but before acceptance: the request stays recoverable. Check and retry confirms acceptance or reuses its ID within the same server stream.
4. Restart the backend between confirmation and submission: the obsolete stream is rejected; inspect history before manually sending anew.
5. Sleep and wake the computer: it is unreachable while asleep; the page catches up after network/tunnel recovery.
6. Revoke the device from the desktop: streams end and private chat data is removed. Pair again to reconnect.

## Source and Tests

- [Build plugin](../../../pwa-plugin.ts) / [tests](../../../pwa-plugin.test.ts).
- [Service worker](../pwa/service-worker.ts) / [tests](../pwa/service-worker.test.ts).
- [Browser lifecycle](../pwa/pwa-client.ts) / [tests](../pwa/pwa-client.test.ts).
- [Installation and update status](../components/pwa/PwaStatus.tsx) / [tests](../components/pwa/PwaStatus.test.tsx).
- [Remote pairing](remote-access.md), [chat input](chat.md), [approvals](permissions.md).

Mobile layout applies to viewports below 768 CSS pixels and to devices with a coarse primary pointer up to 1024 CSS pixels. The sidebar drawer, focus isolation, composer and Settings share this condition and update automatically when folding, unfolding or rotating changes the viewport. Wider viewports retain the desktop layout.

Mobile conversations, session titles, list entries and tool summaries use 16px text; secondary controls use 13–14px. Browser text autosizing is kept at 100% so folding or rotation does not apply inconsistent text enlargement. Browser desktop-site mode or a saved page zoom can still scale the entire page.

Mobile HTML enables interactive-widget=resizes-content where supported. The document and root are constrained to the viewport, with a 16px body baseline. The composer reserves a 72px text area, uses 44px minimum toolbar targets and 22px send/attachment icons; the header reserves 56px. VisualViewport continues to manage the visible shell height during keyboard changes.

pages.title: Remote Connection Settings
pages.markdown:
# Remote Connection Settings

**Settings → Remote access** controls an experimental private Microsoft Dev Tunnel hosted by the computer's Web process. The section is available in English and Chinese. Other settings and the local chat interface remain usable while connecting.

## Usage

Follow the four compact vertical steps. Each step has a small empty circle until complete, then a green check; thicker vertical separators leave a gap before and after each circle. Action icons sit immediately to the left of the step title. Hover shows the full action label even when the button is disabled, and each button has the same accessible name. Disabled actions remain unavailable. Actions unlock as their prerequisites complete:

1. **Install Dev Tunnels CLI** downloads and verifies the official CLI or verifies the existing installation.
2. **Sign in** opens Microsoft sign-in in the computer's system browser. A system credential prompt can appear first; the progress track tooltip and accessible status ask for that approval before browser sign-in.
3. **Connect Tunnel** starts hosting using the CLI account authorized through Sign in. Step 3 keeps one plug button: Connect Tunnel uses diagonal, rounded plug halves with visible prongs and a gap. After connection, the title and button change to Disconnect Tunnel with the halves joined along a diagonal seam. Both icons use the current theme color and contain no embedded text. The plug button is disabled while connecting or disconnecting; no extra Stop / cancel button appears. A host authorization failure is reported for an explicit retry.
4. **Paired devices** displays the pairing QR code automatically after connection, then shows desktop approval requests and paired-device revocation.

**Uninstall Dev Tunnels CLI** replaces the first step title and its action tooltip after installation. The uninstall icon sits to the left of the title. The title stays Uninstall during removal and returns to Install Dev Tunnels CLI only after removal succeeds. Clicking Uninstall immediately shows the same full shimmering progress track to the right of its title and a loading ring in Step 1, continuing while the backend removes the CLI. No percentage, Pause, Stop or separate status caption appears; localized uninstall guidance stays in the tooltip and accessible status. Completion, removal failure or an unconfirmed request removes the track. The track follows the shared theme, forced-color and reduced-motion behavior. It is disabled during status checks, downloads (including paused downloads), sign-in, uninstalling and hosting. Uninstall removes only the currently managed executable, preserves Microsoft credentials and other CLI installations, resets the completion checks and restores Install. Removal failures retain the installed state and allow retry; starting uninstall clears the remembered sign-in even if removal later fails.

Every entry into this section checks installation and reads the remembered sign-in and current host state, even when a previous status is cached. During this check, step markers show loading rings instead of completion checks. An active action similarly replaces its step marker with a loading ring, without a check or cross. The rings follow the current theme and respect reduced motion. Previously completed steps show a red cross when a later check or operation fails; untouched incomplete steps keep an empty circle. A failed status request marks cached completed steps as check failures, without claiming which underlying service failed. Retry shows loading rings instead of crosses; a successful check restores confirmed completion marks. Installation failures, explicit reauthorization failures and unexpected exit of a connected tunnel retain their step failure in the current backend process until recovery. Intentional Stop, Sign out and Uninstall reset the affected steps without adding crosses. Setup actions are disabled until the entry check succeeds; failed checks offer **Retry**. Checking never installs the CLI, opens sign-in or starts/stops hosting.

No application IDs, scopes or terminal commands are required. Unsupported operating systems or CPU architectures show an explanation and disable setup actions. Hover over the heading's info button to see Microsoft's license terms and privacy statement links. The tooltip opens to the right of the button, or above it when horizontal space is limited, keeping the steps below clear. Keyboard focus or clicking the button also opens this tooltip; Tab reaches its links and Escape dismisses it.

Independent row sizing and 12px gaps keep step spacing compact. Warnings and errors appear to the right of the action icon and title on the same row; wrapped messages expand only their own step. Empty detail areas are hidden, and vertical separators retain clear gaps around the circles. Starting, finishing or canceling a download keeps the following steps in place. Installing reveals a compact progress bar immediately to the right of Install Dev Tunnels CLI on the same line. The row reads: installation label, progress track, percentage, Pause / Resume, then Stop and delete download. No download size or status caption appears below the track. The track shrinks to fit the available space and long step labels truncate with their full text available on hover. Pausing preserves the partial file and percentage, stops progress animations and releases the download request. Resume requests the remaining bytes; if the source does not support ranges, it restarts from zero. Stop deletes the unfinished file; the next installation starts fresh. Pause survives switching Settings sections within the running Web process, but does not resume across process restarts. Known download totals drive its filled length and percentage; the remaining track stays hollow. A highlight sweeps left to right within the filled portion. Before the total is known, an indeterminate segment shows activity without inventing a percentage. The colors follow Light, Dark and System themes, and reduced-motion preferences disable the sweep and transitions. Unknown totals show an em dash in the percentage slot rather than an invented percentage. Download, pause and installation details remain available in the track tooltip and accessible status. Once the transfer finishes, the tooltip and accessible status change to **Verifying and installing…** (localized in Chinese); Pause / Resume disappears, the percentage slot shows an em dash and the full track keeps shimmering while verification and installation run. The empty Pause / Resume slot stays reserved to the right of the percentage so the track and Stop button do not shift. Stop / cancel remains on the right. The first marker keeps loading until verification and installation succeed; only then does it show a green check and unlock Sign in. No extra step is added. The bar disappears after completion, cancellation or failure. Sign-in and connection checks keep their own step active while verifying an installed CLI, without displaying progress in the installation step. If that check discovers a missing or invalid executable, automatic reinstallation displays the bar in the first step. Sign-in shows the same progress track inline beside its label, filled to full width with the shared shimmer animation. It shows no visible guidance, percentage, Pause or Stop controls; the full fill indicates activity, not completed authorization, so no numeric percentage is reported to assistive technology. The credential/browser guidance stays available in its tooltip and accessible status. Theme, forced-color and reduced-motion behavior match installation, and the track disappears on success, failure or timeout. Connecting shows the same full shimmering track immediately to the right of Connect Tunnel, starting when the action is requested and continuing while the backend is connecting. It replaces the visible Connecting… caption, shows no percentage or cancellation controls, and retains the localized status in its tooltip and screen-reader announcement. The track disappears on connection, failure or cancellation. Other progress appears within its corresponding step. The sign-in step has no Stop / cancel icon while authorization is in progress; it waits for success, failure or the three-minute deadline. Download cancellation remains available; tunnel connection and disconnection use only the plug button.

Connected status is shown by the completed Step 3 marker and Disconnect Tunnel title and action. The settings screen hides the service's HTTPS address and the redundant Tunnel connected caption. Remote clients must complete [device pairing](#device-pairing) before accessing chats; desktop configuration remains local. PWA installation is not yet implemented.

Disconnect Tunnel closes hosting and clears the connection check while keeping completed installation and sign-in checks. During shutdown, Step 3 shows its loading ring, disabled Disconnect Tunnel action and the same full shimmering progress track to the right of the title. The track appears as soon as disconnect is requested and stays visible while the backend is stopping, without a visible Stopping… caption, percentage or extra controls. Localized shutdown guidance remains in the track tooltip and screen-reader status. Completion or failure removes the track. The same presentation applies when Sign out first disconnects the tunnel; only after shutdown succeeds does progress move to the account step. **Sign out** replaces the Step 2 title and action tooltip after successful sign-in and is also available while connected. The title and disabled action remain Sign out during tunnel shutdown and account sign-out, then return to Sign in when sign-out finishes. It first stops the tunnel with only Step 3 loading; Step 2 keeps its completed marker until stopping succeeds. Then Step 3 becomes incomplete and Step 2 shows a loading ring and the full shimmering account progress track while signing out. When the tunnel is already disconnected, Step 2 shows its loading ring and Sign out progress track immediately on click, including while waiting for the command response. Account sign-out uses the same full shimmering track beside the label, without a percentage or extra controls; localized guidance stays in the tooltip and accessible status. Completion, account failure or an unconfirmed request removes the account track. A stop failure stays in Step 3 and preserves sign-in without invoking logout; an account-stage failure appears in Step 2. Sign out clears the sign-in step and uses the official CLI's shared account store for the current OS user, so it can sign other Dev Tunnels CLI uses out too. It does not sign the Microsoft browser session out. After a successful connection, Loop also remembers that the tunnel should stay enabled. A backend restart starts a fresh connection with the Step 3 loading ring and progress track, then shows Disconnect Tunnel after CLI readiness and stable cloud connection verification. During connection or automatic recovery, Disconnect Tunnel remains available to cancel hosting. It reuses the saved persistent tunnel and port so the address remains stable; occupied ports or missing cloud resources report failure instead of silently changing it. The initial migration from temporary hosting creates a new address and requires pairing once there. A tunnel can expire after thirty days without activity; service activity extends that window. Disconnect, sign-out, reauthorization, uninstall or a missing/invalid CLI clears this preference; normal shutdown preserves it. Startup reconnect requires the verified CLI and remembered sign-in, never downloads or launches browser login, and can require system credential-store approval. Initial restore failure appears in the responsible step for manual retry without claiming success. After an established host exits or cloud checks twice confirm disconnection, Loop shows Step 3 connection progress and retries the same tunnel up to six times with bounded backoff. Cloud API errors alone preserve a working host. Stop or sign-out cancels recovery; exhausted retries report the connection error for manual retry. The last successful Sign in survives backend restarts, so Connect becomes available after the installation check. Loop stores only a versioned boolean at `<dataRoot>/web-ui/remote-access/sign-in.json`; credentials remain in the CLI account store. A separate versioned enabled boolean at `<dataRoot>/web-ui/remote-access/connection.json` stores only the reconnect preference, without credentials or addresses. Failed preference writes appear in Step 3; disconnect still closes hosting, but the preference must be cleared by retrying after storage permissions are fixed. The marker is cleared before reauthorization, sign-out or uninstall, and when the managed executable is missing or invalid. Missing, unreadable or invalid state starts unconfirmed. If the marker cannot be saved, the operation shows a translated error and does not complete. Failed reauthorization or cancellation before CLI success leaves it unconfirmed. Stop, shutdown and ordinary tunnel failures preserve the remembered sign-in. This is a remembered result, not proof that credentials are still valid: external CLI logout, Keychain changes or revoked service access are not detected by opening Settings. If connection reports an authorization problem, use Sign out and Sign in to reauthorize. The CLI can reuse its own saved credentials. The saved tunnel identity and ingress port keep the address stable across reconnects.

## State and Errors

The frontend uses the local [control API](../../backend/docs/remote-access.md#local-control-api), requests a fresh check on mount, and polls the in-memory state every 1.5 seconds afterward without restarting checks or flashing loading rings. A failed status request stops automatic polling until a manual Retry succeeds; window focus and network reconnection do not retry failed status checks. During active installation, sign-in, sign-out, connection or stopping, entry checks use the operation's current state without competing with the CLI. Query cancellation prevents an old status response from replacing a command response. The remembered sign-in result is not an independent check of credentials or current service authorization; host status reflects CLI readiness and exit notifications, not an independent network health probe.

Status distinguishes off, preparing/downloading, verifying and installing, uninstalling, browser sign-in, sign-out, connecting, connected, stopping and failure. Displayed errors use translated fixed codes, never raw CLI or identity responses. Download/save failures omit the explanatory alert and leave the install action available for retry; integrity failures retain their alert. Installation, uninstall, sign-in and connection errors appear to the right of their own step’s action icon and title, with a red warning icon followed by translated text. Wrapped lines retain the same message alignment. In-progress messages below the heading align with the step title. Unsupported-platform guidance appears as a yellow warning in Step 1. Unconfirmed command requests show a yellow warning in the step where the action was requested; only section-wide status request failures remain below the steps with Retry. The backend’s `errorStep` identifies the failed operation even when a connection request first installs the CLI or signs in. Sign-in and connection errors explain the next action. Network-command failures tell the user to refresh status before trying again.

Opening this section and automatic status requests never invoke CLI account commands or read Keychain credentials. Explicit sign-in, sign-out and tunnel operations can trigger a macOS Keychain authorization dialog for the CLI credential item. This is an OS credential-store prompt, not a Microsoft browser sign-in or installation prompt. It requests the login keychain password, which is usually the macOS account password. The CLI can wait inside this credential read before opening a browser, so no browser window does not by itself mean that the login command was not started. Complete the macOS prompt manually; if canceled, wait for the sign-in failure or timeout before retrying. Approving once may require approval on later CLI invocations; Always Allow changes the keychain access permission for the requesting executable. Loop does not enter passwords or change those permissions automatically.

The frontend does not receive or persist Microsoft credentials or host tokens in JavaScript storage. The local control cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict. Remote clients enter through the [pairing gate](../../backend/docs/remote-devices.md); settings and project administration are available only on the computer.


## Device Pairing

**Step 4 → Paired devices** automatically generates a pairing QR code once Step 3 is connected. The fourth marker shows a green check while at least one device has valid pairing authorization, including while another QR code is generated. Each paired device also shows a green check and its localized authorization expiry date. If all remaining devices have expired, Step 4 shows a red cross; individual expired devices retain their red cross even when another device is valid. A newly unpaired list keeps an empty marker. Scan the QR code with the phone. The brief “Scan with your phone.” guidance appears to the right of Paired devices; the QR image below has no pairing link. The paired-device list sits to the right of the QR image, with a maximum height of 208px matching the code; additional devices scroll vertically inside the list. Pending approval requests remain above this row, and the list uses the full row when no QR image is available. The invitation expires after five minutes and can be used once. Its URL uses Step 3’s public tunnel origin plus a one-use pairing secret in the fragment; the bare tunnel address alone cannot pair a device. Ordinary status polling does not replace the code. The single-arrow **Refresh pairing code** icon immediately left of Paired devices replaces the invitation and QR code on demand, including while a code is valid, without changing the tunnel URL. While this settings section remains open, an expired code is automatically replaced if the tunnel is connected and no pairing request awaits a decision. Failed generation, including an already-expired response, stops automatic renewal and leaves the icon available for manual retry. Refresh is disabled while disconnected, generating, processing a device action or awaiting a pairing decision. A new tunnel connection generates a fresh code and discards late results from the old connection. While a device request is pending, the used QR code is hidden; after the request is resolved, a fresh invitation becomes available automatically. The tunnel remains private: Microsoft service authorization may be required before the phone reaches Loop.

Enter a device name on the phone and select **Request access**. Compare its six-digit code with the pending device on the computer. Select **Approve** only when the codes match and the request is expected; **Decline** rejects it. Approval grants access to all registered projects and chats, prompt attachments and Agent commands under the session's existing permissions, including permission changes and tool approval. It is not a read-only or per-project grant.

The phone receives a standalone pairing page with the device-name form already in HTML. Its small script applies the saved/browser language and theme, removes the invitation fragment from browser history, enables submission and checks existing authorization in parallel. Before removal it saves the unsubmitted invitation only in same-origin, same-tab sessionStorage, with a five-minute limit from capture. Reload restores it without extending that deadline; a fresh scan replaces it. Successful submission or authorization clears it. Storage failure leaves the initial scan usable but disables refresh recovery. Server-side invitation expiry and one-use validation remain authoritative, and this storage never contains approved device credentials. A fresh QR invitation displays the form immediately, without waiting for React, full application translations or the authorization round trip. Ordinary refresh starts with a theme-aware Loop loading screen and keeps the entire pairing card hidden while checking authorization and downloading chats; authorized devices enter chats without a device-name form flash. A browser with no pairing cookie shows “This browser is not paired” and guidance to scan the current QR invitation, without claiming expiry or requiring a QR replacement. A plain tunnel URL in another browser or an incognito window cannot reuse the original browser’s authorization. Expired requests retain expiry guidance, and unavailable checks offer Retry. A pending authorization check cannot replace a pairing request already submitted. Pairing requests display the comparison code and poll for desktop approval; failed requests offer Retry, and rejected or expired requests require a new invitation. Network requests time out after ten seconds.

Only an authorized device downloads the React chat entry and shell, in parallel. Existing authorized devices open chats after the background check; newly approved devices exchange their cookie and recheck authorization first. The React gate consumes that check once from memory, avoiding another blocking round trip while it remains fresh for fifteen seconds; periodic checks and explicit authorization invalidation remain active. Settings loads when opened. Math rendering, its styles and code highlighting load only when message content needs them; ordinary Markdown appears immediately. Opening chats has a loading caption and failed downloads offer Retry. The phone waits without loading projects, conversations or other business data. Approval sets a Secure HttpOnly cookie and opens the existing chat interface. The credential is never returned to JavaScript or saved in browser storage; a separate CSRF value exists only in memory. Requests and invitations disappear on disconnect or backend restart.

**Revoke access** removes a paired device and closes its active requests and streams. The phone returns to pairing when authorization is rechecked, including after an SSE failure, or within the fifteen-second periodic check. Unavailable authorization checks hide the chat UI and offer Retry. Conversation snapshots and query data are cleared on authorization loss; user-written drafts and uncertain-delivery records remain in that browser. Already downloaded content cannot be retracted. Previously accepted Agent work can continue on the computer after revocation.

Device access expires fourteen days after approval and is not renewed automatically. Expired devices remain visible with a red cross and a prompt to pair again. **Remove device** deletes an expired record; the next successful approval also prunes expired records. Removing every device returns Step 4 to its empty marker. Expiry never grants access, and QR invitation renewal does not extend device authorization. Cookies belong to the exact public hostname. Persistent tunnel reconnection and backend restart preserve that hostname, so the same browser can reuse unexpired device authorization. A changed data root or replacement address requires new pairing. Disconnect preserves the cloud tunnel; pending invitations and active streams are still invalidated. Embedded browsers and external browsers have separate cookie stores: opening an already paired page in another browser requires a fresh invitation and desktop approval there. The consumed QR invitation cannot transfer authorization between browsers. Normal top-level page navigation from another app or Microsoft sign-in is accepted; cross-site API requests remain blocked. Settings, project registration, archive/delete operations and provider/MCP/skill configuration remain local and their controls are hidden remotely. See [mobile layout and installed app](pwa.md) for touch controls, home-screen installation, static caching and update prompts.

## Source and Tests

- [Settings component](../components/settings/RemoteAccessSettings.tsx) / [tests](../components/settings/RemoteAccessSettings.test.tsx).
- [Step issue](../components/settings/RemoteAccessIssue.tsx) / [tests](../components/settings/RemoteAccessIssue.test.tsx).
- [Step marker](../components/settings/RemoteAccessMarker.tsx) / [tests](../components/settings/RemoteAccessMarker.test.tsx).
- [Setup progress](../components/settings/RemoteCliProgress.tsx) / [tests](../components/settings/RemoteCliProgress.test.tsx).
- [License info tooltip](../components/settings/RemoteAccessInfo.tsx) / [tests](../components/settings/RemoteAccessInfo.test.tsx).
- [Control hook](../hooks/useRemoteAccess.ts).
- [Backend setup, lifecycle and limits](../../backend/docs/remote-access.md).

- [Remote gate](../components/remote/RemoteAccessGate.tsx) / [tests](../components/remote/RemoteAccessGate.test.tsx).
- [Phone pairing](../components/remote/RemotePairing.tsx) / [tests](../components/remote/RemotePairing.test.tsx).
- [Standalone pairing bootstrap](../remote/remote-bootstrap.ts) / [tests](../remote/remote-bootstrap.test.ts) and [HTML](../remote.html).
- [Desktop devices](../components/settings/RemoteDevicesSettings.tsx) / [tests](../components/settings/RemoteDevicesSettings.test.tsx).

pages.title: Voice Input and Calls
pages.markdown:
# Voice Input and Calls

Loop uses local recognition and speech on the computer running its backend. Voice controls add text to the existing conversation and retain its permission checks, tool results, queue and history. The browser never uses cloud speech recognition or synthesis.

## Usage

Open **Settings → Voice** and follow the three setup steps:

1. **Choose voice features**: select editable voice input or input with local spoken replies.
2. **Install voice components**: use the Download icon button beside the title to install all components. Any missing component keeps this action visible; only a complete installation changes it to the Uninstall icon button. The same row provides cancellation; download progress appears only in each package ring. Four evenly spaced horizontal package markers show waiting circles with package names below and detached separator lines, inner rings filling clockwise from the top with centered percentages for active downloads (a dash when the total is unknown), with a highlight repeatedly tracing the filled arc (static under reduced-motion preferences), green checks for installed packages and a red cross for the failed package; hover or focus the cross to read that package’s error; hovering identifies the package and its state. Hover or focus the info icon beside each package name to inspect that package’s version, sizes and license. Package names stay on one line with ellipsis and show the full name on hover. Loading starts when the command is sent; completion comes from backend resource checks. Errors stay in this step with manual retry, and status refresh recovers background work after a lost command response.
3. **Test voice**: select a microphone and test recognition after the selected resources are ready. A nonempty final transcript marks this step complete; partial speech and voice previews do not. Stopping a successful test retains its completion, while changing microphone or resource readiness resets it. The successful check is saved in this browser for the selected feature profile, microphone and resource versions, so closing Settings or reloading the page retains completion. Changing the profile or microphone, managing components, or observing unavailable or changed resources requires a fresh check.

Management is available only on the host computer; paired phones can select and test components already installed there. Missing published engine assets or unsupported platforms remain unavailable rather than silently falling back to a different speech service. Downloads support cancellation, without a separate pause control.

Component sizes distinguish the download archive, the installed file size required even before installation, and bytes currently installed. Temporary download and extraction space is additional.

Use **Verify and repair** for an installed profile to recheck file hashes and replace damaged downloadable components. A locally imported engine may require another local import when its files are damaged. Updates become available when the installed activation differs from the available catalog.

**Uninstall** also clears managed partial downloads and damaged installations. Resources are stored under the backend's Loop data directory (`~/.loop/voice` by default), never inside the PWA. The current prepared ASR/VAD models require about 167.3 MiB of download; adding bilingual spoken replies adds about 123.8 MiB. The platform engine and temporary installation space are additional, and Settings reports reviewed sizes when published assets are available.

The locally validated macOS ARM64 engine brings the complete profile to about 299.7 MiB of download and 384.5 MiB expanded. These are measurements of prepared local artifacts; published versions may differ.

Choose **Test microphone** to inspect recognition in session-independent test mode without requiring a chat session or sending an Agent prompt. Its separate sampling row hides the capsule until microphone preparation completes and listening begins. Starting disables the microphone button; connecting and finalizing show a spinner around it. During preparation only the microphone spinner is visible. The capsule contains Discard, a waveform derived from live PCM energy that shifts left as samples arrive, and Stop; it has no Send action or visible status caption. A countdown outside the capsule on its right appears at 30S only after recording starts and decreases while sampling; its fixed-width slot remains reserved while its text is hidden before recording, while connecting and after recording ends. Each sample automatically stops 30 seconds after listening first starts; connecting time is excluded and status changes do not reset this limit. Intermediate phrase transcription keeps recording, waveform feedback and Stop available. During recording, the microphone spinner follows local audio energy and stays active through quiet speech and brief pauses using a lower continuation threshold, and clears after 1.2 seconds without detected speech; connection and finalization also retain their spinner. Stop drains queued microphone frames and the last partial PCM frame, then waits for backend transcription completion before showing all collected final phrases. While waiting, the sampling controls remain visible and Stop stays disabled. Completion keeps the collected final text visible in the same row with a Retry action, marking the test complete only when nonempty. Retry clears the previous result and starts a fresh recording and transcription on the same prepared connection, without restarting the microphone or engine. During recording, the leftmost X cancels capture, clears the sample and hides the capsule; Retry appears only beside the completed result. The input row keeps the same height before, during and after recording; long results scroll within the fixed-height text area. Clicking the microphone again also starts a fresh sampling cycle. Retry waits for the previous recognition boundary before clearing buffered phrases so old text cannot enter the new sample. The speech-preview control remains on its own row and is disabled during sampling. **Test speech** plays a short local sample when speech resources are installed, mutes microphone input during playback, then closes the connection and releases capture. A spinner surrounds the preview icon during connection and synthesis. Once connected, the sample text appears to its right; its highlight advances using the actual audio playback clock, approximating position within the text without word timestamps. Preview loading, completion and failures do not change microphone-test state or Step 3 completion. Completed microphone tests retain their prepared connection with capture paused for Retry; disabling the test, leaving Settings or starting speech preview closes it. The controls prevent overlapping use of the shared local engine; preview does not verify recognition. Both require an explicit browser microphone permission and a secure origin.

Select a microphone to use it for the next call. Device names refresh after microphone permission is granted; opening settings alone never requests recording access. The selection is stored in this browser, and an unavailable device falls back to the system default.

Both session entry buttons become available once the required components are ready for the selected profile. Step 3 is an optional microphone and speech test; its verification result does not gate entry. Hovering over a disabled entry points to **Settings → Voice** for details. Loading or failed resource checks also keep entry disabled. An active recording can still be finished, and a call can still be ended.

The composer toolbar sizes voice controls to their contents with a 4px gap between Voice input and Call, an 8px gap before Send and matching button footprints and gives Send and the orb the same footprint without extra horizontal padding. Audio animation stays inside the orb without outward expansion. It places two icon-only voice controls immediately before Send, in this order: **Voice input → Call → Send**.

- **Voice input**, the microphone icon to the left of Call and Send, remains visible whether the draft is empty, typed or transcribed, allowing another recording after Stop. New dictation appends to the existing draft. Draft whitespace is preserved. While recording, sampling controls replace the entire bottom toolbar with the full-width waveform, while an audio-reactive orb occupies the rightmost Send position, leaving the editable draft above in place. The toolbar shows a dense live waveform with smaller dots, Discard, Stop and reserved countdown. Discard and Stop use red icons in Light mode and softer coral-red icons in Dark mode. Interim text stays buffered. Choose Stop or wait for the 60-second limit to end capture; pending transcription continues until the backend confirms that queued audio and the last phrase have finished, then fills the editable draft. Intermediate final phrases do not close the connection. A finalization failure or timeout reports an error instead of inserting an incomplete result. Use the usual Send button afterward. Discard drops this recording and preserves the existing draft and attachments. Manual typing pauses voice input. Attachments and selected Skills remain in the draft.
- **Call**, the waveform icon immediately to the left of Send, replaces the entire bottom toolbar with full-width waveform controls and a Stop button that ends the call; an animated audio-reactive orb appears at the rightmost Send position; the left side contains icon controls for microphone mute, spoken-reply pause and steering the next utterance, with hover titles and pressed states. The lower call panel and duplicate End call button are removed. A paused call uses a Resume icon. Correction is selected by default when starting or resuming a call and turns off after the next submitted utterance. During initial connection, a locally synthesized melody loops until readiness, cancellation or failure; the looping wave animation also covers reconnection. Reconnection after readiness stays silent. Tone nodes disconnect immediately when stopped. The connection melody uses direct Web Audio output, isolated from the speech media stream. The melody starts once microphone audio preparation provides a running audio context; browser audio permissions still apply. The animation respects reduced-motion preferences. The call keeps listening and submits final utterances automatically. The typed draft, attachments and selected Skills stay separate. Ordinary requests use the existing task queue. Choose **Use next utterance to correct direction** to submit the next final utterance as steering at the current tool batch boundary.

Call controls occupy the full composer toolbar before the rightmost orb during a continuous call; there is no separate lower call panel or submission-status text row such as “Sent to Agent”. Both toolbar actions share one voice connection. Switching sessions closes that connection. During a call, microphone mute and spoken-reply pause have independent toggles; the red Stop button ends the call. Task cancellation remains available through explicit voice commands. Speaking stops playback immediately and keeps listening. The explicit phrases `stop task`, `cancel task`, `停止任务`, `停止执行` and `取消任务` cancel the current Agent task. They do not undo completed changes. The screen remains available for messages, code, tool output and approval cards; speech does not approve tool requests.

Say `resume task`, `继续任务`, `恢复任务` or `继续执行` to resume an available stopped task. Say `调整要求：…`, `纠正方向：…` or `correct direction: …` to submit the nonempty remainder as steering. Only final transcripts are interpreted as commands.

Editing an existing queued message pauses automatic sending. It cannot withdraw an utterance that the Agent has already accepted. Unmute after editing to continue the call. New utterances never replace a queue item being edited. Existing request IDs and stream IDs protect voice submissions against uncertain delivery; the ordinary Check and retry action applies if acceptance is unknown.

## Lifecycle and Recovery

Microphone capture and playback start from an explicit click or tap. The browser requests mono audio with echo cancellation and noise suppression, resamples its actual capture rate to 16 kHz PCM, and shows call status independently from Agent task status. Browser audio processing and physical echo performance vary by device.

The browser also finalizes active speech after 1.2 seconds of silence. Finishing voice input waits for the backend to acknowledge completion of queued audio and final transcription before closing. A 65-second deadline reports failure rather than inserting incomplete text. Spoken replies begin at completed sentences in the streaming draft and retain the unfinished tail until completion. Narration plays one segment while synthesizing at most one segment ahead, retaining remaining text in order; user interruption or pausing reading clears that backlog.

Transient socket interruptions reconnect to the same live call with a fresh one-time ticket, retrying transient failures up to five times within 30 seconds. Previous audio and partial utterances are discarded. Completed speech is not replayed, and commands are not automatically resent. If the backend or call lease expires, choose Continue voice to start again; server restarts do not restore queued tasks.

Backgrounding, locking the phone, losing the network or a system microphone interruption pauses the foreground call. Navigating away also closes microphone capture and clears the live transcript; restoring the page from browser history keeps the call paused until Continue voice is chosen. Mute and spoken-reply pause requested during connection also apply when startup finishes. Switching chats ends the previous foreground call; accepted Agent tasks continue in their original session. Hanging up does not stop a task.

## Privacy and Limits

Concurrent status checks share Release discovery rather than returning an unpublished engine while the manifest is still loading. Settings retries unavailable engine discovery every five seconds; the backend bounds remote retry frequency to once per minute. A valid installed activation remains usable when remote discovery fails.

Microphone capture and backend initialization prepare concurrently. Chat dictation and microphone tests request recognition only, so installed TTS files are neither read for integrity verification nor loaded for these calls. Continuous calls and Test speech retain synthesis. Every selected engine/model file still receives full integrity verification before use; each recording creates a fresh engine process. Failed or cancelled microphone preparation closes any backend call already created.

Audio remains in bounded processing buffers and is not saved as a recording. Final text is stored through the usual conversation history and sent to the configured Agent, which may be cloud hosted. A phone sends audio to the computer through its paired connection; the current tunnel service terminates transport TLS, so local inference does not mean audio stays on the phone.

Wake words, continuous background listening and operating-system voice integration are not provided. Mobile microphone permissions, audio-route changes, speaker echo and foreground recovery require real iOS/Android browser and installed-PWA checks. Model and engine availability is reported by the backend; the UI does not imply that release assets have been published.

Both surfaces map microphone RMS levels continuously to waveform height, suppressing levels below 0.002 and reaching the unchanged 28-unit peak at 0.3 RMS instead of 0.05, so ordinary and louder speech remain visually distinct. Both surfaces share recording controls, countdown and the input-session lifecycle for waveform sampling, speech feedback, transcript buffering, finalization and cancellation. Settings hides the waveform capsule, Discard, Stop and countdown until microphone preparation completes and listening begins; only the microphone spinner is shown during preparation. The capsule stays visible during finalization, then persistent completed text and Retry replace it without changing the row height, including for an empty result. Settings accepts final transcripts with a 30-second limit; chat retains editable dictation with a 60-second limit.

## Source and Tests

- [Submit actions](../components/chat/ComposerSubmitActions.tsx), [call entry](../components/chat/VoiceCallButton.tsx), [voice controls](../components/chat/VoiceControls.tsx), [call toolbar](../components/chat/ComposerVoiceCall.tsx), [call actions](../components/chat/VoiceCallActions.tsx) and their colocated tests.
- [Composer integration](../hooks/useVoiceComposer.ts), [submission queue](../hooks/useVoiceSubmission.ts) and their colocated tests.
- [Settings](../components/settings/VoiceSettings.tsx), [profile step](../components/settings/VoiceProfileStep.tsx), [resource step](../components/settings/VoiceResourceStep.tsx), [test step](../components/settings/VoiceTestStep.tsx), [microphone sampler](../components/settings/VoiceInputTest.tsx), [shared sampling controls](../components/voice/VoiceInputSampler.tsx), [composer sampling](../components/chat/ComposerVoiceInput.tsx), [live waveform](../components/voice/VoiceSampleWaveform.tsx), [step layout](../components/settings/VoiceSetupStep.tsx), [resource actions](../components/settings/VoiceResourceActions.tsx), [package progress](../components/settings/VoicePackageProgress.tsx) and their colocated tests.
- [PCM resampling](../voice/pcm-resampler.ts), [PCM utilities](../voice/pcm-utils.ts), [playback](../voice/voice-playback.ts), [narration](../voice/narration-utils.ts), [narration tracking](../voice/voice-narration-tracker.ts) and [socket transport](../voice/socket.ts), each with colocated tests.
- [Backend contract](../../backend/docs/voice.md), [chat input](chat.md), [approvals](permissions.md) and [mobile/PWA](pwa.md).

Component downloads and installation run concurrently. A failed package does not stop other packages; the operation waits for all workers and only activates after every required package and the engine probe succeed. Retry verifies and reuses completed packages. Cancellation stops all downloads and waits for cleanup before allowing another operation. Progress sums bytes across packages.

The feature dropdown shows each profile name with its description underneath inside the option. The closed dropdown shows only the selected name. Arrow keys navigate options, Enter selects and Escape closes.

Microphone and feature choices share the same dropdown option layout, selected checkmark and keyboard navigation.

Stopping installation enters a paused state without an installation error. Download stays disabled and a Resume icon continues retained partial downloads after cleanup.

### Speaker echo handling

Microphone capture requests browser echo cancellation, noise suppression and automatic gain control. Local speech uses a MediaStream-backed audio element rather than direct Web Audio speaker output, allowing the browser media playback path to provide an echo reference. Capture remains active during speech for interruption; no transcript similarity filter drops repeated user words. Playback is started from the initiating gesture, and its tracks and media element are released on cancellation, failure or hangup. Browser support and acoustic conditions still affect cancellation: verify speaker-only playback causes no submissions, then verify user interruption during playback at several speaker volumes. Automated tests cover routing and cleanup, not acoustic effectiveness. No recordings are saved by this change.

Call narration reads assistant text as streaming sentences complete, including intermediate execution messages, in ordered segments of at most 110 UTF-16 code units. Long sentences are split rather than skipped, and queued segments are retained until played or explicitly interrupted. Code blocks and URLs remain omitted. Tool transitions retain brief factual announcements. Connection or reading pauses do not mark unseen updates as already narrated.

pages.title: Approval Requests
pages.markdown:
# Approval Requests

Coding-agent core owns session-scoped approval requests that wait indefinitely by default. A trusted host registers one interaction handler, receives a request, and submits a decision through the session API. The model does not assign approval outcomes or call an approval tool. Ordinary event subscriptions do not count as an available interaction handler.

Managed built-in tools use this lifecycle before operations that need additional authority. An allowed-once decision resumes only the waiting call with its captured arguments and scope, without changing the session preset. Calling requestApproval directly still only returns a decision; it does not schedule or execute a tool.

## Minimal usage

From the repository root, with model configuration available, this example exercises a deterministic host rejection without making a model request or executing a tool:

```typescript
import { createAgentSession, SessionManager } from "@loop/coding-agent";

const { session } = await createAgentSession({
  sessionManager: SessionManager.inMemory(),
  tools: [],
  permissionPreset: "read-only",
});
const detach = session.registerApprovalHandler((request) => {
  // A human-facing adapter can display the request and submit the decision later.
  session.respondToApproval({
    sessionId: request.sessionId,
    requestId: request.requestId,
    decision: "rejected",
  });
});

try {
  const result = await session.requestApproval({
    toolName: "write",
    toolCallId: "example-call",
    reason: "Review the proposed operation",
  });
  console.log(result.outcome);
} finally {
  detach();
  await session.abort();
  session.dispose();
}
```

## API

| API | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `session.requestApproval(input, options?)` | Returns `Promise<ApprovalResult>`. Input requires nonempty `toolName`, `toolCallId`, and `reason`. These identify a proposed operation; they do not prove its arguments or execution scope. |
| `input.operation` | Optional `ApprovalOperation` snapshot. Managed tools supply their validated arguments and the execution scope described below. Host-created metadata is not an execution capability. |
| `options.mcp` | Trusted host-only exact MCP toolKey and catalog lifetime AbortSignal; managed MCP adapters provide this context. Never derive it from model arguments or approval responses. |
| `options.signal` | Optional caller cancellation, combined with the active run's cancellation signal. |
| `options.timeoutMs` | Omitted or null (the value of `DEFAULT_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS`) waits indefinitely. A positive integer up to 2,147,483,647 milliseconds explicitly opts into a timeout for SDK requests. |
| `session.registerApprovalHandler(handler)` | Registers the single host interaction handler and returns an idempotent detach function. A second registration rejects until the first detaches. |
| `ApprovalHandler` | Receives an isolated `ApprovalRequest` snapshot; returns void or a promise of void. Returning from delivery does not approve anything. Submit decisions separately. |
| `session.respondToApproval(response)` | Requires `sessionId`, `requestId`, and `decision`: `allowed-once`, `rejected`, or `allowed-session` for requests advertising `allowSession`. Returns true only for an accepted first decision. |
| `session.state.pendingApprovals` | Fresh snapshots of current requests; an empty array when none remain. The shared state type permits omission; AgentSession supplies an array. |

Eligible MCP requests also advertise `allowSession: true`. Requests have a generated `requestId`, the owning `sessionId`, the input fields, the effective `policy`, and a Unix-millisecond `createdAt` timestamp. `expiresAt` is null by default, or a Unix-millisecond deadline when the caller explicitly supplies a timeout. The result contains the original request snapshot, `outcome`, and `resolvedAt`. Requests without a deadline have no expiry timer. Explicit timeout enforcement uses elapsed monotonic time so delayed timer delivery cannot accept an expired response.
