Undefined content continues existing user history without appending input; empty user history rejects.

| Option | Boundary and contract |
| --- | --- |
| getSteeringMessages(signal) | Return native prompt content arrays before the first request and after each successful response and complete tool batch. |
| getFollowUpMessages(signal) | Return native prompt content arrays only after a successful response without tools and no steering. |
| prepareRequest(signal) | Return systemPrompt, tools and streamFn for the next request and its tools. |
| finishTurn({ message, history }, signal) | Awaited after the complete response and tool batch, before queue polling. History is an isolated snapshot. |

Callbacks are optional lower-layer contracts. Hosts provide queue storage, Skill preparation, save checkpoints and compaction; Agent has no application imports. Callbacks must cooperate with cancellation and avoid consuming inputs before preparation succeeds. A callback failure rejects the run. No polling follows model failures, cancellation or a failed finishTurn. A reached maxTurns budget does not consume another queued input; tool continuations reject, while a naturally finished response returns successfully.

Steering does not cancel streams or skip tools. Tool results precede steering user messages in history and in the next model request. One Agent and cancellation signal remain active until tool continuations, steering and follow-ups are exhausted. Hosts can return one input at a time to preserve per-input configuration and timing. See [message queue](../../../coding-agent/src/docs/message-queue.md).

pages.title: Agent API
pages.markdown:
# Agent API

Use Agent when a host needs a reusable in-memory conversation. The host supplies model configuration, authentication and streaming.

## Create and prompt

This example accepts a configured model and stream function. Calling runExample makes a real request.

```typescript
import { Agent } from "@loop/agent";
import type { AgentOptions, StreamFn } from "@loop/agent";

export const runExample = async (model: AgentOptions["model"], streamFn: StreamFn) => {
  const agent = new Agent({
    model,
    systemPrompt: "You are a helpful assistant.",
    tools: [],
    streamFn,
    maxTurns: 4,
  });
  const answer = await agent.prompt("Hello!");

  for (const part of answer.content) {
    if (part.type === "text") console.log(part.text);
  }
};
```

For a custom URL and streamed output, use the runnable [Agent sample](../agent.sample.ts).

## Options

| Option | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `model` | Required `Model<Api>`. |
| `streamFn` | Required [model stream function](agent-loop.md#model-boundary); there is no default registration. |
| `systemPrompt` | Optional text sent separately from conversation history. |
| `messages` | Optional initial `Message[]`, including user, assistant, and tool results. |
| `tools` | Optional readonly array of [AgentTool](tools.md). Defaults to none. |
| `streamOptions` | `SimpleStreamOptions` without `signal`; Agent owns cancellation. |
| `maxTurns` | Optional positive integer limiting model requests within each prompt. |

## Instance API

| Member | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `prompt(content: PromptContent): Promise<AssistantMessage>` | Runs all model/tool turns and returns the final successful assistant message. |
| `continue(): Promise<AssistantMessage>` | Runs from completed user history without adding another user input. |
| `messages: Message[]` | Isolated snapshot of completed history, including tool calls and results. |
| `isRunning: boolean` | Whether a prompt is currently running. |
| `subscribe(listener): () => void` | Adds an [event listener](events.md); returns unsubscribe. |
| `abort(): void` | Signals cancellation; await the prompt promise to observe completion. |

PromptContent reuses UserMessage content: a string or an array of text/image blocks. Images use base64 data and mimeType. Image-only prompts are supported; an empty input or image input with a text-only model rejects before history changes or model calls. Content is copied before processing.

## History and concurrency

Construction copies initial history. Each accepted non-empty prompt appends one user message; completed assistant and tool messages are appended by the loop. Streaming drafts are not history entries. Changing the returned `messages` array does not change Agent state.

Repeated prompts on the same instance retain history. A new instance starts empty unless `messages` is provided. System prompt and tool declarations are rebuilt for requests and do not accumulate in history.

For persistence, capture `agent.messages` after the run settles and pass that snapshot into a new Agent. The [coding session](../../../coding-agent/src/docs/sessions.md) handles this automatically. Concurrent prompts reject with `Agent is already running`; there is no input queue or runtime model setter. Construct a new Agent to change model configuration.

## Source

[agent.ts](../agent.ts), [types.ts](../types.ts), and [agent.test.ts](../agent.test.ts). See [cancellation and errors](cancellation.md) for rejected prompts and recoverable history.

## Continuation and scheduled inputs

Use continue(): Promise<AssistantMessage> to resume completed user history without appending input. It runs model/tool turns to completion with the same cancellation and pairing guarantees as prompt(). Empty user history and concurrent calls reject. Each invocation uses one cancellation signal and one maxTurns budget across all model requests, including scheduled inputs.

AgentLoopOptions accepts getSteeringMessages and getFollowUpMessages callbacks returning native prompt content arrays. The loop polls steering before its first request and after complete tool batches; ordinary follow-ups are polled only after a successful response without tools. The returned inputs are appended and processed inside the same running Agent. Hosts own queue storage, editing and persistence. See [loop boundaries](agent-loop.md#scheduled-inputs-and-checkpoints).

pages.title: Cancellation and Errors
pages.markdown:
# Cancellation and Errors

A successful `prompt()` returns the final assistant message. Failures reject the promise; Agent always clears its running state in `finally`.

## Cancel a run

Each prompt has an independent `AbortController`. `agent.abort()` signals it and returns immediately. Observe the rejected prompt promise before starting another prompt.

The signal reaches the model runtime and local tools. The loop checks it before each model request and tool execution. Waiting for stream acquisition, iterator events, and the final result is abortable. Tool execution must cooperate with the signal; there is no forced interruption of arbitrary local code.

## Completion rules

| Condition | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `stop` or `toolUse` without calls | Return the final assistant. |
| `stop` or `toolUse` with calls | Execute the batch and continue. |
| `error` or `aborted` | Reject and execute no tools from that response. |
| `length` | Reject as truncated; do not execute potentially incomplete calls. |
| `deferred` or `pending` | Reject as unsupported; no polling. |
| Reached `maxTurns` | Reject before another model request; never silently report success. |
| Tool lookup, validation, or execution failure | Append an error tool result and let the model continue unless cancelled. |
| Unexpected stream or listener exception | Reject and release running state. |

Errors use ordinary `Error` values, including a provider's `errorMessage` where available. There is no exported structured error-code hierarchy; inspect the failure and completed history rather than assuming every failure has a particular string.

## History after failure

Completed messages remain accessible through `agent.messages`. Draft deltas are not appended individually. A provider error/aborted assistant may appear in display history; request normalization filters such messages before the next model request.

When an assistant's batch is interrupted, the loop adds error results for calls not completed, preserving IDs. It does not execute skipped calls or start another model request. Error/aborted assistants are excluded from this pairing because request normalization removes them on replay.

History retention does not undo tool side effects. For durable session snapshots and storage failures, use [coding-agent sessions](../../../coding-agent/src/docs/sessions.md).

## Source

[agent.ts](../agent.ts), [agent-loop.ts](../agent-loop.ts), [cancellable waits](../abortable-promise.ts), [stream cleanup](../stream-model-response.ts), and cancellation cases in [agent.test.ts](../agent.test.ts).

pages.title: Agent Events
Agent Tools
SSE Events
pages.markdown:
# SSE Events

The server pushes session snapshots and coding-agent events to the browser using Server-Sent Events. HTTP commands flow downward, while SSE reports execution state without importing frontend code into lower layers.

## Connections and Frames

Connect to `GET /api/sessions/:id/events`. SSE data is a JSON Frame and its id is `streamId:seq`. Business frames have no custom SSE event field; browsers consume them through onmessage. Named heartbeat events are transport-only and have no business sequence.

| Frame type | Content |
| --- | --- |
| session.snapshot | Complete snapshot on first connection or when replay is unavailable |
| session.state | Complete snapshot after command-state changes and run finalization |
| run.accepted | Accepted requestId and runId |
| loop.event | SDK SessionEvent, runId, and optional messageIndex |

Every frame includes sessionId, streamId, and seq. streamId belongs to one SessionEvents instance. seq increments on publish; a connection snapshot uses the current sequence without incrementing it.

SDK events include message_start, message_update, message_end, tool_execution_start, tool_execution_end, prompt_timing, agent_settled and session_title. Web wraps them in loop.event without renaming them. message_update still carries the original AI event. See [coding-agent events](../../../../coding-agent/src/docs/events.md) for the full contract.

Session-level title, permission_changed, approval_requested and approval_resolved updates publish session.state snapshots, including when no prompt is active. Approval snapshots carry state.pendingApprovals; resolution removes the matching request and records compact lastApproval outcome metadata. Replay can include an earlier pending snapshot followed by its resolution; fresh snapshots contain only currently pending requests. A server restart restores none. Ordinary SSE viewers do not register a handler; /events?approvals=1 explicitly opts into the session's shared interaction adapter. See [permission endpoints](permissions.md) for decisions, indefinite pending waits across reconnects and disconnect cleanup.

## Replay and Snapshots

Clients can supply a cursor through Last-Event-ID or the cursor query parameter; the header takes precedence. If the cursor belongs to the same stream, precedes the current sequence, and the buffer still contains contiguous subsequent frames, replay them in order. Otherwise send a full snapshot, then subscribe to new events.

The default cache holds at most 256 frames and 4 MiB of serialized data, evicting old frames when either limit is exceeded. There is no await between snapshot/replay and live subscription, avoiding lost events at that boundary. State projection replaces drafts and completed messages by messageIndex and merges tool results by call ID.

## Connection Lifecycle

Named heartbeat events with an empty JSON object are sent every 15 seconds without an id or business sequence number. Each connection has a 1 MiB output-buffer target. A client that stops consuming data is disconnected; the frontend reconnects using replay or a snapshot.

SSE responses use text/event-stream with Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform and X-Accel-Buffering: no to discourage intermediary transformation and buffering. The remote ingress replaces the cache policy with no-store, no-transform, retaining the anti-transformation directive and buffering header. Session updates are forwarded as they arrive rather than waiting for model completion; reconnect uses the same replay/snapshot contract. These headers request streaming behavior but cannot guarantee that every external relay or mobile network honors it.

Aborting a request or cancelling its stream removes only that connection's listeners and timer, without cancelling AgentSession. Disposing an instance closes its connections. Server restart creates a new streamId. Replay is not a durable event log, does not recover unsaved execution, and does not re-execute commands.

## List Change Notifications

Connect once per page to `GET /api/workspaces/events` independently of the selected session. SSE data is a JSON ListFrame with streamId and seq, using the same id format and onmessage handling as session events.

| Frame type | Client action |
| --- | --- |
| lists.reset | Refresh projects, cached session lists and archived chats |
| sessions.changed | Refresh the session list for workspaceId and archived chats |
| projects.changed | Refresh projects, the session list for workspaceId and archived chats |

Incremental notifications contain only workspaceId and cursor metadata, without messages or snapshots. They are published after project registration/rename/removal and archive/restore/deletion operations, on accepted runs, first user messages, command-state changes, run settlement, asynchronous title updates and durable read receipts. All loaded controllers are observed, even without a per-session browser connection. Token deltas and tool events do not trigger list refreshes. Operations that partially complete before failing also notify clients so completed changes remain visible.

Each new connection always receives lists.reset at the current sequence, even if Last-Event-ID is supplied. The list stream retains no replay buffer; clients reload lists to recover missed changes. It shares the transport's 15-second named heartbeat, backpressure and disconnect cleanup. Heartbeats do not read history or refresh lists. Controller disposal removes its watcher; registry shutdown closes all list connections.

Notifications cover changes made through this Web process. They do not watch external CLI writes or filesystem edits; reload the page to pick up those changes. This stream synchronizes list queries, not another page's selected session or unsent drafts.

## Source and Tests

- [SessionEvents](../session-events.ts) / [replay tests](../session-events.test.ts).
- [ListEvents](../list-events.ts) / [notification tests](../list-events.test.ts).
- [SSE response](../http/sse.ts) / [cursor and cancellation tests](../http/sse.test.ts).
- [SessionController](../session-controller.ts) / [tests](../session-controller.test.ts).
- [Shared protocol](../../shared/protocol.ts), [state projection](../../shared/session-projection.ts) / [tests](../../shared/session-projection.test.ts).
- See [frontend streaming state](../../frontend/docs/events.md) for the consumer.

pages.title: HTTP Boundaries
pages.markdown:
# HTTP Boundaries

The desktop Web API serves a local single-user interface. Browser and API share an origin. Routes validate request origin and input before calling the SDK. Feature endpoints are documented under [projects](projects.md), [sessions](sessions.md), [providers](providers.md), and [SSE](events.md).

## Local Request Validation

The request URL host must be localhost, 127.0.0.1, or `[::1]`. If a Host header is present, it must match the URL host. A supplied Origin must exactly match the current origin, and Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site is rejected. Failures return invalid_host or invalid_origin (403).

The service listens only on 127.0.0.1. These checks are neither login authentication nor a tool sandbox; local programs can still access the service. There is no cross-origin CORS access or multi-user isolation. A separate authenticated tunnel ingress uses the [remote device policy](remote-devices.md); it does not bypass these desktop checks.

## JSON Input

Write endpoints using readBody require Content-Type starting with application/json and a streamed request body no larger than 1 MiB. JSON must be a non-null object. Arrays and invalid JSON return invalid_body (400); oversized input returns body_too_large (413), and an incorrect media type returns json_required (415).

requiredString checks for nonempty text while preserving the original string, including prompt whitespace. Model configuration has additional field-length and URL validation. Session routes resolve IDs through the registry instead of accepting arbitrary session file paths.

## Error Responses

Errors use this shape. The frontend translates code and displays message for unknown errors:

```json
{
  "code": "session_busy",
  "message": "session_busy"
}
```

| Condition | Status and code |
| --- | --- |
| Invalid input | 400 with the relevant field/configuration code |
| Missing project or session | 404, project_not_found / session_not_found |
| Busy session or pending save | 409, session_busy / pending_save |
| Project removal or provider configuration conflict | 409, project_busy / provider_busy |
| Same request ID with different text | 409, request_conflict |
| Server shutdown | 503, server_closing |
| Unexpected exception | 500, operation_failed; message retains the exception description |

Unmatched routes return 404 with not_found. Some matched features return 405 for unsupported methods; do not assume every path handles invalid methods identically.

Normal routed responses set Cache-Control: no-store; errorResponse constructs exception responses separately. Error details can include SDK or filesystem information for local display, not a public log or telemetry interface. Provider configuration endpoints return only redacted views.

## Source and Tests

- [router](../router.ts) / [tests](../router.test.ts).
- [local-request](../http/local-request.ts) / [origin validation tests](../http/local-request.test.ts).
- [input](../http/input.ts) / [input-limit tests](../http/input.test.ts).
- [errors](../http/errors.ts) / [error contract tests](../http/errors.test.ts).

pages.title: MCP settings endpoints
pages.markdown:
# MCP settings endpoints

The Web server owns one coding-agent McpManager, supplies it to session factories and closes it at shutdown. Startup does not await MCP loading/discovery. Routes remain available while a server is connecting; config writes wait only for local persistence.

| Route | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| GET /api/settings/mcp | Redacted servers, status, toolCount and safe error code |
| POST /api/settings/mcp | Create a server; duplicate IDs return 409 |
| PUT /api/settings/mcp/:id | Replace config; body ID must match an existing server |
| PATCH /api/settings/mcp/:id/enabled | Persist `{ enabled: boolean }` |
| POST /api/settings/mcp/:id/retry | Restart enabled server discovery |
| DELETE /api/settings/mcp/:id | Remove config and stop its connection |

Successful commands return `{ servers: McpServerView[] }` immediately after local persistence; they do not wait for discovery. POST/PUT saves allow a transient 120-second STDIO setup attempt, while HTTP, startup, enable and Retry retain normal deadlines. Status polling reports the result independently. All endpoints use the router's local host/origin checks and no-store responses. Unknown IDs return 404, invalid configs 400, duplicate IDs 409, storage errors 500. Failure messages contain stable codes, not raw server errors or secret values. Server snapshots distinguish queued, connecting, refreshing, ready, disabled and error; error rows include a safe connection/discovery failure code.

Configuration is global for the Web backend, shared across projects. It is stored through core in `<agentDir>/mcp.json`, independently of model/provider files and chat histories. Mutations do not take the session/model configuration lock. Connection configuration changes and disabling a server revoke its catalog lifetime, session grants and pending approvals/calls; display-name-only changes preserve that lifetime. MCP authorization uses live session permissions and temporary exact tool/session grants. Configuration contains no separate approval defaults or tool overrides; legacy permission fields are ignored and omitted on the next write. Ready tool snapshots are selected at each prompt; discovery never restarts a user's prompt.

See the public [core contracts](../../../../coding-agent/src/docs/mcp.md) for transport fields, write-only values, background limits, tool approvals and error behavior. The browser workflow is documented in [Integrations](../../frontend/docs/integrations.md).

Source: [routes](../routes/mcp.ts), [route tests](../routes/mcp.test.ts), [server](../server.ts), [session bridge](../loop.ts).

pages.title: Permission Endpoints
pages.markdown:
# Permission Endpoints

Each SessionController owns an approval adapter and consumes the public coding-agent session APIs. The browser submits explicit decisions; it never receives an execution permit.

## HTTP contract

| Endpoint | Body or behavior |
| --- | --- |
| GET /api/settings/general | Return the effective default as permissionPreset. |
| PUT /api/settings/general | JSON permissionPreset: read-only, workspace-write or danger-full-access. Persist and return the default for future Web sessions. |
| PUT /api/sessions/:id/permission | JSON preset: read-only, workspace-write or danger-full-access. Persist before changing authority; return the session snapshot. |
| GET /api/sessions/:id/events?approvals=1 | Opt into an interactive approval connection; optional cursor follows normal SSE rules. |
| POST /api/sessions/:id/approvals/:requestId | JSON decision: allowed-once, rejected, or allowed-session for eligible MCP requests. Return the snapshot only when core accepts the decision. |

Example bodies:

```json
{ "preset": "workspace-write" }
```

```json
{ "decision": "allowed-once" }
```

Invalid preset/decision values return 400 with invalid_permission_preset or invalid_approval_decision. Busy or pending-save sessions reject permission changes with 409; pending approvals also block other commands. Decisions bypass the command lock so a paused tool can resume. Stale, duplicate, expired, wrong-session or disconnected decisions return 409 approval_not_pending. Unknown sessions return 404.

These routes share the existing [local HTTP checks](http.md): loopback Host, matching Origin when supplied, cross-site request rejection and JSON input validation. There is no account authentication or per-tab ownership; request IDs are correlation identifiers, not secrets. Same-origin interactive pages may answer the same session's requests, with first settlement winning.

## New-session default

Settings → General stores the permission default in `<agentDir>/web-ui/settings.json`, shared across projects and browser pages using this server data directory. GET and PUT use the same shape:

```json
{ "permissionPreset": "workspace-write" }
```

PUT rejects missing or invalid presets and extra fields with 400 invalid_permission_preset. Writes are serialized and atomically replace the file with mode 0600; success is returned only after persistence. A failed write does not change the previous saved default. This endpoint does not invoke a model or modify any session. There is no separate approval tool: the frontend confirms Full access before submitting PUT.

Each newly created Web session reads the default and passes it to the managed session factory. If the Web settings file is absent, the SDK settings default applies, with Read only as the built-in fallback. Invalid or unreadable Web settings report an error and prevent new-session creation instead of silently substituting permissions. Existing and restored sessions retain their own presets without reading this Web default. Existing drafts also retain the preset selected at creation. CLI and SDK defaults are unaffected. Concurrent server processes do not coordinate writes; the last atomic replacement wins.

## Handler lifecycle

Ordinary event connections and internal observers remain read-only viewers. The first explicitly interactive connection registers one handler with the session. Subsequent connections share it. Core requested/resolved events publish session.state with pendingApprovals. lastApproval records only outcome, resolution time and session/request/tool identifiers for outcome display.

After the last interactive connection disconnects, retain the handler and existing pending requests for the lifetime of the session. There is no disconnect-expiry timer. Built-in tool approvals have no deadline; custom SDK requests may explicitly opt into a timeout. New requests with no connected client fail immediately. Reconnection reuses the handler and restores pending snapshots. Responses require at least one live interactive connection. Heartbeat/backpressure or cancelled SSE connections remove only the client subscription; explicit run abort or controller disposal settles the request.

Disconnecting does not stop the model run. Closing the controller aborts the run and pending requests, releases the handler and closes event connections. A restart restores persisted session permissions but no pending approvals, outcome metadata or reusable grants.

## Scope and limits

File approval authorizes one exact replacement, with core path/content/identity rechecks. Shell approval authorizes one unsandboxed invocation and descendants with host filesystem, network and environment access. Neither changes the stored preset. There is no command-text risk classifier or automatic retry. Built-in approvals are one-call only. MCP uses session permissions and memory-only exact tool grants; allowed-session is rejected unless the pending request advertises allowSession. Full access automatically allows MCP calls; restricted presets require approval or a tool/session grant. Disabled servers and service authentication/refusal remain enforced. See [core approvals](../../../../coding-agent/src/docs/approvals.md) for enforcement.

## Source and validation

[Session adapter](../session-approvals.ts) / [tests](../session-approvals.test.ts), [routes](../routes/sessions.ts) / [HTTP/tool integration test](../routes/sessions.test.ts), and [controller](../session-controller.ts). Tests cover connection opt-in, multiple tabs, long disconnects, reconnect, explicit SDK expiry, abort, stale/wrong-session responses, local request rejection, persisted presets and a managed write that waits for approval.

[General settings routes](../routes/settings.ts) / [tests](../routes/settings.test.ts) and [Web settings storage](../settings/web-settings.ts) / [tests](../settings/web-settings.test.ts) cover validation, fallback, atomic persistence, failure recovery, new sessions across projects, and restoration without changing existing authority.

pages.title: Projects and Directories
pages.markdown:
# Projects and Directories

Project registration maps a local directory to a workspaceId so the browser can create and restore sessions. Removing registration does not delete the directory or SDK conversation history.

## Project API

| Endpoint | Input and result |
| --- | --- |
| GET /api/workspaces | Return id, name, cwd, and accessible |
| POST /api/workspaces | Accept path and optional name; return the registered project |
| PATCH /api/workspaces/:id | Accept name and update the display name |
| DELETE /api/workspaces/:id | Remove registration; return 204 on success |
| POST /api/workspaces/:id/archive | Accept ids (session ID array) and archived (boolean); archive or restore the selection; return 204 |
| DELETE /api/workspaces/:id/archive | Accept ids; permanently delete only the selected archived chats; return 204 |
| DELETE /api/workspaces/:id/sessions/:sessionId | Permanently delete one chat belonging to the project, archived or unarchived; return 204 |

path must be an absolute directory. Registration resolves it with realpath and checks read/traversal permissions. The same directory or a symlink to it reuses the existing project. The default display name comes from the directory name. Listings retain unavailable directories with accessible set to false.

## Persistence and Concurrency

ProjectStore saves the project array to `<agentDir>/web-ui/projects.json`. Writes are serialized within the process, using a temporary sibling file and atomic replacement. Invalid content reports an error rather than being overwritten with an empty list.

SessionRegistry guards removal. Pending loading/creation, an active session, or unsaved history returns project_busy (409). New session operations are blocked during removal. Success disposes instances and clears sessionId-to-workspaceId mappings. Registering the same directory again exposes its existing SDK sessions.

Archive and restore use the same project exclusion guard. Every ID must belong to the project; an unknown ID returns session_not_found (404) without changing the archive. The request contains the exact IDs shown in the confirmation, so newly created chats are not silently included. GET /api/sessions?workspaceId=… returns unarchived chats with user messages, including live first runs; add archived=true to list archived chats, including older empty archives. Drafts without user messages are excluded from project archive selections. Direct session reads still work for archived IDs. Archived chats retain their history, titles, attachments and IDs; no model call is made by archiving or restoring.

The public coding-agent [SessionArchive](../../../../coding-agent/src/docs/session-archive.md) stores membership beside project history. It is independent of project registration, so removing and re-adding a directory retains archive membership. The Web bridge reuses one archive writer per canonical history directory. Invalid metadata or write failures reject without replacing history or partially archiving a batch.

Archive deletion uses the same busy-project guard. It rejects missing, foreign or unarchived IDs with session_not_archived (409) before deleting any selected history. Title work is drained first; selected cached controllers are disposed and their trace writers drained before deleting history and corresponding trace segments, payloads and manifests. Active trace writers in another instance or process reject deletion. Closed controllers are evicted even on failure so surviving history can be reloaded for a retry. Project files and unselected history/traces remain. Archive and restore preserve traces. Web submits each confirmed project's exact selection separately; an error stops later projects, refreshes lists, and leaves already completed projects deleted. See the SDK archive page for staging, rollback and crash limitations.

## Directory Selection API

Single-chat deletion uses the same lifecycle guard and staging operation as archive deletion, with no prerequisite archive step. Missing or foreign IDs return session_not_found (404). The endpoint never accepts a history file path and never deletes project files. Successful deletion drains title writes and disposes any loaded controller before releasing the project guard. Confirmation is owned by the Web UI.

| Endpoint | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| POST /api/directories/pick | Return the system-selected path, or null on cancellation |

Selection opens a system folder picker on non-SSH macOS environments, with one window at a time. Request cancellation reaches the picker process; user cancellation returns null without registering a project. Unavailable pickers return native_unavailable (409); picker execution failures return native_unavailable (500). No directory capability or browsing endpoint remains. The picker only selects a folder; POST /api/workspaces registers it with an optional custom name after validation.

## Boundaries

Folder selection accesses the server's local filesystem; it is not file upload or remote file management. A registered directory supplies the working directory and the managed session's workspace-write boundary; the [core permission policy](../../../../coding-agent/src/docs/permissions.md) enforces file and Bash restrictions. Folder selection itself remains a host operation. Session APIs accept project/session IDs, not arbitrary session file paths. Storage has no cross-process write lock; CLI and Web should not write the same session simultaneously.

## Source and Tests

- [Project routes](../routes/projects.ts) / [HTTP tests](../router.test.ts).
- [ProjectStore](../projects/project-store.ts) / [tests](../projects/project-store.test.ts).
- [SessionRegistry](../session-registry.ts) / [removal and load-race tests](../session-registry.test.ts).
- [Native picker](../directories/native-picker.ts) / [tests](../directories/native-picker.test.ts).

pages.title: Provider Configuration
pages.markdown:
# Provider Configuration

The backend stores multiple built-in and custom model providers and connects them through coding-agent's public createProviderRuntime. The model runtime handles model requests, authentication protocols, streaming events and parsing. Web implements configuration and optional catalog discovery, not model generation transports.

## HTTP API

| Route | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| GET /api/settings/providers | Redacted providers and the built-in API-key catalog |
| POST /api/settings/providers | Create; duplicate IDs return provider_exists (409) |
| PUT /api/settings/providers/:id | Edit; the body ID must match and already exist |
| DELETE /api/settings/providers/:id | Remove configuration and stored key; preserve conversations |
| POST /api/settings/providers/discover | Fetch models for an unsaved custom provider draft |
| GET /api/models | Saved providers' models with provider IDs, providerName display labels, model IDs, names and supported efforts; empty before configuration |

Create/update/delete return the redacted collection. Input uses id, kind (builtin/custom), name, baseUrl, api, authentication, optional apiKey, and models. Models contain id and optional name, contextWindow and maxTokens. Custom model fields are limited to those listed above; image attachments and effort selection belong in the composer. Built-ins retain trusted catalog capabilities; custom gateways allow image content and standard effort choices without prerequisite configuration. See [form constraints](../../frontend/docs/models.md). Built-in endpoint/protocol/models are resolved from the trusted model catalog rather than accepted from request input. Custom models are limited to 500 unique IDs, with positive integer capacities no greater than 100 million; output tokens cannot exceed context.

The public record has hasApiKey instead of apiKey. Custom providers may have an empty models array; they contribute no chat models and keep their credentials for later edits.

The model menu never falls back to the full model catalog. Only saved providers contribute entries, and Web model selection rejects models outside that list. Provider display names come from saved configuration; built-ins use their canonical catalog names. Provider IDs remain the identity for grouping and requests, even if two providers share a display name. A custom entry may use a built-in ID such as openai; kind determines whether catalog endpoint/protocol defaults apply. The custom entry retains its supplied target, protocol, authentication and selected model subset. IDs remain unique, and changing an existing entry's kind is rejected.

## Storage

The file is <agentDir>/web-ui/provider.json, normally under ~/.loop; LOOP_DATA_DIR changes the root. The file uses version 2 with a providers array. Unsupported versions are rejected without modifying the file. An absent file or an empty collection exposes no models.

Writes use a synced temporary file with mode 0600 followed by atomic rename. Keys are local plaintext, not encrypted in the system keychain. API responses and browser storage never contain saved keys. Invalid JSON, unsupported versions, duplicate IDs or invalid entries fail closed with provider_config_invalid; content is never included in the error.

Omitting apiKey preserves it only for the same normalized URL and protocol. A changed target requires a fresh key. No authentication deletes stored credentials and supplies the model runtime with the non-sensitive local-placeholder key; gateways must tolerate its authentication header. Keys never fall through from other configured providers.

The separate provider.json.selection file contains only the last Web-selected provider/model and optional effort. Invalid or removed selections fall back to the first configured model for new sessions. This Web preference does not change coding-agent settings.json or CLI defaults.

## Discovery

Discovery first checks the draft Provider ID against the built-in catalog. An exact match returns all its model IDs, names and capacities locally, without querying the supplied Base URL or resolving credentials. For other IDs, discovery supports the three custom protocols. It requests GET <baseUrl>/models, with Anthropic's /v1 and x-api-key/anthropic-version headers as needed; OpenAI protocols use bearer authentication. savedId may reuse a stored key only for the same URL and protocol. A supplied key is transient and never persisted by discovery.

Endpoint responses accept a data array or models map, limited to 2 MiB and 500 IDs. Valid contextWindow/context_window and maxTokens/max_tokens/max_output_tokens values are retained; invalid capacities are omitted. Requests time out after 10 seconds and do not follow redirects. Errors return provider_discovery_failed without echoing upstream bodies or credentials. The frontend merges all returned models into the editable draft, keeping existing per-model edits; persistence still requires Save. Local catalog entries do not claim gateway availability. Manual IDs work independently of discovery. This operation reads the model catalog; it does not call generation endpoints.

## Session Lifecycle

Custom runtime construction resolves the exact provider/model ID's catalog thinking-level mapping. The model API and session validation therefore allow xhigh/max only when supported and retain catalog exclusions for other levels. The map is runtime metadata rather than a new persisted provider field, and configured endpoints, protocols and credentials are unchanged. Unknown identities keep the standard effort defaults.

A stable runtime facade resolves the latest configuration for every preflight and request. Only configured models can run. Configure a provider in Settings → Models before creating a session. Built-in models retain their individual protocols, endpoints and metadata.

New sessions select a valid remembered Web model or the first configured model. Existing sessions retain their selection. Web opts into createAgentSession's allowUnavailableModel restoration mode so removed models do not prevent reading history; prompt preflight still rejects until a configured model is explicitly selected. Re-adding the same identity also permits continuation.

SessionRegistry.configure rejects mutations during execution, loading, switching, pending saves or project removal with provider_busy (409), and blocks new operations until the mutation finishes. There is no mid-request connection switch or automatic abort/retry. Discovery neither mutates configuration nor changes sessions.

## Limits

No OAuth, account login, keychain integration, automatic connection test, external-file watching or host-editor opener. API-key catalog providers that need additional platform configuration are excluded. Saved configuration is read on initialization and after application mutations; restart after manual file edits. Provider settings apply to Web only.

## Source and Tests

- [Routes](../routes/providers.ts) / [tests](../routes/providers.test.ts).
- [Validation](../providers/validate-provider-config.ts) / [tests](../providers/validate-provider-config.test.ts).
- [ProviderStore](../providers/provider-store.ts) / [tests](../providers/provider-store.test.ts).
- [ProviderSettings](../providers/provider-settings.ts) / [tests](../providers/provider-settings.test.ts).
- [Discovery](../providers/discover-models.ts) / [tests](../providers/discover-models.test.ts).
- [History and defaults](../loop.test.ts), [SDK models](../../../../coding-agent/src/docs/models.md).

pages.title: Private Tunnel Connection
pages.markdown:
# Private Tunnel Connection

Loop manages the official Dev Tunnels CLI to sign in to Microsoft and host a private tunnel. A separate loopback ingress serves the built application to explicitly paired devices after the service’s own access checks. Unpaired devices can open the pairing page but cannot access business APIs. See [device pairing and remote authorization](remote-devices.md).

## Setup and Usage

Start Loop normally, then open **Settings → Remote access**:

1. Select **Install Dev Tunnels CLI** in the first step. Loop downloads and verifies the official tool if needed. No terminal commands, Microsoft application registration, Client ID or scopes are required.
2. Select **Sign in** in the second step and complete Microsoft sign-in in the computer's system browser. Personal Microsoft accounts, including Outlook accounts, use the official CLI's Microsoft login; organizational policies and service consent can still apply.
3. Select **Connect Tunnel** in the third step. The completed third step and Disconnect Tunnel action indicate connection; the settings screen hides the HTTPS address and redundant connected caption. Step 4 automatically shows a QR invitation after connection. Its URL uses this tunnel origin plus a one-use pairing fragment.
4. The download cancel icon cancels installation; **Disconnect Tunnel** stops hosting through the existing stop command. The tunnel step shows one plug button, disabled while connecting or disconnecting, without a separate cancellation icon. Sign-in has no stop icon and settles on success, failure or timeout. Closing the settings tab does not stop the Web process.

Completed steps show green checks; incomplete steps show empty circles, with actions unlocked in order. The heading's info button shows the license terms and privacy statement on hover, focus or click. The local API still supports automatic installation before login or connection. With an installed CLI, login starts in signing-in and an already authorized connection starts in connecting, including during executable verification. Only a missing or invalid executable returns these operations to installing for a verified replacement. **Sign out** in the sign-in step is available while connected as well as after hosting stops. It first finishes tunnel shutdown in the stopping phase without changing signedIn or its persisted marker. Only then does it enter signing-out, clear the marker and invoke CLI logout. Shutdown failure is assigned to Step 3 and preserves sign-in without invoking logout; account-stage failure is assigned to Step 2. The CLI account store is shared with other uses of Dev Tunnels under the same OS user: logout can affect those uses too. It does not sign the Microsoft browser session out or revoke consent.

After a successful connection, Loop saves a reconnect preference and rehosts the saved persistent tunnel asynchronously on the next backend launch. Startup reports connecting until CLI readiness; it never restores a connected phase or an old address from disk. Every entry into Remote access checks the installed executable and returns the persisted sign-in result and current host state. It never invokes CLI account commands or reads the credential store. Checking never downloads, signs in or starts/stops hosting; a missing or invalid executable clears the local remembered sign-in. Concurrent entry checks share one probe; during an active operation they return its current state without running competing CLI commands. Installation checks validate only the executable file. Startup restores the last successful Loop sign-in from `<agentDir>/web-ui/remote-access/sign-in.json`. This version-1 file contains only `version` and `signedIn`, with no account identifiers or tokens. Writes are serialized and use a synced mode-0600 temporary file followed by atomic replacement. Missing, unreadable, invalid or unsupported-version files start unconfirmed. Start reuses a remembered login without calling login or user show again; when unconfirmed, it signs in through the CLI, which may reuse its own credentials. No old host process or connected status is reused; the saved tunnel identity and port are reused after CLI readiness. Independent Web processes do not coordinate these state files; the last atomic replacement wins.

## Development Restarts

`pnpm dev` runs a stable gateway and a separate business worker. The gateway owns Vite, the desktop listener, Tunnel lifecycle, pairing requests, device cookies and CSRF state. Backend, shared protocol and core TypeScript edits restart only the worker after a short debounce; frontend edits use HMR locally and automatically rebuild the remote production frontend. The build watcher starts with pnpm dev, serializes builds, retains the last successful build on failure, and stops with the development command. Changes to gateway or Tunnel implementation require manually restarting the development command.

During worker startup or restart, remote document requests receive an uncached HTTP 503 recovery page that retries after two seconds. Business requests receive `backend_restarting` with Retry-After; writes are never queued or replayed. Existing SSE connections close and the browser reconnects using the normal snapshot/replay contract. Browser reloads and disconnects cancel upstream response streams without logging expected cancellation as a server error; SSE streams also end quietly when their worker is replaced, allowing browser reconnection. Unexpected upstream failures and incomplete non-SSE responses still fail instead of appearing successful. Running model calls are interrupted by worker restart; saved history is recovered, not resumed generation. The gateway forwards business calls only to its loopback worker using an ephemeral IPC-provided capability; remote Host, Origin, device and CSRF checks run before forwarding.

Stopping the entire development command still stops the Tunnel. Production startup and direct `web --dev` retain their existing single-process lifecycle. This does not bypass Microsoft's sign-in or fix failures on an external authentication page.

## Installation and Credentials

Loop pins CLI version `1.0.2115+e16833f284`, its official HTTPS artifact URL and SHA-256 digest per supported platform. Automatic installation supports macOS and Linux x64/ARM64, and Windows x64. Other targets report an unsupported-platform error. Platform runtime and credential-store requirements are those of the official CLI.

The executable is saved below the data root at `bin/devtunnel/<version>/devtunnel` (`devtunnel.exe` on Windows), defaulting to `~/.loop/bin/devtunnel/<version>/devtunnel`. Setting `LOOP_DATA_DIR` relocates this directory with the rest of Loop's data. Downloads use a private temporary file, a 100 MiB limit, a cumulative ten-minute active-transfer deadline that excludes paused time, digest verification and atomic rename. Every use checks the installed digest; invalid content is replaced through a verified download. Loop neither modifies PATH nor installs a system package. It does not reuse arbitrary executables from PATH or accept executable paths, commands or download URLs through the API. Updating the pinned release requires a Loop update.

Uninstall deletes only the current pinned executable from the managed directory, without invoking the CLI, logging out, reading Keychain credentials or changing system installations. Missing files count as already removed. Unexpected directories are not recursively deleted. Starting uninstall clears and persists the remembered sign-in before removing the executable; a failed removal leaves installation confirmed but sign-in unconfirmed. Successful removal resets installed and signedIn; CLI credentials remain available for later explicit sign-in. Removal errors report cli_uninstall_failed. Uninstall is rejected during a check, download, sign-in, stopping or hosting.

After the transfer completes, `download.stage` becomes `verifying` while the controller remains `installing` and `installed` stays false. Pause and Resume are unavailable during full-file digest verification, flush, permission setup and atomic placement. Only successful installation sets `installed` to true and clears `download`; verification failure or cancellation removes the temporary file without completing the step.

During downloading, Pause aborts the current request while retaining the private temporary file. Requests pin Azure Storage API version `2023-11-03` to obtain standard ETags and conditional range handling. Resume uses HTTP Range and If-Range when a validator is available; a full response truncates the partial file and restarts from zero. Invalid or inconsistent range responses fail closed. The complete file must still pass the pinned SHA-256 check before installation. Stop, graceful shutdown or failure removes the incomplete file; Stop never deletes an already installed executable. Paused downloads remain in the current Web process and are not restored after a restart.

The CLI owns browser authorization and credential storage. On macOS, explicit login, logout and hosting can request access to the system login keychain. Automatic refresh never runs user show; it retains the persisted sign-in result and clears it when the executable is absent or invalid. Reauthorization and sign-out clear the remembered result before invoking account commands. Login completion is shown only after its successful result is saved; failed state writes report sign_in_state_failed in the responsible step. Failed reauthorization or cancellation before CLI success leaves the marker false. Stop, shutdown and ordinary tunnel failures preserve it. This marker does not verify credentials: external CLI logout, credential-store edits, expiration or service revocation may make it stale. No background credential probes run; reauthorization after an actual authorization failure requires explicit Sign out and Sign in. Loop does not automate approval or modify Keychain access permissions. Failed frontend status checks stop automatic polling and require manual Retry. Account operations are never retried automatically; they report failure on CLI exit or their deadline. A Keychain Deny response is managed inside the CLI and cannot be observed directly by Loop; sign-in settles on CLI exit or its deadline. The control API still accepts Stop to cancel an operation, but the sign-in step does not expose a stop icon. Loop does not use MSAL, send Microsoft tokens to frontend code, scrape login output for tokens, or maintain a separate credential cache. Raw CLI diagnostics are not returned to the UI or written to Loop logs. Cancel terminates the child process, with forced termination after two seconds if needed. Browser windows already opened by the CLI can remain open.

Browser sign-in has a three-minute deadline; account commands have a thirty-second deadline and initial hosting readiness has a sixty-second deadline. A failed operation reports a fixed error code and can be retried. Unexpected host exit clears the address and closes the isolated ingress. Hosting status reflects CLI readiness; temporary network interruptions inside a running CLI are not independently detected by Loop.

## Tunnel Lifecycle

The reconnect preference is stored at `<agentDir>/web-ui/remote-access/connection.json` as version 1 with only an enabled boolean. It uses the same serialized, synced mode-0600 temporary writes and atomic replacement as sign-in storage; it contains no tunnel IDs, URLs, account details or credentials. A successful Connect saves enabled=true before reporting connected. A missing, unreadable, malformed or unsupported-version record defaults to false. Existing connections from before this feature need one successful Connect to create the preference.

At startup, an enabled preference verifies the installed CLI and remembered sign-in before launching one fresh host using the CLI credential store. Restore never downloads the CLI or invokes login automatically; missing prerequisites clear the preference and leave hosting off. Host startup may still request OS credential-store approval. Failure is reported in the responsible step without a retry loop or a false connected state; the enabled preference remains for a later backend launch. A normal shutdown or unexpected host exit preserves the preference. Explicit Disconnect, sign-out, reauthorization, uninstall and detection of a missing or invalid executable clear it. Stop waits for an in-flight connection save before clearing, so a late completion cannot re-enable the preference. Disconnect still closes the host if saving fails, but reports connection_state_failed in Step 3 and does not proceed to CLI logout; retry after fixing storage permissions to clear the stale preference.

The first Connect saves a generated tunnel name and randomly assigned loopback ingress port, creates a private persistent tunnel with a thirty-day inactivity expiration, and configures its single HTTP port. It saves the canonical CLI tunnel ID before completing port setup. Every later Connect binds that same local port, verifies that the tunnel has exactly that HTTP port, and hosts the saved ID. An occupied port, missing tunnel or unexpected port configuration reports failure instead of changing the address. Port setup uses separate port commands; hosting an existing tunnel never batch-updates ports. It passes --host-header unchanged and --origin-header unchanged so relay requests retain the public Host and Origin required by the pairing ingress checks; the CLI defaults would rewrite both to localhost. Restart the Web backend and reconnect an existing tunnel to apply updated hosting arguments. It never enables anonymous access. The first verified HTTPS origin is saved and later connections must report the same origin. Access policy and transport are managed by the official CLI and service.

Stop first closes the ingress, invalidates pending pairing and terminates remote request/stream access, then shuts down the host process. Disconnect, sign-out, uninstall and ordinary shutdown preserve the persistent cloud resource and saved identity. The address remains stable across reconnection and backend restart with the same data root and authorized CLI account. The service can expire a tunnel after thirty days without activity; activity renews this sliding window. External deletion or expiry causes connection failure and does not silently create a replacement. CLI output is parsed only for the pinned version's readiness marker and port-specific HTTPS address; inspect URLs are not presented as connection addresses.

The strict version-1 file at <agentDir>/web-ui/remote-access/tunnel.json stores the tunnel ID, local port, setup-completion flag and optional verified HTTPS origin; it contains no access tokens or account details. Writes are serialized, synced and atomically replaced using mode-0600 temporary files. Missing state starts initial provisioning; malformed or unreadable state fails closed. Setup resumes with the saved name/ID after interruption, and never uses the CLI global last-used tunnel. One Loop process must own this data root and port. Existing temporary connections migrate to a new stable address on their next Connect; phone browsers need one new pairing on that address. The former SDK environment variables and MSAL cache are no longer read. Existing local records are left untouched; this change does not erase previously stored credentials or cloud resources.

## Local Control API

| Request | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/remote-access` | Returns sanitized status and sets a process-lifetime HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict local control cookie |
| `POST /api/remote-access` | Accepts exactly one action field: install, uninstall, login, start, stop, logout, pause or resume; requires the cookie and exact same-origin Origin |

Example request body:

```json
{ "action": "start" }
```

POST returns HTTP 202 with the accepted state. Status includes `supported`, `installed`, `signedIn`, `phase`, optional `download` (`received` and optional `total` bytes, optional `paused` boolean and optional `stage` (`downloading` or `verifying`; omission means downloading)), `url`, optional `failedSteps` (`install`, `login`, `start`), sanitized `error` and optional `errorStep` (`install`, `login`, `start`). `errorStep` identifies the stage where an operation failed, including generic CLI errors and failures during automatic prerequisites; it is cleared when another command starts or an operation is intentionally stopped. The frontend uses it to display errors within the responsible setup step. signedIn records the last successfully persisted Loop login, restored on startup; it is not an independent credential-store or service-authorization probe.

The optional `failedSteps` list records previously completed steps that later fail: an absent or invalid installed executable, failed reauthorization, or unexpected exit of a connected host. Successful recovery clears only the affected failure. Intentional stop clears the connection failure, sign-out clears the login failure, and successful uninstall clears all step failures. This metadata lasts only for the current process and never requires automatic credential probes. A failed refresh request returns HTTP 503; failure to clear a missing executable’s remembered login can leave its in-memory login unconfirmed, the frontend marks its cached completed steps as failed checks until a successful retry.

Phases are `off`, `installing`, `uninstalling`, `signing-in`, `signing-out`, `connecting`, `connected`, `stopping` and `error`. Stop can cancel an active action, including paused downloads. Pause and resume are accepted only while the download transfer is active, and retain the installing phase with download.paused indicating the state. Other overlapping or inapplicable commands return 409. Malformed commands return 400, invalid origin/cookie returns 403 and unsupported methods return 405. The API accepts no CLI options or arbitrary URLs. It trusts local processes as the rest of Loop does; the cookie is not a multi-user authentication system.

Entry uses GET with the query parameter **refresh=1** to verify installation before returning the remembered sign-in and current host state. Ordinary GET reads only memory. Both responses disable HTTP caching and set the local control cookie. Refresh preserves a running host and its address, including when a probe fails. Stop and shutdown cancel a pending check; other actions return 409 until it completes. A failed probe or state-clear write returns HTTP 503 with the fixed code **remote_status_failed**, without CLI diagnostics. The frontend offers Retry; rechecking has no installation or authorization side effects, but clears the remembered sign-in when the executable is missing.

Errors distinguish unsupported platforms, download/storage failure, integrity failure, CLI operation failure, sign-in failure/timeout, sign-in-state storage failure, connection-preference storage failure and tunnel failure. Changing account requires an explicit action; application launch reconnects only when a previously successful connection left the preference enabled. After CLI readiness, Loop confirms cloud hostConnections for at least two seconds after the new process is at least four seconds old, with a forty-five-second verification deadline and eight-second probe timeouts. Connected hosts are checked every thirty seconds, including when timers resume after system sleep. A failed control API probe alone never tears down a working host. Two consecutive disconnected samples or an unexpected host exit trigger recovery using the same persisted tunnel identity and port. Recovery shows the connecting phase, closes stale ingress and hosting, and retries at one, two, four, eight, sixteen and thirty seconds. Each attempt must pass cloud verification. A minute of observed healthy hosting resets the retry budget. Six unsuccessful attempts report a sanitized tunnel failure for manual retry and retain the startup preference. Explicit Disconnect, Sign out and process shutdown abort probes and retry delays; recovery never installs the CLI or opens account sign-in.

## Limits

Remote access uses the [device-pairing policy](remote-devices.md) and existing chat UI. Phone layout and PWA behavior are described in [mobile layout and PWA](../../frontend/docs/pwa.md); background delivery is not implemented. In development mode, remote ingress serves the last production frontend build; wait for the initial automatic frontend build before testing remote access. The Web build stages Vite output before publishing, replaces each entry atomically after its resources exist and publishes the service worker last. Failed builds keep the prior frontend active. Node builds preserve dist/web; old hashed resources remain available for open tabs. Use pnpm --filter @loop/web-ui build:frontend for frontend-only updates. Direct vite build bypasses staged publication. Old hashed assets are retained until the build output is explicitly cleaned while the server is stopped. Disconnected ingress returns 503. Automated tests use synthetic subprocess and service responses; they do not establish real account authorization, China connectivity or cross-platform execution.

Microsoft's managed service is in preview without a production SLA. Browser HTTPS ingress terminates TLS at the service; Loop does not promise encryption that hides traffic from the relay. The CLI is a separate downloaded executable, not an npm package or a self-hostable Microsoft relay. See [CLI installation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/developer/dev-tunnels/get-started), [service security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/developer/dev-tunnels/security), [license terms](https://aka.ms/devtunnels/tos) and [privacy statement](https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement).

## Source and Tests

- [Reconnect preference storage](../remote-access/connection-store.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/connection-store.test.ts).
- [Startup restore](../remote-access/create-remote-access.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/create-remote-access.test.ts).
- [Sign-in marker storage](../remote-access/sign-in-store.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/sign-in-store.test.ts).
- [Setup operation](../remote-access/setup-operation.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/setup-operation.test.ts).
- [Controller](../remote-access/controller.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/controller.test.ts).
- [Download transfer](../remote-access/cli-download.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/cli-download.test.ts).
- [Pinned releases](../remote-access/cli-release.ts) and [installer](../remote-access/cli-installer.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/cli-installer.test.ts).
- [CLI processes](../remote-access/cli-process.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/cli-process.test.ts).
- [Runtime](../remote-access/cli-runtime.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/cli-runtime.test.ts).
- [Tunnel recovery](../remote-access/tunnel-recovery.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/tunnel-recovery.test.ts).
- [Hosting](../remote-access/cli-tunnel.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/cli-tunnel.test.ts).
- [Persistent tunnel setup](../remote-access/persistent-tunnel.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/persistent-tunnel.test.ts).
- [Tunnel identity storage](../remote-access/tunnel-store.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/tunnel-store.test.ts).
- [Closed ingress](../remote-access/closed-ingress.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/closed-ingress.test.ts).
- [Local routes](../routes/remote-access.ts) / [tests](../routes/remote-access.test.ts).
- [Frontend workflow](../../frontend/docs/remote-access.md).

pages.title: Remote Device Pairing
pages.markdown:
# Remote Device Pairing

The Web server opens a separate random loopback ingress for the managed private tunnel. The desktop listener retains its local request checks. Remote ingress authenticates every business request before calling the same HTTP/SSE router; it never delegates tunnel controls to the remote router.

## Usage and Trust

Connect through [Remote access](remote-access.md), use the invitation automatically generated in Step 4 after connection, scan it on the phone, request access and compare the six-digit confirmation codes before approving on the computer. Microsoft service authorization still applies because the tunnel does not enable anonymous access. No Microsoft credentials are exposed to frontend code.

Approval grants the device the computer owner's chat access across registered projects, with prompt files/images, model and permission selection, queue controls, tool approvals and Agent commands. Existing core permission enforcement remains in force; the device can change a session's permission preset as the desktop can. Pair only trusted devices. No per-project, read-only or separate remote-user roles exist.

## Local API

All routes below use the desktop listener. GET status sets the process-lifetime local control cookie; mutations require that cookie and an exact local Origin. The outer local router also rejects nonlocal Host/Origin and cross-site requests.

| Request | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/remote-access/devices` | Connection state and ephemeral connectionId, nonexpired device metadata in devices, expired metadata in expiredDevices and pending requests with comparison codes |
| `POST /api/remote-access/pairing` | Fresh `{url, expiresAt}` invitation; replaces the unused invitation |
| `POST /api/remote-access/pairing/:id` | Exactly `{approve: boolean}`; approve or decline a pending request |
| `DELETE /api/remote-access/devices/:id` | Persist revocation, then terminate that device's tracked access |

The random connectionId identifies one ingress lifetime without exposing the public URL or granting access. It is stable during status polling, changes on every reconnect and is absent while disconnected; the desktop uses it to discard stale QR results and generate a fresh code.

Invitations require an active tunnel, expire after five minutes and are consumed by one successful request. Both invitations and device credentials use independent 256-bit random secrets. Invitation URLs carry the secret in the fragment, omitted from HTTP request targets; the frontend removes it from history immediately. Unsubmitted invitations are temporarily retained in same-tab sessionStorage for at most five minutes from capture, without extending their server deadline; successful submission or authorization clears them. This permits refresh before requesting access without saving approved device credentials in JavaScript storage. The six-digit code is for human comparison, not authentication. A maximum of sixteen pending requests bounds memory. Rejected, expired and already-decided requests cannot be approved.

## Remote API and Policy

| Request | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/remote-session` | Remote authorization state; authorized devices receive sanitized metadata and a process-bound CSRF value |
| `POST /api/remote-pairing` | Exactly `{token, name}`; consumes an invitation, returns a comparison code and sets the pairing cookie |
| `GET /api/remote-pairing` | Unpaired/pending/rejected/expired state; an approved request exchanges the pairing cookie for the device cookie |

With no valid pairing cookie, the polling route returns `unpaired`, meaning this browser has no resumable pairing request. It does not assert that an invitation expired. A well-formed pairing credential with no remaining request returns `expired`; pending requests still resume across page refreshes. A bare tunnel URL in a new browser or incognito session shows unpaired guidance and requires scanning the current unused QR invitation before requesting approval.

Both cookies use the `__Host-` prefix, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict and Path=/. Pairing cookies expire after five minutes. Device cookies and records expire after fourteen days without automatic renewal. Duplicate or malformed credential cookies are rejected. No raw device credential is returned in JSON. The CSRF value is derived from a process-random key and the credential; a backend restart changes it.

Remote writes require the configured public HTTPS Origin and `X-Loop-CSRF`; foreign Origin or cross-site fetch metadata is rejected even for reads. The only cross-site exception is GET/HEAD top-level document navigation to /, /index.html or /remote.html, identified by Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate and Sec-Fetch-Dest: document. This permits browser handoffs and sign-in redirects to open the public pairing page; it never exempts APIs, embedded frames, static subresources or writes, and a foreign Origin remains rejected. The ingress accepts only its bound loopback Host or the exact public host. Loop starts the CLI with --host-header unchanged and --origin-header unchanged so the relay preserves the phone’s public Host and Origin instead of rewriting them to localhost. The default rewrites would fail the Host check on page load and the Origin check on pairing requests. Forwarded and X-Forwarded-Host headers never grant authority. Existing host processes must reconnect after this change to use the new arguments. Browser credentials remain scoped to the public hostname and browser cookie store; reconnecting with a new hostname or switching from an embedded browser to another browser requires pairing again with a fresh invitation. Used invitations cannot be transferred to another browser. Persistent tunnel hosting keeps the same origin and port across reconnects and backend restarts, allowing the same browser to reuse its unexpired device cookie; a new authorization check obtains the new process CSRF value. Migration from an older temporary tunnel requires pairing once at the new address.

The allowlist serves project/session/model lists, session snapshots and SSE, new sessions in existing projects, prompts and attachments, queue/resume/abort/flush/compact, model/title/permission changes, read/pin state and tool approvals. It permits reading the installed skill catalog for the existing composer. Provider credentials, settings administration, MCP/skill installation, directory picking, project registration/removal and archive/delete endpoints are unavailable remotely. New endpoints remain denied until explicitly added. Static application assets and pairing routes are public; the frontend gate mounts business hooks only after authorization.

Responses disable caching; SSE additionally retains no-transform and X-Accel-Buffering: no so intermediaries are instructed to avoid transforming or buffering streamed chat updates. Successful responses also suppress referrers, MIME sniffing and framing. Errors use fixed codes without raw backend/CLI diagnostics. Authentication failures return 401, policy/Origin/CSRF failures 403, missing local devices 404, stale decisions/disconnected invitation requests 409, connection/pairing limits 429, unavailable ingress or failed storage 503. Other remote errors use a generic 500 code.

## Storage and Lifecycle

`<agentDir>/web-ui/remote-access/devices.json` is a strict version-1 file holding only device IDs, names, creation/expiry timestamps and SHA-256 credential hashes. Missing storage starts empty; malformed, unreadable or unsupported storage fails server startup closed. Serialized mutations write a synced private mode-0600 temporary file and atomically replace the record. No raw credentials, pairing tokens, addresses or Microsoft tokens are persisted there. Independent Web processes do not coordinate writes; use one owner process.

Approval becomes effective only after storage succeeds. A desktop approval already being saved remains durable if the tunnel disconnects during that write; it remains visible for later revocation, although its old pairing request is invalidated. Failed approval writes cannot grant access. Revocation persists first; a failed write reports failure and leaves the grant active for explicit retry. Expired records are excluded from authorization and the active devices list. Desktop status exposes their sanitized metadata separately in expiredDevices so Settings can show a red cross and offer removal, including after restart. They are pruned on the next successful approval or removed explicitly through the device DELETE route. Expired metadata never includes credential hashes and cannot authorize requests.

Requests and streams are bound to device expiry, revocation, tunnel disconnect and client cancellation. At most sixteen simultaneous business responses are allowed per device. Closing a stream cancels its source reader, unsubscribes existing SSE listeners and clears heartbeat timers. An in-flight request whose response arrives after invalidation cannot return that business response. Disconnect closes ingress before stopping the host process; the persistent cloud tunnel is retained. Pairing state is memory-only and resets on disconnect/restart. Already accepted commands may continue on the computer; revocation cannot undo actions or retract previously downloaded data.

## Limits and Validation

The private relay still requires service access and terminates browser TLS; it does not provide encryption that hides traffic from Microsoft. Remote ingress serves built frontend assets even when the local listener uses Vite development middleware. It maps / and /index.html to the separate remote.html pairing entry, whose HTML already contains the device-name form; its small bootstrap shows that form immediately for a fresh QR invitation, keeps pairing hidden during ordinary-refresh authorization checks and chat downloads, and imports the chat application only after authorization. Authorized devices refresh directly into chats through a theme-aware loading screen; failed or unauthorized checks expose only pairing recovery or Retry. The local entry keeps index.html. Both entries must be included in custom asset directories.

With pnpm dev, ingress uses the Web package’s dist/web directory; production keeps the packaged web directory, and an explicit assetsDir overrides the default. The remote entry never serves Vite source modules or HMR. Run `pnpm build` before remote testing and rebuild after frontend changes; pnpm dev alone does not build the remote page. The Web build publishes only successful staged frontend builds, replacing entries after assets are available and preserving old hashed resources for open pages; failed builds keep the previous frontend. Frontend-only changes can use pnpm --filter @loop/web-ui build:frontend. A missing build returns 404 at the remote root even though the local Vite page works. See [mobile layout and PWA](../../frontend/docs/pwa.md) for installation and static caching. Foreground/network stream recovery is implemented; background delivery remains unsupported. Transient authorization-check failures preserve loaded chats, while explicit denial clears access. See the mobile/PWA verification steps for real-device checks.

Static JavaScript, CSS and JSON responses of at least 1 KiB use gzip when explicitly accepted with a nonzero quality value, with Vary: Accept-Encoding; clients without gzip receive the original bytes. HTML remains uncompressed for remote bootstrap injection, and API/SSE responses do not use this static-file compression path. Remote responses remain no-store. Authorization starts parallel chat entry/shell downloads, while settings, math and code-highlighting assets remain optional.

Automated tests use synthetic origins, temporary private stores, injected CLI results and model streams. The business integration test reads successive model deltas over the real loopback HTTP ingress before generation completes, checks the projected phone draft, and reconnects mid-generation before receiving further live updates. It also checks the SSE anti-transformation headers. These checks do not establish real Microsoft sign-in, phone-browser compatibility or relay connectivity.

- [Ingress](../remote-access/remote-ingress.ts) / [security and SSE tests](../remote-access/remote-ingress.test.ts).
- [Existing business integration test](../remote-access/remote-business.test.ts).
- [Devices](../remote-access/remote-devices.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/remote-devices.test.ts).
- [Storage](../remote-access/device-store.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/device-store.test.ts).
- [Pairing requests](../remote-access/pairing-requests.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/pairing-requests.test.ts).
- [Local control routes](../remote-access/local-device-routes.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/local-device-routes.test.ts).
- [Allowlist](../remote-access/remote-policy.ts) / [tests](../remote-access/remote-policy.test.ts).
- [Frontend workflow](../../frontend/docs/remote-access.md).

pages.title: Server Startup
pages.markdown:
# Server Startup

One Node HTTP service provides the React page and same-origin API, listening only on the IPv4 loopback address `127.0.0.1`. Vite middleware provides frontend development assets and HMR on the same HTTP server. Production reads prebuilt assets.

`GET /api/sessions/:id/images?path=...` serves local PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP images explicitly referenced by Markdown in that session's assistant messages or streaming draft. Relative paths resolve against the project. Canonical files must remain within the project, the system temporary directory or `/tmp` on POSIX; outside symlink targets, non-regular files, unsupported signatures and files larger than 32 MiB return a sanitized 404. HEAD returns the same metadata without a body. Responses disable caching and MIME sniffing. Remote ingress requires a valid paired-device credential before invoking this route.

`GET /api/sessions/:id/files?path=...` downloads regular files up to 512 MiB explicitly linked in assistant Markdown history or the current draft. It uses the same project/temporary-directory boundaries and remote device authentication. User messages alone do not authorize access. Missing, outside-root and oversized files return `404 file_not_found`. Files stream from disk without buffering the full body; HEAD returns metadata only. Single byte ranges return 206 and Content-Range; invalid or multiple ranges return 416.

Downloads use `application/octet-stream` and attachment disposition with a UTF-8 filename. Add `preview=1` for inline MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, OGG/OGA, FLAC, MP4, WebM, MOV, OGV or PDF; unsupported extensions still download. PDF previews require a PDF header. All responses disable caching and MIME sniffing and apply restrictive content policies; PDF responses allow the native viewer without the HTML sandbox directive. Media decoding and PDF rendering depend on the browser; no conversion or transcoding is provided.

## Start

Run these commands from the project root:

```bash
pnpm dev
pnpm dev --port 3081 --no-open
node --conditions=loop-source --import tsx packages/web-ui/src/main.ts --help
```

| Argument | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| --port | Defaults to 3080; accepts 0–65535, with 0 requesting an available system-assigned port |
| --no-open | Start the service without automatically opening a browser |
| --help, -h | Print usage without loading the frontend or starting a server |
