Unknown arguments and invalid ports report errors. SSH environments do not open a browser automatically. An occupied port causes a startup error instead of silently selecting another port.

## Readiness and Development Updates

startServer asynchronously creates project storage, provider settings, a session registry and routes, then waits for the listening socket. The Fetch API router is adapted through @hono/node-server so SSE remains streamed and response cancellation propagates. Production pages come from the build directory; development mounts Vite middleware. Icons are built without inline data URLs, with conventional favicon and Apple touch aliases. Static responses reject traversal, symlinks resolving outside the asset directory and non-GET/HEAD methods; confinement uses the operating system's path separator, including on Windows. Startup consumes the homepage before printing its URL and opening the browser.

Safari can retain icons from a previous application hosted at the same address, separately from ordinary page caching. A correct icon response does not prove that an existing Safari tab or bookmark has refreshed. After changing icon routes, restart the service and reload the page. Use a private window to compare before clearing browser data; clearing website storage can also remove local drafts and preferences. Existing pinned tabs or bookmarks may retain their own icon until recreated.

Development mode enables Vite React/CSS HMR. The pnpm dev command runs a stable gateway with a separate business worker. Backend, shared and core source edits restart the worker while the gateway retains its local listener, Tunnel and device authorization. Frontend changes use local HMR and rebuild remote assets. Worker replacement interrupts active requests and generation; browsers recover using their event cursors. See [development remote access](remote-access.md#development-restarts).

Saving model settings uses the running API and requires no restart. This differs from updating backend source. See [provider configuration](providers.md).

Frontend configuration errors do not shut down the API, session registry or remote ingress. If Vite cannot initialize, development serves the last built frontend from the Web build directory. Without that build, the homepage returns a small unavailable page with HTTP 503 and automatic refresh. Frontend requests retry Vite initialization at most once every two seconds; API and SSE requests bypass these attempts. Fix the configuration, then refresh to return to Vite. Terminal output retains the underlying error. Production still requires a working built homepage before announcing readiness.

The backend watcher excludes frontend source and package-level TypeScript build configuration, including Vite configuration and its PWA plugin. Vite manages its own configuration reloads, keeping the backend and sessions alive. Restart `pnpm dev` once after changing the watcher command itself. Backend/core source updates still restart the process and interrupt active requests; this development setup is not process-crash recovery.

## Shutdown and Storage

main handles SIGINT/SIGTERM by rejecting new session operations, waiting for registered loading/configuration work, cancelling sessions, attempting pending saves, and closing subscriptions and the server. Failed shutdown saves report an error and set a failing exit code. Closing the server is not proof that data was saved.

The data root comes from coding-agent's getAgentDir, defaults to `~/.loop`, and can be set with `LOOP_DATA_DIR`. Project and provider configuration live in its web-ui subdirectory; sessions use the SDK's existing sessions directory. Closing the browser does not shut down the service.

## Limits

This is a local single-user service with no public listening, login system or background daemon. The root distribution includes production assets and the web command. Publishing to npm requires separate authorization and package ownership.

## Source and Tests

- [server.ts](../server.ts), [main.ts](../../main.ts) / [startup tests](../../main.test.ts).
- [Development watcher regression](../../../dev.test.ts) covers backend restarts, frontend exclusions, Codemode calls and shutdown.
- [Development frontend](../http/development-frontend.ts) / [tests](../http/development-frontend.test.ts) cover failed configuration, static fallback, streaming continuity and recovery.
- [Argument parsing](../startup/arguments.ts) / [tests](../startup/arguments.test.ts).
- [Browser opening](../startup/open-browser.ts) / [tests](../startup/open-browser.test.ts).
- [Session registry](../session-registry.ts) / [tests](../session-registry.test.ts).

## Paged session history

GET /api/sessions/:id and session event snapshots include the latest three user rounds and history metadata (start, total, userStart). Message and timing indexes in events remain absolute. GET /api/sessions/:id/history?before=<message-index>&streamId=<stream-id> returns up to three preceding rounds with start, end, total, userStart and messages. Invalid boundaries return 400 invalid_history_cursor; a replaced server stream returns 409 history_changed. Authenticated remote devices may read this endpoint under the existing device and origin policy. The route pages the live controller history so pending saves and active messages remain consistent; core SessionManager.readHistory separately supports indexed disk reads. Pagination does not replay commands or reduce the model's context.

pages.title: Session Commands
pages.markdown:
# Session Commands

`POST /api/sessions/:id/compact` holds the existing idle command lock, publishes operation `compact` with `compactionStartedAt` (epoch milliseconds), invokes `session.compact()` and returns the settled snapshot. The start is stable across live snapshot fetches and SSE reconnects and clears when the operation settles; it is not stored in session history. Short contexts return HTTP 400 with `nothing_to_compact` without authentication, model calls or storage writes; they settle with idle outcome and no session or command error, leaving the initiating UI responsible for a transient notice. `/abort` cancels generation. Pending saves and approvals block compaction. Persisted checkpoints survive reopening; snapshots contain only lightweight `state.compaction` metadata for the latest checkpoint, including the history count used to position the completed marker. See [core compaction](../../../../coding-agent/src/docs/compaction.md).

Each sessionId has one writable AgentSession in the current Web process. Web manages commands and event connections; the coding-agent SDK owns model loops, tools, and JSONL history storage.

Session lists include only the supported storage format. Files with other formats or versions remain untouched and do not block listing, opening supported conversations or creating new sessions. Looking up an excluded session returns session_not_found (404). Malformed current-format files and storage failures still report errors.

## API

| Endpoint | Input and result |
| --- | --- |
| GET /api/sessions?workspaceId=… | Return unarchived conversations containing user messages, including live first runs, without session file paths |
| POST /api/sessions | Accept a registered workspaceId or explicit null for an independent chat; return a draft snapshot with 201, without writing a history file |
| GET /api/sessions/:id | Open or retrieve a session and return its complete snapshot |
| POST /api/sessions/:id/prompt | Accept requestId, text and optional images/files; return runId with 202 |
| POST /api/sessions/:id/abort | Wait for cancellation and cleanup, then return a snapshot |
| POST /api/sessions/:id/flush | Retry saving existing results and return a snapshot |
| POST /api/sessions/:id/compact | Summarize older context and return the settled snapshot; originals remain saved |
| PUT /api/sessions/:id/model | Accept provider and id; return a snapshot after switching |
| PUT /api/sessions/:id/title | Accept nonempty title; normalize, save and pin it against automatic generation |
| POST /api/sessions/:id/title | Regenerate from saved user text; return the snapshot on completion |
| PUT /api/sessions/:id/permission | Persist a supported session preset while idle |
| PUT /api/sessions/:id/read | Accept workspaceId and a nonnegative safe-integer messageCount; clear header unread only when the viewed count matches nonempty saved history and return { read: boolean } |
| PUT /api/sessions/:id/pin | Accept workspaceId and boolean pinned; persist header pinnedAt and return { pinnedAt: string or null } |
| POST /api/sessions/:id/approvals/:requestId | Answer with allowed-once, rejected, or allowed-session for eligible MCP requests |

A complete snapshot contains model identity, supported efforts, selected effort, SDK state, operation, tool projection, optional runId/requestId and compact lastApproval outcome metadata. operation is idle, prompt, compact, model, flush, title or permission; it does not indicate whether model text has started arriving.

Session list summaries include userMessageCount and isGenerating, derived from saved history and the current Web process's live session state. Drafts with no user messages are omitted from the default list. Unloaded historical sessions return isGenerating: false. The first completed user-message event publishes a sessions.changed notification on the [list stream](events.md#list-change-notifications), so the sidebar item appears while the response is still streaming, even on pages viewing another session. Archived listings continue to include older empty archived records for management.

Web enables first-prompt title generation through coding-agent. List summaries include optional title text; snapshots expose title source and optional titleError in SDK state. Background title events publish session.state without changing the operation or opening a run. Explicit title commands share the command lock. Provider reconfiguration and project removal cancel and drain auxiliary work before changing its runtime or disposing sessions. See [session titles](../../../../coding-agent/src/docs/session-titles.md).

## Creation and Restoration

Session summaries expose optional pinnedAt from the saved header, including the current manager's accepted metadata for loaded sessions. PUT /api/sessions/:id/pin validates project membership and boolean pinned, shares the session's write queue, and makes no generation call. It remains available during a prompt or approval wait without changing that operation. true preserves an existing timestamp; false removes it. The endpoint returns 400 for invalid input, 404 for unknown projects/sessions or a mismatched owner, 405 for other methods, and enforces the same local-origin request checks as other mutations. Project removal, deletion, server shutdown and provider reconfiguration are coordinated by the existing project operation guard. Persistence errors leave accepted metadata intact and return an error. Success publishes sessions.changed so every browser page refreshes its summaries; list reconnects resynchronize from headers. Archive and project removal preserve session files and their pins; deletion removes both. There is no browser-state import, fallback or separate pin file.

List summaries include isWaitingForApproval, derived from the live session’s pending requests. Saved history and sessions without pending requests report false; pending approvals are not restored after server restart. Approval request and resolution events refresh background lists through session.state notifications.

List summaries and session state expose unread from the session header. New completed output sets it to true in the same history commit; reading the latest output sets it to false. Empty drafts start false, and missing fields default to false. No separate read-receipt file or browser storage is used.

PUT /api/sessions/:id/read checks membership in the supplied project or independent scope and uses its shared session instance without making a model call. SessionManager.markRead compares the viewed messageCount with the current saved history inside the session's write queue. A mismatched count or empty history returns { read: false } without clearing unread; a matching count returns { read: true } after persistence, including duplicate receipts. Negative or noninteger counts return 400; missing sessions return 404; pending history saves must be flushed before marking read. Read writes atomically replace the existing JSONL snapshot, preserving messages, activity timestamps and other metadata. Concurrent history saves retain newer unread output. Successful reads publish session.state and sessions.changed for the active conversation and background lists. Failed writes retain unread and the frontend retries while completed content remains visible. Archived and unloaded lists read the same header, and server restarts restore it. Independent server processes do not coordinate writes or notifications.

New Web sessions use SessionManager.draft: a stable in-process ID and target history path, with model/title changes kept in memory until a commit contains a user message. Attachment-only user messages qualify. Invalid submissions or model preflight failures leave the draft unlisted. The normal end-of-run commit persists the first history, including cancellation or model errors after the user message was added; failed saves remain recoverable through flush. Unsent draft handles can be reopened within the server process, but do not survive a server restart. The API does not automatically delete older empty history files.

LoopBridge lists a project's sessions through the public SDK, then opens SessionManager from the matching record. Unknown session IDs or history outside registered projects and the independent collection are rejected. Browsers cannot supply arbitrary file paths. Concurrent loads of one sessionId share a Promise and instance.

New sessions use the valid remembered Web model/effort or first configured model; a provider must be configured before creating a session. Restored sessions retain saved model identity and effort. Missing models do not block reading history, but prompts require a configured model. Changing Web defaults does not update existing sessions. See [provider configuration](providers.md).

## Submission and Mutual Exclusion

Managed SDK sessions expose state.permissionPreset in snapshots. New Web sessions use the default saved in Settings → General → Permission, falling back to the SDK settings default when no Web override exists (built-in Read only). Changing this default leaves existing sessions and drafts unchanged. Restored sessions retain their preset, independently of the new-session default. Permission changes publish a complete session.state frame outside any prompt run. The Web picker and approval cards use [permission endpoints](permissions.md); permission changes share the idle command lock, while approval responses can unblock a running tool. File/Bash denials appear as ordinary tool errors; see [core permissions](../../../../coding-agent/src/docs/permissions.md).

1. Validate text or attachments and a requestId of at most 128 characters.
2. Synchronously reserve command state, record requestId/runId, and publish run.accepted.
3. Call session.prompt immediately and track its Promise; return 202 without waiting for the full answer.
4. Forward message, tool, and agent_settled events, then publish session.state on completion.

Model and flush operations require idle state. Prompt submissions during generation or a pause use the core queue; no second model loop runs concurrently. hasPendingSave blocks new prompts and model changes; only flush can retry saving. Different sessions have separate controllers, while provider updates also use a global exclusion guard.

The controller deduplicates up to 256 recent request IDs. The same ID and prompt content return the original runId without executing again; the same ID with different text, images or file names/contents returns request_conflict. This cache is in memory, so restart or eviction removes the exactly-once protection.

## Cancellation, Failure, and Disposal

Browser prompt requests include the observed streamId. When supplied, it must match the current controller stream after asynchronous skill preparation and immediately before prompt acceptance; a mismatch returns 409 delivery_unknown without executing. Older clients may omit the field. This closes the restart window between a browser status check and submission, without adding durable request deduplication.

abort is independent of ordinary command locking and can stop an accepted request. It waits for SDK cancellation and the active operation. Disconnecting SSE does not call abort. Lower layers handle model/tool cancellation through signals; completed side effects cannot be undone.

SDK save failures retain hasPendingSave. flush neither requests the model nor executes tools again, and another save failure leaves recoverable state intact. Preflight or unexpected errors also settle to idle with error details, preventing the UI from remaining permanently busy.

Closing a tab does not dispose its session. Instances remain until project removal, confirmed session deletion or server shutdown. DELETE /api/workspaces/:id/sessions/:sessionId removes one archived or unarchived chat through the project's busy guard, without loading a model or archiving first. There is no automatic idle eviction, branching, or cross-process write coordination. See [project deletion routes](projects.md) and [coding-agent sessions](../../../../coding-agent/src/docs/sessions.md) for history and save-failure semantics.

## Image Attachments

POST /api/sessions/:id/prompt accepts text and optional images (native image blocks containing type, data and mimeType). Text may be empty when images are present. Up to four PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF images totaling 3 MiB decoded are accepted. Prompt JSON bodies have no application-imposed byte limit, while other routes retain 1 MiB. Malformed/oversized image payloads reject before starting an operation. Known text-only models return model_images_unsupported.

The request identity includes text and image content; retrying the same requestId with changed images returns request_conflict. Only a content digest is retained in the bounded deduplication map. The model API receives the native image blocks, and session history retains them for reload and later turns.

## Text File Attachments

POST /api/sessions/:id/prompt also accepts an optional files array of objects with name and text strings. Text may be empty when files are present. Up to four UTF-8 text/code files are accepted without a per-file or combined text byte limit. The prompt route reads JSON with an unlimited byte budget, and the Node HTTP adapter does not impose a separate attachment limit. Other JSON routes retain their bounded reads.

The server validates filenames, supported text/code extensions (or extensionless names), text controls, Unicode and file count before accepting a run. Paths in filenames, binary contents and unsupported formats reject with invalid_text_files. The browser additionally decodes source bytes with strict UTF-8 validation. See [the shared contract](../../shared/prompt-files.ts).

Each file becomes a native text block containing a reference-content label and a JSON object with its name and exact decoded text. This representation is persisted by the existing SDK history and rendered as expandable file cards by Web. It works with text-only models and needs no new Agent message type, parsing dependency or provider-specific file API. Original files are not written to the project.

After HTTP acceptance, coding-agent checks the complete [context budget](../../../../coding-agent/src/docs/context-budget.md), including file text, project instructions, runtime context and tool schemas. An over-budget request settles with an error before main model dispatch, while retaining the complete user message and attachments in history and attempting the ordinary save. The accepted request ID still deduplicates, including after budget rejection; Web receives context_budget followed by the settled error state. Requests that fit reach the provider without file truncation and can still fail against its actual limits. Full files and request bodies remain in memory, so browser/server resources and provider capacity constrain practical sizes. This path does not implement separate file storage, on-demand retrieval or automatic compaction.

## Model and Effort Updates

PUT /api/sessions/:id/model accepts provider, id and optional effort. Values are default, off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh or max; non-default values must be supported by the selected model. Invalid levels return invalid_model_effort (400). Omitted effort preserves the existing level when supported, otherwise Default. Updates run through the existing model command lock and return/publish the complete snapshot; they never call generation. Session metadata and the new-session Web preference are saved before success is returned.

## Source and Tests

- [SDK bridge](../loop.ts) / [tests](../loop.test.ts).
- [Session routes](../routes/sessions.ts), [shared snapshot types](../../shared/protocol.ts).
- [SessionRegistry](../session-registry.ts) / [tests](../session-registry.test.ts).
- [Unread header storage](../../../../coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts) / [persistence tests](../../../../coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.test.ts) / [HTTP tests](../routes/sessions.test.ts).
- [SessionController](../session-controller.ts) / [streaming, cancellation, and save tests](../session-controller.test.ts).

## Queue and Resume Routes

POST /api/sessions/:id/queue accepts id and action: edit (text and optional images/files/skills), move (optional beforeId; omit for end), delete, steer, begin-edit or cancel-edit. begin-edit marks the item as held in state.queue; the scheduler skips it until edit or cancel-edit releases it. begin-edit returns the held item with its full content and Skills for the main composer. The hold survives reconnects. Editing preserves omitted attachments and Skills, or replaces them with validated supplied arrays (including empty arrays for removal). Saving releases the item at its reserved position unless a later item was dispatched during editing, in which case the edited item moves to the queue tail. Cancelling restores the original item at its reserved position. The browser hides the held row while editing in its composer. Missing/consumed items return queue_item_missing; conflicts return queue_conflict. Only POST is supported. Edit bodies allow the same unlimited text budget as prompts.

POST /api/sessions/:id/resume returns 202 for an idle resumable task with no pending save; core events publish activity and completion. Abort retains unconsumed inputs and pauses draining. Model/flush/title commands retain their idle locks.

Snapshots carry ordered state.queue, state.canResume and bounded acceptedRequestIds. Core queue_changed events publish authoritative state while preserving active draft indexes and running tool status. A queued request uses its original requestId as queue ID. Deduplication covers the original payload even after editing/deletion; reusing its ID does not recreate it. This memory-only protection is lost on restart or eviction.

See [core queue lifecycle](../../../../coding-agent/src/docs/message-queue.md), [queue route](../routes/session-queue.ts) and [controller regression tests](../session-controller.test.ts).

## Independent sessions

POST /api/sessions with an explicit null workspaceId creates an independent draft. GET /api/sessions?scope=global lists its nonarchived history; append archived=true for archived entries. Missing workspaceId without scope=global is invalid. Snapshot, summary and sessions.changed events carry workspaceId: null. Pin and read commands also accept explicit null. No endpoint changes the ownership of a conversation.

History is stored in <dataRoot>/sessions/global/<sessionId>/ using the same metadata, messages and round index as project sessions. SessionManager.list(undefined, collectionDirectory) reads the collection across working directories; existing cwd-filtered listing remains unchanged. Registry startup discovers independent history without requiring registered projects or a database.

Each independent draft has a private working directory under a sibling of dataRoot named <dataRoot-name>-workspaces, with a generated UUID directory. The saved cwd is reused on restore. This location keeps generated files outside protected Loop storage. Normal permission presets, context loading, resource integrations and approvals apply to that directory. Traces use <dataRoot>/traces/global/<sessionId>. Archive preserves working files, and deleting history does not remove generated files. Empty handles can leave working directories; automatic cleanup is not implemented.

Independent archive and delete operations use /api/workspaces/global/archive and /api/workspaces/global/sessions/:id with the existing body and method contracts. The global scope is internal, is not registered as a project and cannot be renamed or removed as a project. Settings archive lists include independent chats. Session file and image responses resolve references against the session working directory. Remote users retain the existing local-only archive/delete restrictions.

pages.title: Skill endpoints
pages.markdown:
# Skill endpoints

Skill management shares the local request and JSON validation described in [HTTP boundaries](http.md). The backend owns one shared public `SkillManager`, injects it into sessions and closes it during shutdown. Scanning is asynchronous and does not block server startup.

## Routes

All paths start with `/api/settings/skills`. Optional `?workspaceId=<id>` selects a registered project and its personal/project catalog. Without it, only personal skills are listed.

| Method and suffix | Input / result |
| --- | --- |
| GET `/` | Current `SkillCatalog`, including scanning/error state |
| POST `/refresh` | Await scan and return catalog |
| POST `/preview` | `SkillPreviewInput`; return `SkillJob` with status 202 |
| GET `/jobs/<id>` | Current job stages/candidates/error |
| DELETE `/jobs/<id>` | Cancel; status 204 |
| POST `/install` | `{ jobId, keys, scope, updateId? }`; install and return catalog |
| GET `/<skillId>` | Summary and current instruction body |
| PATCH `/<skillId>/enabled` | `{ enabled: boolean }`; return catalog |
| POST `/<skillId>/update` | Preview a managed GitHub update; status 202 |
| DELETE `/<skillId>` | Uninstall an owned managed folder; return catalog |

Project installs require `workspaceId`. Source kinds are `github`, `local` and `created`. Jobs expose real downloading, checking or installing stages rather than a percentage. Error inputs and `SkillError` failures return status 400; ordinary filesystem failures follow the shared HTTP error contract. Failed installations leave the prior installation intact.

## Chat

POST `/api/sessions/<id>/prompt` accepts optional `skills: string[]`, with at most eight 24-character hexadecimal source identities. Selection participates in request deduplication. New selections are validated before accepting the run; unavailable skills return a 400 error so the browser retains the draft. Replays use the previously accepted request without rereading skill files. Core rechecks availability when the run starts. Loaded skill events project into session state and saved runtime-context snapshots.

The management routes neither execute scripts nor alter tool approval policy. See [core skills](../../../../coding-agent/src/docs/skills.md) for discovery, storage, limits and lifecycle.

## Source and tests

# Local Voice Transport

Loop's Web voice layer connects authenticated browser audio to the public coding-agent voice runtime. Agent sessions continue to receive ordinary text prompts and retain their existing tools, permissions, approvals and queue scheduling.

## Setup

Call creation accepts an optional boolean `synthesis`. It defaults to true for conversation mode and false for dictation and test mode. Test speech explicitly enables it; microphone tests leave it disabled. Recognition-only calls skip TTS resource verification and initialization.

Install compatible resources from **Settings → Voice** on the computer running Loop. Installation is explicit and local-only. The settings response reports supported platform, individual engine/ASR/VAD/TTS components, download progress, installed bytes, versions and errors. Resource downloads must exist in the reviewed Loop release catalog before installation is available; no resource is downloaded at startup.

The managed files live under the coding-agent data directory's `voice/` folder. Changing `LOOP_DATA_DIR` changes that data root. Microphone audio, temporary recognition state and generated speech remain in memory. Submitted final text uses the existing session storage.

## HTTP Contracts

| Endpoint | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/voice/status` | Installation/resource status; remote devices cannot see the absolute resource directory. |
| `POST /api/voice/install` | Local-only `{action, profile}`, with install/update/cancel/uninstall and input/conversation profiles. Installation runs asynchronously; poll status. |
| `POST /api/voice/calls` | `{clientId, mode, sessionId?}` creates one call and returns `{callId, ticket, expiresAt}`. Mode is dictation, conversation or settings test. |
| `POST /api/voice/calls/:id/connect` | The original owner/client requests a fresh single-use connection ticket. |
| `POST /api/voice/calls/:id/close` | The original owner/client ends audio processing, independently of the Agent task. |

Local commands require the exact request Origin; remote commands retain paired-device cookies and CSRF protection. Call tickets expire after thirty seconds, are delivered only in a protected response and are never placed in a URL. A server process permits one active call.

## WebSocket Protocol

Connect to `/api/voice/calls/:id/socket` on the same origin, then send an authenticate JSON frame containing the ticket. The handshake checks local Host/Origin or paired remote-device authorization. Production, remote ingress and the authenticated development gateway all support the same protocol.

- Browser binary frames contain mono 16 kHz PCM16LE, at most 32 KiB per message. Server input buffering is limited to about two seconds; overflow terminates the audio connection rather than dropping and splicing samples.
- JSON controls configure microphone/reading state, finish the current utterance, interrupt a playback generation, request short speech, or close the call. Control and audio processing remain separately cancellable.
- The server emits ready, transcript, status and error JSON frames. Each utterance carries a stable ID; partials are replaced until one final.
- Each audio JSON frame describes a playback generation, sample rate and WAV format; the next binary frame contains that WAV chunk. Generated audio is not served through session file downloads or written to disk.
- The browser stops playback immediately on local speech detection. Generation checks discard late synthesis, download and decode results.

Final text is submitted through the existing session prompt endpoint. Its optional boolean `steering` is part of the deduplication signature and reaches core enqueue atomically. Ordinary speech while busy adds follow-ups; steering takes effect at the next model boundary after the current response and complete tool batch. Stopped sessions remain paused until explicit Resume.

## Recovery and Authorization

An ordinary transport disconnect cancels speech, discards the incomplete utterance and starts a thirty-second call lease. Reconnection needs a fresh ticket and does not replay microphone audio or old TTS. Device expiry, durable revocation, explicit hangup and server shutdown immediately dispose of the call. Device invalidation reaches a development worker over private IPC even while the call is disconnected.

Authorization is checked before and after asynchronous session/resource startup. Expiry, revocation and cancellation of the opening HTTP request stop an opening native runtime before a ticket can be published. Cancelling that request after its response does not end an established call. The development supervisor includes prior invalidations in the worker's initial handshake and waits for a per-request revocation acknowledgement after native cleanup. Worker exit also settles that wait; an unresponsive worker is terminated. WebSocket heartbeat pings cross the development proxy and require the browser's pong rather than an automatic proxy response.

The browser pauses automatic submission if either voice transport or the main session stream is unavailable. It uses the existing request identity and stream checks for uncertain text delivery. A backend restart expires voice calls and in-memory queues; completed session history remains authoritative.

Phone use requires a secure context, microphone permission and a foreground page. Remote audio is inferred on the computer but passes through the configured tunnel relay; local inference does not imply relay-blind encryption. See [remote devices](remote-devices.md) and [PWA limits](../../frontend/docs/pwa.md).
